[112] CYCLE OF PREPARATORY DEBATES FOR THE PREPARATION OF THE WHITE PAPER

[113] A little less than five years ago I had the pleasure of presenting to you the first update of the White Paper on Defence, eleven years after its first edition

[114] Imbued with the spirit of the Bicentennial of the May Revolution, this text aimed to generate an in-depth debate about national defense policy and its inextricable link to the prevailing economic and social model

[115] I still remember when in July 2008, just a few months after taking office as President of the Nation, we launched the Master's Degree in National Defense together with the University of Tres de Febrero

[116] That day I emphasized that there is no successful National Defense System in a country guided by a deficient economic and social model

[117] On the contrary: virtuous economic and social models are what create the conditions for the emergence of a National Defense Policy that transcends time

[118] This is what we have done since May

[119] We have certainly come a long way in defense policy, seeking, at the same time, to fulfill the primary mission outlined in the Defense Law and inviting the Armed Forces to play a leading role in the nation's development

[120] Over these twelve years, we have tried to permanently instill in all our men and women involved in the Defense, whether they wear uniform or civilian clothes, the need to think of one country, to think of one Homeland, a word that was long forgotten

[121] We have done so with a conviction: as long as there was unity between the Armed Forces and the people, history could be written for Argentina in letters of gold

[122] This new update to the White Paper on Defense that we are presenting attempts to account for these processes over the last five years

[123] It is, in a sense, an assessment and accountability process, promoting transparency in information about an area that often appears obscure to the public

[124] But this White Paper is also an invitation to plan and think about the future, so that everything achieved in recent years can become a solid platform for continuing to advance in the face of new challenges

[125] It is no coincidence, then, that this White Paper proposes a comprehensive and integrative overview of everything accomplished in this area, beginning with a clear description of the international arena in which our National Defense Policy operates

[126] In this regard, we address the international dimension of defense, an area in which we have gained new prominence through cooperation and dialogue, actively participating in United Nations peacekeeping operations, and helping to streamline the work of the Defense Council of the Union of South American Nations

[127] The document also seeks to account for the structural changes we have promoted in terms of regulations to provide national defense with a solid foundation for the future

[128] Gender and human rights policy in the field of defense is also addressed, as well as the changes made in the training and development of military and civilian personnel

[129] This White Paper delves into the national defense planning cycle and the organization and deployment of our Armed Forces, with their human and material resources, in the service of various military operations, which are detailed and analyzed

[130] A special chapter deserves the military coordination of emergency assistance, where the Armed Forces, through the Ministry of Defense, have regained prominence by standing shoulder to shoulder with Argentines who, for various reasons, need everyone's supportive embrace

[131] In many places, I saw military men and women actively working with social organizations and volunteers in operations to combat floods, landslides, fires, and landslides

[132] I assure you that I was filled with pride to see this commitment and this vocation for coordinated action

[133] Something similar happens with the work done around science, technology and production for Defense

[134] We have begun a historic process of recovering capabilities that we had lost due to policies that ended up privatizing or directly eliminating the role of the State in key areas

[135] The new impetus we gave to Military Manufacturing, FAdeA, and the Argentine Naval Industrial Complex (CINAR) attempted to correct that strategic error

[136] This White Paper describes what has been done in this regard, aware that the final results will be visible over time, when many of the projects we have developed and promoted in recent years bear fruit

[137] In short, I am extremely proud to present as President of the Nation and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces—this latest update to the White Paper on Defense, the second in less than eight years of my administration

[138] I am sure that reading and analyzing it will lead to new ideas that will help us think about the future in terms of sovereignty

[139] I said it at the last Fellowship Dinner: sovereignty is going to be the word that defines the future of this 21st century

[140] That's why we must engrave this word in our hearts

[141] We are not talking about sovereignty linked to the protection of our territorial integrity

[142] Or the one that arises when proudly singing the anthem or raising the flag

[143] Sovereignty must exist in each and every area: in production, in research, in science and technology, in education, and in health policies

[144] Therefore, welcome this White Paper on Defense as another contribution to the construction of a sovereign Argentina. The governments of Néstor Kirchner and Cristina Fernández consolidated the paradigm of civilian leadership of our armed forces within the framework of one of the greatest historical transformations recorded in this sector

[145] This indispensable reform made it possible to overcome decades of delegationism by political authorities who, abdicating their responsibilities, encouraged autonomous and disjointed behavior within the armed forces, thus making it impossible for the nation's military to function properly and jointly

[146] In this vein, over nearly twelve years, a myriad of laws, decrees, and resolutions, as well as the daily exercise of leadership, determined, among other things, the missions, functions, and jurisdictional areas of the armed forces; the strategic posture of our defense policy; a capabilities-based planning system that would allow us to overcome the outdated model of planning based on conflict assumptions; and the restoration of the defense science, technology, and production system

[147] All of this is within the framework of a human rights policy that would free the Republic's leading institutions committed to the defense and respect of national sovereignty, the Constitution of the Republic, and the rule of law from destructive obstacles

[148] Joint military action is an essential condition for the proper functioning of our armed forces

[149] In this regard, the "Rattenbach Report"—declassified by our President and Commander-in-Chief in 2012—exposed the problems that occurred on the battlefield as a result of disjointed actions

[150] Promoting joint action was essential in all areas of the armed forces' professional life, and it was in this context that the role of the Joint Chiefs of Staff—and its Operational Command—was consolidated, giving it precedence over the general staffs of each of the forces and promoting integrated, coordinated, and joint action in the areas of training, planning, intelligence, and resource management

[151] The integration, cooperation, and coordination of the defense research, development, and production subsystem with the National Science, Technology, and Innovation System has been one of the pillars of the three administrations that have succeeded each other since

[152] President Néstor Kirchner then appreciated the unique contribution that the defense sector could make to a national project based on work, social inclusion, industrialization, and the generation of added value

[153] Within this framework, capacities were recovered that had been abandoned during the 1990s, when neoliberal governments closed, privatized, and dismantled leading organizations that had been pioneers in the history of various industrial sectors in the country

[154] Gradually – and not without difficulty – the Córdoba Aircraft Factory, the TANDANOR Company and the Domecq García Shipyards (today called “Almirante Storni”) were recovered

[155] Also within this framework, a significant fiscal effort has been made to develop strategic technological capabilities: primary and secondary radars, access to space, unmanned aerial vehicles, among other technological developments

[156] The return of the Directorate of Military Manufacturing (DGFM) to the Defense sector represents another milestone in the aforementioned effort, highlighting the opening in 2014 of a new explosives manufacturing plant in San José de Jáchal, San Juan province

[157] This is the first inauguration at the Military Manufacturing complex in more than six decades. Its main objective is the production of Sipolex, a powdered explosive, a blasting agent created, developed, and patented by FM

[158] This same Directorate began producing goods for civilian use, such as railway hopper grain cars, and, together with the company INVAP we have manufactured and implemented long-range 3D primary radars, the Argentine Primary Radar (RPA) and the Argentine Secondary Monopulse Radar (RSMA), with the aim of strengthening air traffic control

[159] Our restored Argentine Aircraft Factory is now exporting again after twenty years and has undertaken complementary projects with other countries in the region, such as the UNASUR I basic training aircraft. At the CINAR complex, we carried out mid-life repairs on the San Juan submarine; we restored and modernized the icebreaker "Almirante Irízar," and we regained the capacity to keep our naval force operational

[160] This enormous challenge required a bureaucratic structure that could politically manage these responsibilities

[161] This effort resulted in the creation of the Secretariat of Science, Technology and Defense Production in

[162] Over the decades, our Armed Forces have acquired vast capacity and experience in providing assistance and support to the community in emergency and disaster situations, circumstances in which they consistently demonstrate their aptitude, capacity, and commitment to acting in aid of Argentine citizens and those of other friendly nations

[163] Work that has been recognized in our country and abroad

[164] However, the complexity with which these unfortunate events have evolved—whether due to natural or man-made causes—led to the need to strengthen the political leadership of these responsibilities and, consequently, the creation, in 2013, of the Military Coordination Secretariat for Emergency Assistance

[165] In light of the diagnosis of historical dysfunctions noted in the first paragraph, we could not leave the indispensable contribution that the defense sector provides to the national civil protection effort to political delegation and a lack of cohesion

[166] Considering that National Defense plays an important role in the country's foreign policy, based on our autonomous, defensive, and cooperative strategic approach, we have promoted multilateral dialogue and integration in defense matters with the countries of our region

[167] We are convinced that South America must consolidate all its integration mechanisms, and we understand that UNASUR is a geopolitical and economic entity of growing importance in the current international context

[168] For this reason, the Argentine Republic has played an active role in the development and strengthening of the South American Defense Council (CDS), the CDS Center for Strategic Studies, and the South American Defense School (ESUDE), as cooperative spaces for laying the foundations for a subregional defense system

[169] It is the CDS, the most active Council of UNASUR, which is why we are convinced it will be a catalyst for other South American integration bodies that may be lagging behind

[170] We are also promoting collective discussion on the new challenges posed by the preservation of our natural resources and cyber defense, a particular and cross-cutting operational area, notable among which are the recent creation of the Joint Cyber Defense Command in 2014 and the General Directorate of Cyber Defense in

[171] From this framework of regional belonging and projection, we continue to assert the legitimate and peaceful claim of sovereignty over the Malvinas Islands, South Georgia, the South Sandwich Islands, and other maritime and island areas, and from where we participate in and lead important peacekeeping missions within the framework of the United Nations System

[172] In this regard, the Defense System has continued to support the national Antarctic policy, with our country having the longest uninterrupted presence on the white continent and the one with the most bases

[173] There, the logistical support of the armed forces makes it possible for hundreds of scientists and researchers to carry out their work, even in extreme conditions

[174] With the understanding that the most valuable asset the armed forces possess is our personnel, a profound transformation has taken place in the training system over the years

[175] In 2006, the Armed Forces Educational Center (CEFA) was launched. This organization brings together the Joint War College and the war colleges of the Army, Navy, and Air Force, thus promoting the educational integration of the military instrument and, subsequently, joint military action

[176] The creation of the National Defense University in 2014 will allow us to leverage all our educational achievements and open up new horizons

[177] In the educational field, recent initiatives have made it possible for all high school students to have a netbook thanks to the "Conectar Igualdad" program and for thousands of volunteer soldiers to complete their studies through the "Fines" plan

[178] We have deepened gender and human rights policy in all aspects of defense

[179] The gender approach involved removing legal and formally institutionalized obstacles that hindered equal professional development

[180] We have raised awareness and disseminated the gender perspective within the armed forces; incorporated the gender perspective into peacekeeping operations; promoted women's access to decision-making spaces; addressed domestic violence; monitored cases of gender-related human rights violations; and designed methodological and statistical tools to more fully assess situations of inequality within the institution

[181] Today, fifteen percent of the armed forces personnel are women, and they increasingly occupy command positions

[182] In terms of human rights, we emphasize the immense legal and historical value of the discovery and declassification of documentation relating to the repressive actions of the last dictatorship

[183] Much of this wealth has been uncovered by the actions of the armed forces themselves, as evidenced by the discovery of hundreds of secret records from the Military Junta in

[184] Material found in the Argentine Air Force's “Cóndor” building and made available to the political and judicial authorities by the Chief of Staff of said force

[185] This and other events demonstrate the commitment our armed forces have to the present and future of the Republic and their rejection of the bloody past

[186] In light of the new challenges the Ministry of Defense has faced since 2013, and to continue fostering trust with the international community and transparency for citizens and taxpayers, we decided to sponsor a new process to update the White Paper on Defense

[187] Following the publication of the White Papers of 1999 and 2010, this is the third edition of this significant document, considered and promoted in various international forums, of which our country is a member, as a measure of mutual trust

[188] Likewise, the two administrations of Dr. Cristina Fernández de Kirchner are the first to publish this important and strategic document in two successive presidencies

[189] Below we share the results achieved, hoping they will contribute to fostering a serious and informed debate on defense issues and, above all, contribute to building a more inclusive, sovereign, supportive, free, and democratic nation

[190] The global context Since the beginning of the 21st century, the international system has been characterized by the redistribution of global power in a framework of growing interdependence

[191] Current trends in the world order indicate the coexistence of the strategic-military unipolarity of the United States of America, intended as exclusive, with a progressive multipolarization in the political-economic dimension, where traditional powers coexist with emerging powers from the South

[192] There is also a progressive shift in the "Euro-Atlantic" center of power—predominant for more than half a millennium—toward the "Asia-Pacific" axis and, as a consequence of demographic, economic, and geopolitical transformations, a redistribution of power from the "North" to the "South

[193] The aspirations of emerging powers are giving the international system a new dynamic, reflected in the formation of spaces for integration, dialogue, and cooperation, such as the BRICS group (Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa

[194] The importance that new forums are acquiring in the processes of global institutionalization offers countries in the South the opportunity to jointly increase their capacity for influence in the international arena and to achieve greater margins of autonomy

[195] In this context, debates on the legitimacy and representativeness of international institutions have been encouraged by a growing number of countries

[196] This trend expresses demands regarding the need to redefine the very foundations of international cooperation, the design of international regimes, and the formation of multilateral forums for global governance, such as the G-20, in which the interests of the nations of the South are articulated in the management of global issues

[197] However, at least two issues must be taken into account

[198] On the one hand, the establishment of an interdependent order with multipolar characteristics does not necessarily imply a world of greater multilateral rules, and on the other, the role and influence of non-state actors in the international system, such as transnational corporations and financial groups, and non-governmental organizations, has continued to expand

[199] Its ability to project forces and influence on a global scale, thanks to the deployment of hundreds of bases selectively located in various geographical enclaves of strategic interest, is the most striking example of this

[200] However, in recent decades we have seen a slow decline in this power – along with that of the European system – and the emergence of new state actors with the capacity to influence the international agenda

[201] The aspirations of these emerging powers, including Brazil, China, India, and Russia, give a new dynamic to the contemporary international system, thus demonstrating a trend toward redistribution of global power

[202] CHAPTER I APPRECIATION OF THE INTERNATIONAL SCENARIO Likewise, to understand the current world order it is necessary to consider that for at least four decades the consolidation and rising influence of financial capitalism on a global scale has been appreciated

[203] The correlate of this accumulation regime is the growth of a regressive income distribution at the global level

[204] Despite notable progress in the fight against poverty, Latin American countries remain among the most unequal in the world

[205] This inequality constitutes a structural feature of the prevailing international order, as does the weakness of multilateral mechanisms for regulating the globalized financial system

[206] Argentina considers it a priority to promote equitable and inclusive growth among nations, as well as to create a legal framework aimed at increasing the efficiency, stability, and predictability of the international financial system

[207] In parallel with the reorganization of the international system, we can see the impact on the sphere of national defense of issues that have deepened since the end of the last century, such as those related to the spread of technological power, cyber defense, and tensions arising from the scarcity of natural resources worldwide

[208] In relation to scientific and technical capabilities, we are witnessing the multiplication of technological power centers, both for civilian and military use

[209] Given the projected trends, countries such as China and India are clear examples of emerging global centers of innovation and development. Like the United States, Russia, and Israel, they will seek to deepen and develop the military application of innovative technologies associated with robotics—especially the development of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs, or drones)—cybernetics, space surveillance, remote sensing, and precision weapons, among other technologies

[210] In this regard, it is important to mention that we are facing a process of emergence, consolidation, and acceleration of disruptive technologies that could lead to the establishment of a new paradigm with profound transformations in the ways of waging war, thinking about strategy, operational art, and military tactics

[211] Even the human role as a central element of combat is beginning to be diluted by the arrival in the theater of operations of drones, robots, and other technological platforms with great destructive power and force projection

[212] IX Meeting of the Executive Body of the South American Defense Council of UNASUR, Paramaribo, Suriname

[215] Americas Asia and Oceania Europe Africa Middle East Another aspect associated with the new scientific-technical paradigm and information technologies is the importance that cyberspace is acquiring for the development of military operations

[216] This artificial, physically undefined area does not constitute a specific operational environment, but rather a different one, with its own resources and rules, which spans land, sea, and airspace

[217] While cyberwarfare originates and develops within the virtual realm of communications networks and computer systems, it can trigger specific kinetic effects in the real world, potentially affecting control of critical infrastructure, energy and drinking water supplies, air and ground traffic, and, among other aspects, the security of strategic information

[218] Therefore, the new challenge posed by cyberspace demands rapid adaptation of defense systems and the development of specific capabilities in this unique operational environment

[224] The growing global demand for vital non-renewable or scarce natural resources, such as hydrocarbons, strategic minerals, food, and fresh water, poses a new challenge to be considered primarily in geopolitical terms, as this demand can generate competition over the appropriation of such resources, their trade routes, or the territories where they are found in significant quantities and are easily accessible

[225] Consequently, there is a clear need to preserve national sovereignty in geographic areas with reserves of vital and strategic natural resources and to establish cooperation mechanisms or instruments in the case of cross-border resources or those shared by several States, based on their consideration as regional strategic assets for the development of interstate plans for their preservation or sustainable use

[226] Such strategies may seem ambitious in many parts of the world that are plagued by security dilemmas, neighborhood mistrust, or unresolved territorial disputes, but, on the contrary, they appear feasible to be fostered in the medium term in regions such as South America, which is considered a true "zone of peace

[227] Along with the new problems facing the international system, we are deeply concerned about the persistence of anachronisms and conflicts between actors in the international system that deserve close attention

[228] For example, with regard to the decolonization process promoted by the United Nations, based on General Assembly Resolution 1514 (XV), there are still seventeen colonial enclaves in the world, ten of which remain under the political and administrative control of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, including the Falkland Islands, South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands and the surrounding maritime areas which, being an integral part of Argentine territory, are illegally occupied by the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

[229] It should be noted that the deployment of military resources by the United Kingdom and other extraregional nations constitutes a serious challenge to the maintenance of the South American peace zone, as well as to the protection of its strategic resources

[230] State and interstate rivalries and conflicts continue to persist, destabilizing regions and potentially even leading to foreign intervention

[231] It also highlights the persistence of unilateral conduct and the preemptive use of military instruments by some countries, to the detriment of current international law

[232] The UN General Assembly approved Resolution 68/304, "Towards a multilateral legal framework for sovereign debt restructuring processes," proposed by the G77 + China at the request of Argentina

[233] Pursuant to this resolution, the General Assembly adopted Resolution 69/247 on modalities for implementing Resolution

[234] This Resolution established an Ad Hoc Committee to develop, through intergovernmental negotiations and as a priority at its sixty-ninth session, a multilateral legal framework for sovereign debt restructuring processes

[235] The Argentine Republic persists in its call for the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland to resume negotiations in accordance with the resolutions of the United Nations General Assembly

[236] Thus, the current global scenario is characterized by the coexistence of a diversity of regions in which neither actors nor behaviors respond to similar logics

[237] In some, practices such as balance of power and deterrence predominate, while in others—even though territorial disputes from the past persist—cooperation and mutual trust have gained ground, with South America being a clear example of this

[238] In the face of a complex international landscape, the Argentine Republic promotes respect and peace among nations and the peaceful resolution of conflicts through institutional mechanisms of international cooperation and governance. It maintains a defense policy rooted in its conception and strategic defensive positioning

[239] In the areas of International Defense and Security, the South American region presents characteristics that distinguish it from any other part of the world

[240] Integration, an aspiration that has existed since the dawn of Latin American countries' independence, is a process under consolidation that can hardly be relegated in the future, and the few territorial disputes between neighboring countries that still persist are no longer amenable to military resolution

[241] South America has established itself as a true zone of peace and has forged institutional mechanisms to support this historic objective

[242] Within the framework of the new strategic scenario of the 21st century, the maturation of the integration processes initiated in the 1980s, such as the Andean Community of Nations (CAN) – Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru – and the Southern Common Market (MERCOSUR) – Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Venezuela – together with the political will of leaders and the consensus of the people, allowed integration to expand to levels of political agreement unprecedented in the region

[243] As a result, the Union of South American Nations (UNASUR) was established in 2008 with the aim of building a South American identity and citizenship and developing an integrated regional space in the political, economic, social, and cultural dimensions, as well as in environmental, energy, and infrastructure matters

[244] The UN General Assembly declared, through Resolution 1514 (XV), entitled "Declaration on the Granting of Independence to Colonial Countries and Peoples", the need to put an end to colonialism, since the subjection of peoples to foreign subjugation, domination and exploitation constitutes a violation of human rights and jeopardizes the cause of peace, world cooperation and the development of the peoples set forth in the Charter of the United Nations

[245] For its part, the UN General Assembly in its Resolution No. 2065 (XX), with the desire to put an end to colonialism everywhere and in all its forms, took note of the existence of a sovereignty dispute over the Malvinas Islands between the Argentine Republic and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and invited their Governments to continue negotiations without delay in order to find a peaceful solution to the dispute

[246] The regional scenario is characterized by all countries' respect for democracy as an indispensable element for the consolidation of international peace and security, the stability and development of peoples, and the guarantee of the protection and promotion of human rights

[268] The integration process gave rise to the creation of the South American Defense Council (CDS) in Salvador de Bahía, Brazil, on December 16, 2008. Member states agreed to advance the development of a South American strategic identity in defense and the joint identification of challenges, risk factors and threats, as well as opportunities and relevant regional scenarios in this area

[269] Since its creation, the CDS has been one of UNASUR's most active councils

[270] In 2010, the Center for Strategic Defense Studies (CEED) was established in Buenos Aires as a permanent advisory body to the CDS, and in 2014, the South American Defense School (ESUDE) was established with the purpose of training civilian and military personnel based on a uniquely South American doctrine

[271] This tendency to consolidate a regional space characterized by cooperative defense actions constitutes a process that surpasses the methods of engagement in this area and military affairs that prevailed during the 20th century in the inter-American arena, although instruments and organizations from an obsolete international context, typical of the Cold War, still survive

[272] For this reason, the Argentine Republic is promoting this debate with the aim of guiding the reform and adaptation of inter-American defense agencies based on current regional strategic conditions and the principles of the rule of law that govern the countries of the region

[273] On this South American path toward unity, the principles and values of each member state converge, and strategic issues of urgent consideration are addressed, such as the protection of natural resources and the defense of South American cyberspace

[274] Shared natural resource reserves and strategic assets require preservation for future generations, which can only be effectively achieved through a common strategy and policy among South American countries

[275] Regarding cyber defense, it is emphasized that it is not only a matter of ensuring the security of information and communication systems and networks against potential espionage, but also of achieving greater autonomy in this matter and advancing the establishment of concerted actions to protect the cyberspace of each member country against external interference that could be perpetrated against the vital and strategic interests of those countries and their populations

[276] These priority issues, which characterize the current regional scenario, are reflected in the short-, medium-, and long-term efforts of the UNASUR member countries and provide a framework for the region's commitment to preserving the regional status of a zone free of nuclear, chemical, and biological weapons

[277] Through multiple declarations and resolutions by CELAC, UNASUR, and MERCOSUR, in compliance with the Treaty for the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons in Latin America and the Caribbean (Treaty of Tlatelolco) and other relevant conventions, the region is guaranteed to remain a nuclear-weapon-free zone

[322] The South American region maintains its commitment to the UN's collective security programs deployed worldwide, confirmed by the fact that the region provides a significant contribution of personnel to military and civilian peacekeeping operations

[323] Examples of this have been the participation in the United Nations Stabilization Mission in Haiti (MINUSTAH) and the joint initiatives undertaken in the region to support the collective system, such as the establishment of the joint and combined binational peacekeeping force "Cruz del Sur" between Chile and Argentina, and the "Libertador Don José de San Martín" Engineering Company, a Peruvian-Argentine engineering company for peacekeeping operations

[324] Likewise, the Latin American Association of Peacekeeping Operations Training Centers (ALCOPAZ), an Argentine initiative aimed at promoting interoperability among the region's armed forces, standardizing a doctrine for peacekeeping operations, and sharing lessons learned, is also important

[325] Another relevant aspect for the analysis of the regional scenario is the respect and support shown by all countries in the region for strengthening democracy as an indispensable element for consolidating international peace and security, the stability and development of peoples, and ensuring the protection and promotion of human rights

[326] The aforementioned conditions distinguish the South American region as one of the most stable and predictable globally. Furthermore, it stands out from other regions in the world in that it has comparatively the lowest levels of defense spending

[327] In the countries of the region, the majority of the military budget is allocated to items corresponding to salaries, personnel training, and general operations, although some states have launched initiatives for the modernization and acquisition of weapons systems, primarily related to the need to technologically update obsolete equipment and improve surveillance and control of their sovereign spaces

[328] While at another historical moment, the acquisition of defense material in one country would have aroused distrust among neighboring states—according to the matrix of military competition that dominated relations between countries from the mid-19th century and for virtually the entire 20th century—the current regional defense scenario is characterized by the progressive loss of relevance of threat perceptions and strategic and military competition

[329] All of this within a framework of full respect for international law and the principles of peaceful dispute resolution, while defense policies are guided by the principle of self-defense and strategic concepts and attitudes of a defensive and cooperative nature

[330] CHAPTER II CONCEPT AND STRATEGIC ATTITUDE OF DEFENSE The Argentine Republic is conceived as a country with a peaceful vocation that promotes respect and the values of the rule of law, democracy and human rights

[331] This is why its defensive strategic conception emphasizes the importance of cooperation as a means of building trust between states, with the aim of contributing to the maintenance of international peace

[332] The defense policy of the Argentine Republic and the organization and design of its military instrument are based on the principles and guidelines derived from its system of essential values, its internal order and the postulates of its foreign policy

[333] These foundations are built on respect for and promotion of democracy, the rule of law, human rights, and adherence to international law and the multilateral system as central instruments for regulating interstate relations and facilitating the peaceful resolution of disputes

[334] The conception, positioning, and strategic attitude that shape the nation's defense policy are framed within the concept of self-defense established in Article 51 of the UN Charter

[335] Consequently, a defense model is designed, structured, and organized to reject and oppose offensive policies, attitudes, and capabilities, as well as the projection of power toward third states

[336] The Argentine defense model is entirely predictable in terms of its strategic conception and strictly defensive in terms of the design and disposition of its military capabilities. It assumes national defense according to the classic scheme and in accordance with the current regulatory framework

[337] The primary mission of the National Defense System is to ward off and repel, through the use of the military instrument of National Defense, external state military aggressions in order to permanently guarantee and safeguard the sovereignty, independence, and self-determination of the nation, its territorial integrity, the protection of its strategic resources, and the life and liberty of its inhabitants

[338] By virtue of its strategic defensive positioning, the Argentine Republic conceives its Defense in a dual autonomous and cooperative dimension

[339] On the one hand, defense planning is geared toward developing military capabilities that guarantee autonomous defense against any external military state aggression

[340] Through the capabilities-based planning model, the National Defense System consolidates its ability to independently execute the full range of operations required by all forms of aggression manifested in conventional conflicts of external origin generated by state actors

[341] On the other hand, the strategic orientation of defense policy embraces cooperation among states as a fundamental principle, as it links to and contributes to the nation's foreign policy and the fulfillment of subregional, regional, and global multilateral commitments

[342] Consequently, this policy aims to strengthen the national contribution to the collective security system by achieving and maintaining the minimum standards required for both multilateral military interaction and advancing the development of adequate levels of subregional interoperability

[343] The Argentine Republic aspires to the eventual construction of a regional system that transcends the levels of mutual trust already achieved

[344] To this end, it is proposed to strengthen ties with the countries of the region in terms of effective military cooperation and complementarity for purposes of mutual interest, such as coparticipation in the control of common border areas and the complementation of capabilities in peacekeeping operations or other support operations, such as logistical assistance in Antarctic research activities

[345] Consequently, the goal is to ensure conditions that contribute to guaranteeing the maintenance of the South American peace zone and regional political and strategic predictability

[346] This political-strategic framework is based on two fundamental principles of the National Defense System: the civil and political governance of Defense and the jurisdictional, organic, and functional differentiation between National Defense and Internal Security

[347] Civilian governance of defense affairs consists of the exercise of institutional leadership, administration, planning, and oversight of national defense policy matters by legitimately constituted political authorities, both in their contribution to foreign policy and in their strategic dimension and in their resulting military policy

[348] The conceptual, organic, and functional distinction between national defense and internal security is based on the consideration that these are distinct state functions, which must be resolved in distinct areas by applying specific instruments to address their respective responsibilities

[349] The Argentine Republic has specialized agencies to address these issues in a differentiated manner

[350] The mission of the National Defense System, as has already been stated, is to ward off and repel military aggression from other States through its armed forces

[351] The Internal Security System, meanwhile, has as its primary purpose the prevention and prosecution, through the use of police and security forces, of criminal acts covered by the Penal Code and other laws

[352] This differentiation of functions and actions implies the design, updating, and application of training, equipment, and employment doctrines different from those of National Defense

[353] The distinction made by the Argentine State between these responsibilities does not ignore the possibility of complementarity between the two systems

[354] The National Defense System collaborates daily with the Internal Security System in a variety of areas and situations provided for in National Law 24,059. The possible participation of combat elements of the armed forces is restricted to cases of extreme gravity and after a declaration of a "state of siege

[355] In another order, the Argentine Republic conceives its defense policy as a contributing factor to its national development strategy

[356] The National Defense System contributes steadily to scientific research, technological innovation, and productive growth in the national defense industry as fundamental pillars for safeguarding national sovereignty and its strategic resources

[357] In Argentina, we are convinced that the national defense effort must contribute, through its sectoral specificity, to the development of the National Science, Technology, and Innovation System (National Law 25.467), either on its own or in conjunction with other research and development organizations

[358] Developments promoted by the defense sector have a positive impact on other productive and technological subsystems

[359] The strategic and multiplying value of research and development in aerospace technologies such as satellite injectors and unmanned aircraft, nuclear propulsion for naval submarine and surface units, and cyber resources for protecting critical infrastructure and information from potential attacks of this nature is once again reiterated

[360] Finally, it is worth noting that the Argentine Republic views its defense policy as integrated into its national policy on Memory, Truth, and Justice

[361] The South American region maintains its commitment to the United Nations collective security schemes deployed globally, confirmed by the fact that the region provides a significant contribution of personnel to military and civilian peacekeeping operations

[362] The responses provided by the country at the domestic level in the fight against impunity and the demands for truth, justice, and reparations for the victims of serious human rights violations during the last military dictatorship constitute fundamental pillars in the comprehensive human rights policy of the Argentine State

[363] The progress made since the restoration of democracy in 1983, and the decisive push given since 2003 to combat impunity and to fight for the vindication and protection of human rights, have placed the Argentine Republic in a position of global leadership in the construction of a more just international order, positively impacting the prospects for international peace and security to which the National Defense System is committed

[364] Self-defense guides national defense policy at all levels, defining the strategic dimension, force design, and the deployment of non-offensive capabilities toward third states

[365] Argentina views its defense policy as integrated into its national development strategy and national policy on Memory, Truth and Justice

[366] The Defense System's capabilities planning model is geared toward developing military capabilities that guarantee autonomous defense against any external military state aggression

[367] Argentine initiatives to prevent massive human rights violations worldwide, its collaboration in establishing mechanisms for the prevention of genocide, its active participation in the creation and operation of the International Criminal Court, its leading role in drafting and signing the International Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance, its campaign for its ratification, and its acceptance of the Committee's jurisdiction, as well as its development of the Right to the Truth, are all examples of Argentina's commitment to the comprehensive promotion and protection of human rights

[368] In a globalized world, and given the levels of integration and cooperation achieved in the South American region, it is unacceptable to consider national defense in isolation and independently of global and regional strategic conditions. It should be emphasized that the cooperative aspect of national defense in no way implies renouncing the development of the capabilities necessary for the autonomous exercise of legitimate defense against external military state aggression

[369] CHAPTER III FALKLANDS, SOUTH GEORGIA AND THE SOUTH SANDWICH ISLANDS, AND THE ARGENTINE ANTARCTIC SECTOR The ratification of the legitimate and imprescriptible sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands and the corresponding maritime and insular spaces, as they are an integral part of the national territory, and the strengthening of Argentine sovereignty rights over the Argentine Antarctic Sector, are central issues of the nation's foreign policy, which are understood from the perspective of the specific and proper responsibilities of national defense in its contribution to the actions aimed at substantiating the sovereign claims of reference and the operation of the specific political objectives derived from them

[370] The national defense policy related to the Malvinas issue responds to the guidelines of the State policy on the matter

[371] The National Constitution, in its First Transitory Clause, ratifies the legitimate and imprescriptible sovereignty of the Argentine Republic over the Malvinas, South Georgia and South Sandwich Islands and the corresponding maritime and insular spaces, as these are an integral part of the national territory

[372] Since January 3, 1833, when the United Kingdom forcibly expelled the Argentine authorities and inhabitants residing in the Malvinas Islands and began its occupation of that part of the national territory, the Argentine people have made their recovery and the full exercise of national sovereignty a permanent and inalienable objective, respecting the way of life of its inhabitants and in accordance with the principles of international law

[373] The Declaration on the Granting of Independence to Colonial Countries and Peoples contained in UN General Assembly Resolution 1514 (XV) established two guiding principles for decolonization: self-determination of colonized peoples subject to foreign subjugation, domination and exploitation, and territorial integrity, making explicit that any attempt aimed at breaking down, in whole or in part, the national unity of a country is incompatible with the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations

[374] In 1965, the General Assembly adopted Resolution 2065 (XX), a milestone of fundamental importance in the consideration of the Malvinas Question by the international community, which establishes that the provisions of the Declaration on the Granting of Independence of Colonial Countries and Peoples apply to the territory of the Malvinas Islands; takes note of the existence of a dispute between the Governments of the United Kingdom and Argentina as the only parties; invites the Governments of the United Kingdom and Argentina to enter into negotiations with a view to finding a peaceful solution to this problem, taking into account the provisions and objectives of the Charter of the United Nations and of Resolution 1514 (XV) and the interests of the population of the Islands, and also invites the two Governments to inform the Special Committee on Decolonization and the General Assembly of the outcome of their negotiations

[375] The South Atlantic conflict in 1982 did not alter the validity or nature of the dispute, as recognized by General Assembly Resolution 37/9 of 4 November 1982, less than five months after the end of the conflict, and all its subsequent resolutions

[376] As before 1982, the international community continued to recognize the relevance of the dispute through repeated pronouncements, year after year, by the General Assembly and the Special Committee on Decolonization

[377] Despite this and our country's continued willingness to negotiate, the United Kingdom has completely refused to engage in dialogue

[378] That country is attempting to distort the right to self-determination in its failed attempt to apply it to the British population it has transplanted over generations and resides on the Islands, and whose composition it controls through strict immigration policies

[379] Neither the General Assembly nor the United Nations Special Committee on Decolonization has ever adopted a resolution mentioning the application of the principle of self-determination to the inhabitants of the Islands

[380] The growing support of the international community for Argentina's legitimate rights in the sovereignty dispute over the Malvinas, South Georgia, and South Sandwich Islands and the surrounding maritime areas in forums such as the United Nations, OAS, MERCOSUR, UNASUR, ALBA, CELAC, Ibero-American Summits, ALADI, OLADE, G77 + China, ZPCAS, CARICOM, SICA, PARLACEN, among others, demonstrate that the "Malvinas Question" is a regional and global cause

[381] The Argentine Republic rejects and questions the unilateral British actions in the disputed area, which are contrary to the provisional understandings under the formula of sovereignty

[382] UN General Assembly Resolution 31/49 urges both parties to refrain from taking decisions that introduce unilateral changes to the situation while it undergoes the process recommended by the UN General Assembly

[383] Britain's unilateral actions currently pose an immeasurable risk to the defense of the South American region

[384] In addition to the possibility of serious ecological damage resulting from the lack of adequate measures to prevent environmental incidents by British companies carrying out illegal hydrocarbon exploration and exploitation activities on the Argentine continental shelf, the illegal granting of fishing licenses by the United Kingdom jeopardizes the sustainability of the exploitation of fish resources

[385] As a sign of this regional concern over the United Kingdom's misappropriation of resources, organizations such as CELAC, MERCOSUR, and UNASUR have spoken out in favor of Argentina's position

[386] In this regard, the commitment reached in November 2010 by UNASUR to adopt, in accordance with international law and its respective domestic legislation, all measures that can be regulated to prevent the entry into its ports of vessels flying the illegal flag of the Falkland Islands is noteworthy

[387] Furthermore, they committed to informing the Argentine government, within the framework of current international agreements, about any vessels or naval vessels sailing to the Falkland Islands, South Georgia, and the South Sandwich Islands, carrying cargo destined for illegal hydrocarbon and/or mineral activities on the Argentine continental shelf

[388] Recently, during the second half of 2014, the G77+China and the Latin American Energy Organization (OLADE) recognized the right of the Argentine Republic to take legal action in full compliance with international law and the relevant United Nations resolutions against unauthorized hydrocarbon exploration and exploitation activities

[389] The British military presence in the South Atlantic creates unnecessary and unjustified tension throughout the region

[390] The Argentine Republic has denounced this situation before the international community

[391] In this regard, on April 11, 2014, a note was sent to the UN Secretary General, as well as to the authorities of the United Nations Special Committee on Decolonization, the OAS, the Ibero-American Summit, UNASUR, CELAC, MERCOSUR, G77 + China, the Arab League, the African Union and ZPCAS, expressing concern about the British military deployment in the South Atlantic and the holding of military exercises

[392] Argentina's concern about this situation is shared by countries in the region, which have expressed their concern through multiple declarations by regional and biregional organizations, and especially by the legitimate coastal states of the South Atlantic, which have declared the area a zone of peace and cooperation and prohibited the introduction of weapons of mass destruction

[393] This concern, regarding the possibility of nuclear weapons or devices entering the South Atlantic, is shared by the member countries of UNASUR

[394] The CDS agreed, in the 2010 Implementation Procedures for Confidence- and Security-Building Measures, to adopt the necessary measures to require respect for and compliance with the commitment to prohibit the use, stockpiling, installation, deployment, or any other form of possession of any nuclear weapons by third States, particularly those possessing such weapons

[395] Likewise, these states were collectively called upon to withdraw the "Interpretative Declarations" to Protocols I and II of the Treaty of Tlatelolco, thereby ensuring that the territories of UNASUR member states, including the Malvinas, South Georgia, and South Sandwich Islands, remain free of nuclear weapons

[396] Latin American countries have firmly supported Argentina's legitimate rights in the sovereignty dispute over the Malvinas, South Georgia and South Sandwich Islands and the surrounding maritime areas, as evidenced by various declarations by the Organization of American States (OAS), UNASUR, the Bolivarian Alliance for the Peoples of Our America (ALBA), the Community of Latin American and Caribbean States (CELAC), MERCOSUR, the Rio Group, the G-77 + China, the South Atlantic Zone of Peace and Cooperation (ZPCAS), the Summit of South American and African Countries (ASA), and the Summit of South American and Arab Countries (ASPA

[397] In September 2011, the G-77 + China devoted a separate paragraph to the Malvinas issue in a final declaration for the first time

[398] The more than 130 foreign ministers of the group's member countries called on the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland to comply with the international community's demands and to resume negotiations with Argentina regarding the Falkland Islands

[399] The document states that the decision was taken "in order to find, as soon as possible, a peaceful solution" and that "governments must refrain from taking unilateral decisions

[400] The G77 + China in September 2014 not only reiterated the above, but also highlighted the right of Member States to permanent sovereignty over their energy resources, indicating that operations carried out by companies not authorized by the Argentine government in the area of the Malvinas Islands relating to the exploration of natural resources, especially hydrocarbon resources, are a serious detriment to the sovereign rights of the Argentine Republic over its continental shelf

[401] The Antarctic continent The national Antarctic policy is oriented towards strengthening Argentina's sovereignty rights over the Argentine Antarctic Sector, which is an integral part of the national territory, and maintaining Argentina's presence in that space

[402] The Ministry of Defense contributes to these efforts through logistical assistance in the execution of Antarctic activities, provided by the operational capabilities of the Nation's military instrument

[403] The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation (MRECIC) considers it of utmost importance to recover and optimize the logistical and operational capabilities of the military instrument necessary for the development of scientific activity, international cooperation, and the preservation of the Antarctic environment, in accordance with national legislation (including National Law No. 15,802 on the Ratification of the Antarctic Treaty) and the international instruments that make up the Antarctic Treaty System

[404] The Argentine Republic has maintained a permanent and uninterrupted presence in Antarctic territory since

[405] For 40 years, it was the only nation with a permanent presence on the continent, a fact that constitutes the best guarantee of its sovereignty south of 60° south latitude

[409] National defense, in its geographic dimension, encompasses the continental spaces, the Falkland Islands, South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands, the Argentine Antarctic Sector, and other island, maritime, and air spaces within the scope assigned by international standards and treaties signed by the nation

[410] Outer limit of the continental shelf After more than eleven years of work and within the period established by the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), on April 21, 2009, the Argentine Republic submitted to the United Nations Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf the scientific documentation that supports the technical basis for defining the outline of the outer limit of its continental shelf, which extends beyond its exclusive economic zone and along the natural extension of its continental territory, the islands of the South Atlantic and the Argentine Antarctic Sector

[411] Thus, by demarcating the continental shelf to the outer edge of the continental margin, which in some areas exceeds even 350 nautical miles, the Argentine Republic carried out an act of sovereign affirmation of its rights over a vast expanse of its continental shelf

[413] THE NATIONAL DEFENSE SYSTEM CHAPTER IV REGULATORY BASIS OF DEFENSE The current legal and administrative system for National Defense is framed within the principles of the Argentine Constitution and a set of laws and international treaties incorporated into it in its 1994 reform, the centerpiece of which is the National Defense Law of 1988, which replaced the one in force since

[414] The new Defense Law was progressively supplemented by the Internal Security Act of 1992, the Voluntary Military Service Act of 1994, the Restructuring of the Armed Forces Act of 1998, the National Intelligence Act of 2001, and the Comprehensive Reform of the Military Justice System Act of

[415] Derived from this body of law, a comprehensive set of regulatory standards has been issued over the last decade, aimed at establishing conceptual guidelines for making concrete management decisions, precisely determining the powers and responsibilities of the various actors that make up the Defense System

[416] The set of provisions and rules finds its primary foundation in the national Constitution, whose preamble already establishes “common defense” as one of the purposes of the State, differentiating it from another, also very important, purpose: internal peace

[417] These purposes and responsibilities of the State are strictly separated in the laws of National Defense and Internal Security

[418] The Constitution also establishes the obligation of every citizen to "arm themselves in defense of the country and this Constitution", and establishes balanced powers and competences for the legislative and executive branches, providing in Article 99 that the President of the Nation: - Is the Commander-in-Chief of all the armed forces of the Nation

[419] It provides for the nation's military positions, with the approval of the Senate, in granting positions or ranks to senior officers in the armed forces; and it alone operates on the battlefield

[420] It has the armed forces at its disposal, and is responsible for their organization and distribution according to the needs of the Nation

[421] Declare war and order reprisals with authorization and approval of Congress

[422] declares one or more points of the Nation under a state of siege, in the event of an external attack and for a limited period, with the approval of the Senate

[423] According to Article 753 of the Constitution, in matters of Defense, Congress is responsible for: Authorizing the Executive Branch to declare war or make peace

[424] Empower him to order retaliation, and establish regulations for such actions

[425] Establish the armed forces in times of peace and war, and establish the rules for their organization and government

[426] Allow the introduction of foreign troops into the territory of the Nation, and the withdrawal of national forces from it

[427] National Defense Law 23,554, sanctioned and promulgated in 1988, essentially modified the concept of defense prevalent in the previous law, Law 16,970 enacted in October

[428] This, imbued with the so-called National Security Doctrine, had established a virtually all-encompassing scope of security and was based on the notion of total and permanent conflict characteristic of the Cold War, foreseeing the possibility of an internal ideological enemy

[429] The definition of national defense in the new law, on the other hand, limits the conceptual scope to the response to external military aggression, including preparation for it during peacetime

[430] It also establishes a distinction between the categories of National Defense and Internal Security, which were previously included in a broad, comprehensive concept in the repealed law

[431] The 1988 law substantially strengthens the President's authority over defense matters, assigning him responsibility for conducting the war at the national strategic level as well as the military strategic level

[432] To this end, it legally abolishes the functions of commander-in-chief in each of the three armed forces (positions that combined administrative and operational leadership powers), with the operational leadership of the military instrument being the exclusive power of the President or, by his delegation, of the Minister of Defense

[433] Another key aspect of the law is the strengthening of the aforementioned minister's functions, who previously served only as an administrative support to the state's armed forces

[434] The legal framework now assigns the Minister of Defense authority over the Chiefs of Staff of each of the forces, as well as over the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and also the direction, organization, and coordination of defense-related activities that are not reserved for him or herself or carried out directly by the President of the Nation

[435] The National Defense Council (CODENA) is established as an advisory and assistance body to the Presidency of the Nation to determine conflict, risk, and threat situations that should receive the attention of the Defense System, as well as the measures that should be taken in this regard

[436] Another key aspect of the law is the strengthening and hierarchization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff (EMC), following, in this and other aspects, the experiences of the Falklands War

[437] The EMCO advises the Minister of Defense on matters of military strategy and, subject to the directives and supervision of the Presidency of the Nation and the Minister of Defense, performs the fundamental functions of joint action: the formulation of joint military doctrine, joint military planning, the direction of joint military training, the control of operational strategic planning, and the effectiveness of joint military action

[438] A fundamentally important aspect established in the Defense Law is the distinction between administrative and operational functions in the armed forces

[439] The armed forces are constituted in the bodies responsible, on the one hand, for the administration of the elements that comprise them, and on the other hand for the preparation for war of those same elements - as well as their logistical support -, all of them being liable to be assigned as components to the joint, specific or combined strategic operational commands whose holders in case of war lead the military operations (strategic operational level), planning such commands during peace the operations that they will have to undertake in the indicated case, also being in charge of the joint training of the components that depend on them

[440] According to the Defense Law, each of the armed forces does not have operational powers on its own; these are reserved for the President of the Nation, the Minister of Defense, and the operational commands

[441] The current Defense Law changed the chain of command during wartime, which in the repealed Law 16,970 went "from the President of the Nation, in his capacity as Supreme Commander of the Nation," to the holders of the strategic operational commands through the Joint Commanders-in-Chief of the armed forces, a circumstance that at the time determined that, as arises from the report of the Commission for the Analysis and Evaluation of Responsibilities in the South Atlantic Conflict (CAERCAS) declassified by Decree 200/2012 - better known as the Rattenbach Report -, the then Commanders-in-Chief of the armed forces frequently interfered with the authority of the Strategic Operational Commander over each of their respective armed forces

[442] Under the current Defense Law, the chain of command in wartime runs from the President of the Nation—military leadership of the war at the strategic military level—to the head of the command that conducts strategic operational operations, with those in charge of the Ministry of Defense (MINDEF), the EMCO, and the General Staffs of the Armed Forces acting as advisors to the President of the Nation for the leadership functions that are his responsibility

[443] Furthermore, the law establishes that the production of intelligence at the military strategic level will be the responsibility of an agency that will be integrated for this purpose with the other intelligence agencies of the armed forces, reporting directly and immediately to the person holding the position of head of the MINDEF (Article 15). This was fulfilled in 2001, following the creation of the National Directorate of Military Strategic Intelligence through National Law 25,520 (National Intelligence Law

[452] Regulatory Decree of the National Defense Law Eighteen years after its sanction and promulgation, Decree 727 of 2006 established the regulations of the Defense Law and further specified the strict concept of National Defense, referring it to the defense of the sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of the country against aggression by foreign military forces

[453] The regulations also specified the Ministry's powers, including the development of the principles, norms, and fundamental guidelines governing the exercise of the functions conferred on the JEMCO, the annual approval of military strategic planning, the readjustment of the organic and functional structures of the armed forces, and the creation of operational units

[456] Internal Security Law Law 24,059, approved and enacted in 1992, establishes in its first article "the legal, organic and functional bases of the system of planning, coordination, control and support of the national police effort aimed at guaranteeing internal security", which it defines in its second article as "the de facto situation based on law in which the liberty, life and property of the inhabitants, their rights and guarantees and the full validity of the institutions of the representative, republican and federal system established by the National Constitution are protected

[469] Thus, Argentina was included in the relatively small number of countries that practiced legislative control of these activities in the early 1990s

[470] Regulatory Decree of the Internal Security Law Decree 1273 of 1992 regulated the Internal Security Law and developed the fundamental aspects relating to the bodies created, highlighting the provisions relating to the Internal Security Council, the Crisis Committee, the Undersecretariat of Internal Security –today the Secretariat of Security–, the Planning and Control Center and the then called National Directorate of Internal Intelligence, today the National Directorate of Criminal Intelligence

[471] The Internal Security Act established a framework for policy formulation and the planning, coordination, control, and support of the actions necessary to guarantee internal security, with specific criteria and institutions for this purpose

[472] In relation to the defense system, it precisely determined the circumstances and forms of employment of the armed forces in internal security, consisting of support through services and elements that do not include intelligence and combat, characterizing the use of combat elements of the armed forces in internal security as particularly exceptional

[473] Regarding the link between internal security and the military sphere of defense, an issue already addressed in Articles 27 to 32, the regulations provide for support from the armed forces for internal security operations with their arsenal, quartermaster, veterinary, health, construction, and transportation services, as well as engineering and communications elements

[474] To this end, the aforementioned regulatory decree indicates that MINDEF will designate an EMCO representative to coordinate support with the Ministry of National Security, if required

[476] However, in no case does assistance imply subordination to the head of operations designated by the Crisis Committee, but rather will seek only to satisfy the requests formulated according to the capabilities of the support element

[477] National Law 24,429 on Voluntary Military Service, of 1995, established voluntary recruitment as the regular source of troop incorporation in Argentina, replacing compulsory conscription

[478] However, the latter remained in place for those exceptional cases in which the voluntary personnel incorporated was insufficient to cover the needs of the national Defense, requiring in this case the incorporation for a maximum period of one year of citizens who in the year of service would have reached eighteen years of age, requiring the sanction of a law of Congress

[479] The Voluntary Military Service Act introduced a significant change to the Defense System by replacing the previous compulsory military service in force since 1901 as the standard form of troop recruitment

[480] Beyond its strictly military needs, it had the objective of being an instrument of geographic cohesion and social and cultural integration of Argentine society at the beginning of the 20th century

[481] Towards the end of this century, the increased training requirements for soldiers resulting from the development of military technology, which led to a significant international trend toward the implementation of voluntary recruitment, plus the country's sociopolitical circumstances, led to the replacement of the troop recruitment system based on compulsory conscription (cadre-conscript system) with one based on the voluntary presentation of aspiring professional soldiers

[482] The law also enshrines rights to safeguard human dignity for citizens who, in exceptional situations and on a compulsory basis, provide service in the National Defense System - such as the principle of conscientious objection, creating the Substitute Social Service -, the elimination of anachronistic gender discrimination by establishing that voluntary military service is "the service that Argentine men and women perform by their own choice" and, finally, the possibility of optimizing the National Defense System itself through a model of volunteer soldiers motivated to learn the military profession, thus enabling full use of training and instruction for a longer period of time compared to the one-year duration of the previous compulsory military service

[483] Among other clarifications, the law established that citizens recruited into Voluntary Military Service would be classified as Volunteer Troops; that the number of soldiers and the quota per force would be set annually by the President of the Nation at the request of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; that these volunteers could perform operational, logistical, and administrative tasks; that the entry age ranges from eighteen to twenty-four years; and that service in the armed forces could last only until the age of twenty-eight

[484] It also defined the general conditions, benefits, and everything related to the military instruction and training of enlisted personnel in the tactical, technical, logistical, and administrative activities that those entering the service must receive

[485] Also, for the indicated exceptional cases in which it was essential to resort to compulsory conscription, it provided for conscientious objection and the performance in such a case of a Substitute Social Service, establishing the characteristics of this in the performance of activities of public utility, which may be fulfilled in the performance of tasks of protection and civil defense, health, social or educational services, environmental conservation, improvement of the rural environment and protection of nature

[486] It also determines the institutions and organizations that will coordinate the performance of the Substitute Social Service, establishing the impediments, obligations, and rights of the persons who perform it
