[489] Regulation of Voluntary Military Service Decree 978/1995 of the National Executive Branch regulated Law 24,429, developing the modalities of provision of Voluntary Military Service and the rules for its application in the three armed forces

[490] These regulations indicate that personnel incorporated under this regime will be grouped into the aforementioned classification of Voluntary Troops (according to Law 19101/1971 for military personnel), with remuneration corresponding to the ranks of second or first class volunteers, enjoying social security benefits and the incorporation must be carried out in a jurisdictional manner by each of the forces

[491] It is also established that the personnel incorporated will perform operational and service functions, and that in the assignment of roles they will form the basis of the hierarchical scale of the permanent staff, with their possible incorporation into the ranks and specialties of noncommissioned officers being foreseen

[492] Likewise, it is contemplated that volunteer soldiers will attend specific training courses depending on whether they perform technical functions or require such training. It is stipulated that responsibility for training will be jurisdictional and preceded by initial basic training

[493] Armed Forces Restructuring Law Law 24,948, enacted in March 1998, established the following objectives: a) the promotion of vocationally motivated military personnel with high theoretical and practical professional training; b) the reduction in the number of operational units and the simultaneous increase in their efficient and effective logistical support, enabling these units to carry out prolonged operations that allow for actions in different specialties and geographic areas; c) the consolidation of commands and general staffs trained to permanently conduct operations, conduct studies, planning, and support leadership at the levels of military strategy, operational strategy, and higher tactics; d) the development of political, strategic, logistical, and mobilization forecasts that will allow, in conflict situations, to increase the operational capabilities of the armed forces in a short period of time; and e) the determination of budgetary allocations that will allow the aforementioned objectives to be met

[494] Another notable aspect of the restructuring law is the provision that the leadership and strategic planning levels will analyze the possible development of a common defense system within the framework of MERCOSUR, considering the requirements that might arise from such agreements

[495] This constitutes a precedent for the cooperative aspect of Argentine defense and the country's commitment to regional integration, which would be further refined and consolidated since the beginning of the current century

[496] As guiding guidelines for restructuring, the law considers the division of the national territory into strategic areas, each equipped with a joint strategic operational command with the mission of conducting studies, forecasting, and developing the doctrines of its specialty and responsibility for the area. In this regard, the concentration of units from the three armed forces comprising each command in contiguous zones is contemplated, thereby facilitating joint training

[497] In the same spirit, the 1998 regulation also provides for prioritizing the formation of joint armed forces over specific units. Furthermore, for restructuring purposes—and especially considering potential deployment needs—the country's geographic expanse, the low population density in some areas, and the possibility of concentrating units in a smaller number of bases. These units could be supplemented with others to be installed if necessary, prioritizing rapid deployment capacity

[498] National Law 24,948 on the Restructuring of the Armed Forces prioritizes the quality of personnel, ensuring that the educational systems of the Armed Forces are aligned with the national educational structure and establishing the requirement of academic qualifications for promotion to certain ranks

[499] The law prioritizes the quality of personnel over their quantity, seeking excellence through the application of the concept of promotion by "selection and vacancy," ensuring the most intensive use of experience and extending the active service period of both male and female military personnel

[500] To this end, it provides that specific education systems be adapted to the national educational structure, ensuring better integration of their members into the general educational cultural environment, and also establishing the requirement of holding academic degrees or qualifications for promotion to certain levels

[501] It should also be noted that the law establishes criteria for decision-making regarding the procurement of material resources for the Defense

[502] In this regard, it establishes that MINDEF will be responsible for evaluating and deciding on the requirements for equipping the forces in the manner that best contributes to meeting the operational capabilities necessary for the joint achievement of national defense objectives

[503] Regarding the alternatives planned for analyzing the equipment, he proposes, in this order: a) whether it is feasible and acceptable to recover the decommissioned material; b) modernize the available material; and c) as a last resort, incorporate new material, in which case priority should be given to those that enhance deterrent capacity, promote joint standardization with existing equipment, and contribute new technological developments

[504] The Armed Forces Restructuring Law continued and deepened the path initiated by the National Defense Law toward establishing and strengthening the political leadership of defense, strengthening joint military action, and pursuing economy, efficiency, and effectiveness in military matters

[505] It completed the list of Armed Forces missions derived from the Defense Law and the Internal Security Law, incorporating peacekeeping missions mandated by the United Nations and operations in support of the national community and friendly countries

[506] It introduced innovative regulations for the incorporation of active military personnel for specific periods, as well as other regulations regarding decision-making regarding the procurement of material resources for defense, ensuring that this was done with rational criteria derived from joint military planning and under the direction of the Ministry of Defense

[507] The Armed Forces Restructuring Law represents a step forward on the path toward establishing solid political leadership for defense—which began with the Defense Law—strengthening joint military action, and pursuing economy, efficiency, and effectiveness in military matters

[508] The National Intelligence Law and the legal framework for intelligence for Defense, Law 25.520 on National Intelligence, sanctioned and promulgated in 2001, provided for the first time the structuring of the National Intelligence System, establishing its main agencies and their functional relationships

[509] It also established limits on intelligence activity, expressly safeguarding the individual rights of the country's inhabitants, and stipulated that an ad hoc Bicameral Commission in the National Congress would exercise specific oversight

[510] Law 27.126, published in the Official Gazette on March 5, 2015, reforms the aforementioned Law 25.520, maintains the spirit that guided its predecessor and, replacing the dissolved Intelligence Secretariat, creates the National Intelligence Agency as the highest body of the National Intelligence System, assuming the coordination of its elements, the production of national strategic intelligence and counterintelligence activities

[511] National Law 27.126 of 2015 created the National Intelligence Agency as the highest agency of the National Intelligence System

[512] Protection of the rights and guarantees of the population The National Defense Law establishes that issues relating to the country's internal politics may under no circumstances constitute working hypotheses for military intelligence agencies

[513] National Intelligence Law 25.520, along with the reform implemented by Law 27.126, stipulates that intelligence agencies carry out their activities in accordance with the provisions of the National Constitution, the Human Rights Treaties they have signed and those to which they may be signed, and any other regulations establishing rights and guarantees

[514] It also prevents: - Carrying out repressive tasks, possessing compulsive powers, or performing police functions on one's own

[515] Nor may they perform criminal investigation functions, except upon specific and well-founded request made by a competent judicial authority within the framework of a specific case under their jurisdiction, or if they are authorized to do so by law, in which case the corresponding procedural rules will apply

[516] Obtaining information, producing intelligence, or storing data about individuals solely because of their religious faith, private actions, political opinions, membership in or affiliation with partisan, social, union, community, cooperative, welfare, cultural, or labor organizations, or because of any lawful activity they engage in in any sphere of activity

[517] Influencing in any way the institutional, political, military, police, social, and economic situation of the country, its foreign policy, the internal life of legally constituted political parties, public opinion, individuals, the media, or legal associations or groups of any kind

[518] Reveal or divulge any type of information obtained in the exercise of their duties relating to any inhabitant or legal entity, whether public or private, unless there is a court order or dispensation

[519] It also establishes that intelligence agencies must excusably frame their activities within the general provisions of Law 25.326 on the Protection of Personal Data, giving special protection to information about citizens or legal entities, public or private, obtained by intelligence agencies in the exercise of their functions

[520] It also guarantees the conditions and procedures regarding the collection, storage, production and dissemination of information, preventing its disclosure or release

[521] Different levels of military intelligence Strategic Defence Intelligence Obtains and processes information related to threats to the nation's external environment; directly advises the person in charge of the Ministry of Defense

[522] Focuses its capacity to obtain and process information on the capabilities and weaknesses of the military potential of countries of interest from the point of view of national defense, as well as the geographic environment of the strategic operational areas determined by military strategic planning

[523] Strategic Operational Intelligence

[524] It specializes in the knowledge, at all times, of the capabilities and weaknesses of enemies or opponents, real or potential, specified explicitly and opportunely by higher leadership, which are considered to be able to influence the use of one's own means and in the geographic environments of interest for the planning and conduct of military operations

[525] Tactical Intelligence** This refers to the knowledge of the capabilities and weaknesses of enemies or opponents, real or potential, and of the geographic environment of interest, necessary for the planning and conduct of military operations at both the higher and lower tactical levels

[526] The National Intelligence Law of 2001 marked the first step toward establishing the principle of political leadership in defense intelligence and consolidating the Defense Intelligence System, providing coherence and coordination to all military intelligence agencies and activities

[527] This law, in accordance with Article 15 of the National Defense Law, created the National Directorate of Military Strategic Intelligence, which reports directly and immediately to the person holding the position of head of the Ministry of Defense

[528] This allows for the production of a joint vision of military intelligence—avoiding the bias that each force might have—and guides all activities toward the goal of complying with the guidelines established by the political leadership of military intelligence activity under the direction of MINDEF

[529] This also makes it possible to specify the powers of military intelligence agencies in the fulfillment of their missions

[530] The 2015 reform of the National Intelligence Law reaffirms the spirit of the preceding precept regarding the subjection of all intelligence agencies and activities to the principle of legality, limiting them to the provisions of the National Constitution, the human rights treaties signed and those signed subsequently, and any other regulations that establish rights and guarantees

[531] Likewise, this reform establishes new criteria regarding the archiving, declassification, and dissemination of intelligence information, providing for the creation of data protection banks and intelligence archives throughout the scope of the law, and the strictest secrecy and confidentiality of the information safeguarded

[532] It also sets strict criteria for transparency in public management, incorporating criteria for expenditure, oversight and control of funds, and accountability

[533] Regarding the personnel of the agencies covered by the law, it establishes the obligation to submit sworn declarations of assets in accordance with public ethics standards

[534] Comprehensive reform of the military systems of discipline and justice Law 26.394 of 2008 repealed the Military Justice Code in force since 1951 (Law 14.029 and its regulations)7, modified the Penal and Criminal Procedure Codes, both of the Nation, and created the new Codes of Discipline of the Armed Forces and of the Joint Justice Service of the Armed Forces

[535] In line with the Principles on the Administration of Justice by Military Tribunals adopted by the United Nations, it abolished military jurisdiction in peacetime, assigning the trial of military crimes to federal civilian courts

[536] This means that, when it comes to the prosecution of crimes, military personnel now enjoy the same guarantees from impartial and independent judicial bodies as other citizens, and consequently have the full right to a defense in court

[537] Military crimes were incorporated into the Penal Code, and the death penalty, which was still provided for in the repealed code, was abolished

[538] Likewise, regulations were incorporated into the Code of Criminal Procedure to facilitate its application to the prosecution of military crimes, as well as a military criminal procedure for wartime

[539] The law included a Code of Discipline based on the pursuit of effective performance by military professionals, ensuring the validity of adequate discipline without prejudice to the validity of procedures that ensure the right to defense and other individual rights protected by the Constitution of the Argentine Nation and the human rights treaties to which constitutional hierarchy has been assigned (article 75, paragraph

[540] National Defense covers in its geographical dimension the continental spaces, the Malvinas Islands, South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands and other insular, maritime and air spaces of the Republic, as well as the Argentine Antarctic sector, with the scope assigned by international standards and treaties signed or to be signed by the Nation, also considering citizens and national assets in third countries, in international waters and in international airspace (article 5 of National Law

[541] National defense is the "integration and coordinated action of all the nation's forces to resolve conflicts requiring the use of the Armed Forces, whether as a deterrent or effective means, to confront external aggression." Its purpose is to "permanently guarantee the nation's sovereignty and independence, its territorial integrity and capacity for self-determination, and to protect the life and liberty of its inhabitants

[542] The Argentine Republic understands aggression of external origin, as defined by the Rome Statute10 of the International Criminal Court, as the use of armed force by a State against the sovereignty, territorial integrity or political independence of our country, or in any other form that is incompatible with the Charter of the United Nations

[543] The Argentine Defense System is based on two principles that are the product of broad political and social consensus and that have cemented its normative foundations: the civilian governance of Defense and the conceptual differentiation between national defense and internal security

[544] The structural and operational logic of the defense leadership body and the military instrument itself are derived from these principles

[545] Civil and Political Government of Defense The full exercise by the legitimately constituted civil authorities of the government of Defense and its military instrument, the armed forces, constitutes the main pillar of the system

[546] Based on this, the national strategic level explicitly guides defense policy and its corresponding military policy for the organization and operation of the military instrument

[547] Within the civilian government of Defense, the national strategic level effectively assumes its responsibilities and powers for the planning, evaluation, and control of all its activities, encompassing all facets: human resources, training, operations, equipment, logistics, and finance

[548] Conceptual differentiation between National Defense and Internal Security The Argentine State conceives National Defense and Internal Security as two non-delegable responsibilities that, due to their different nature, deserve a specific approach, strictly regulated and with specialized bodies and instruments

[549] National Defense differs from Internal Security due to the nature of its functions and the diversity of the areas in which it is exercised

[550] Within the national territory, its jurisdictional waters and airspace are governed by Argentine law and its sole coercive order

[551] Thus, the State, in its role of guaranteeing internal security, prevents and seeks to prevent the commission of crimes, and when these occur, it identifies, pursues, and prosecutes the perpetrator or perpetrators, charges them, judges them within the framework of constitutional guarantees, and, if appropriate, sentences them

[552] All of this with investigative capacity, knowledge of criminal procedural law and substantive criminal law, the application of the minimum necessary force, rationality, gradualness, strict adaptation of means to ends, and, especially, the protection of life and physical integrity

[553] At the international level, it is imperative that the State itself develop a defense policy in the event that it becomes necessary to protect national heritage and the lives and rights of the country's inhabitants from attacks by other states

[554] This may involve significant violence and the use of high-powered weapons

[555] Facing external military aggression constitutes the greatest risk a State can be forced to face, and its prevention demands the development of an adequate defense system

[556] There are also various public assets that need to be protected. First and foremost are the rights and freedoms of the country's inhabitants, which must be guaranteed by the political system

[557] And in the second, the very existence of the Nation, its integrity and survival

[558] The rights and freedoms of all inhabitants are the object of internal security, and the integrity and survival of the Nation are the object of defense

[559] This difference in objectives entails the need for specific policies and instruments for each one

[560] From this principle derives the functional and operational specialization of State agencies in the areas of Defense, on the one hand, and Internal Security, on the other

[561] Since the restoration of the rule of law in 1983, the need to differentiate between the spheres of Defense and Internal Security has been progressively consolidated in a new body of regulations resulting from a widespread political and social consensus

[562] The National Constitution in its preamble already establishes internal peace and common defense as two independent objects or motives

[563] Laws 23.554 on National Defense and 24.059 on Internal Security interpret these constitutional principles and unequivocally establish the objectives of each of the respective systems

[564] That of Defense to ward off aggressions of external origin perpetrated by armed forces belonging to one or more other states, that of Internal Security to preserve or restore with the help of police and security institutions "the de facto situation based on the law in which the freedom, life and property of the inhabitants, their rights and guarantees and the full validity of the institutions of the representative, republican and federal system established by the National Constitution are protected

[565] National defense differs from internal security due to the nature of the functions to be exercised and the diversity of the areas in which such exercise must take place

[566] The Argentine State's differentiation of both responsibilities does not ignore the complex dynamics of transnational criminal phenomena and provides for the possibility of an orderly complementarity between the two systems in its legal and institutional framework

[567] This separation generally implies the exclusion of the armed forces from internal security matters, except for the collaboration they may provide in specific and exceptional cases established in the respective laws and regulations

[568] In this way, the legislation professionally focuses each of the State agencies on their corresponding missions and functions

[569] The Argentine Republic thus has specialized institutions to address these issues in a differentiated manner: the armed forces for national defense, and the security forces and police institutions for internal security (National Gendarmerie, Argentine Naval Prefecture, Airport Security Police, Argentine Federal Police, and provincial police forces

[570] While the Defense System's mission is to repel military aggression from other States, the Internal Security System's primary purpose is the prevention and prosecution of crimes defined in the Penal Code and other special laws

[571] These differences in the problems to be solved imply specific training, equipment and employment doctrines

[572] Phenomena such as drug trafficking, organized crime, economic crimes, money laundering, and transnational terrorism do not fall within the responsibilities, powers, and instruments of the Argentine defense system under the Argentine legal and institutional framework

[573] Addressing these criminal acts is the responsibility of the internal security system through its police, security, and intelligence agencies, in accordance with current legislation

[574] Purpose of the National Defense System Law 23.554 in its article 8 specifies that the purpose of the National Defense System is: a) The formulation of plans that contribute to the preparation of the Nation for a possible armed conflict, and for the conduct of the national Defense in the strategic military and operational aspects

[575] To address the direction of the war in all its aspects from the level of national strategy

[576] To lead the armed forces, as well as the efforts of other sectors of the country affected by a war, at the strategic military and operational levels

[577] d) Prepare and implement national mobilization measures

[578] e) Ensure the execution of joint military operations of the armed forces, and eventually combined operations that may be carried out between two or more countries

[579] Establish the necessary alliances to adequately resolve the possible outbreak of war, as well as to control post-war actions

[580] The National Defense System is oriented, both structurally and organizationally and functionally, to the determination and maintenance of the National Defense Policy aimed at warding off external military aggressions perpetrated by other states

[581] Any matter related to or related to internal security, a responsibility that falls under the purview of other state agencies organized and trained for this purpose, is outside its jurisdiction in matters of doctrine, planning, training, and intelligence production

[582] DEFENSE SYSTEM INTERNAL SECURITY SYSTEM Repel military aggression from other States

[583] Prevent and prosecute crimes classified in the Penal Code and other special laws

[584] Obtains and preserves evidence as an assistant to the Judicial Branch

[585] Operational organizations Armed Forces • Argentine Army • Argentine Navy • Argentine Air Force Police institutions and security forces • Argentine National Gendarmerie • Argentine Naval Prefecture • Airport Security Police • Argentine Federal Police • Provincial and CABA police forces Defense and internal security systems Powers of the members of the National Defense System 4.1 President of the Nation The President of the Nation exercises the highest authority of the National Defense System and is Commander-in-Chief of the armed forces

[586] The citizen holding the National Executive Branch is responsible for directing defense and leading the armed forces, powers conferred upon him or her by the National Constitution

[587] It establishes, with the advice of the National Defense Council (CODENA), the content and guidelines for the implementation of national defense planning, controlling its design and execution

[588] The head of the Executive Branch is thus responsible for the comprehensive management of the war with the advice and assistance of the aforementioned CODENA, and the military management of the war with the assistance and advice of the Minister of Defense, the Head of the EMCO, and the Chiefs of the General Staffs constituted in a "Crisis Committee

[589] The National Defence Policy Directive (NDPD) is the principal civilian defence policy guidance document

[590] It is issued by the President of the Nation and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, spelling out the central guidelines of national defense policy and military policy, while also determining the criteria and parameters that will guide the organization, operation, planning, employment, and administration of the human and material resources of the Armed Forces

[591] It is also the document that initiated the Strategic Planning Cycle (Decree 1729 of 2007) and therefore the articulator of the capacity-based planning model that would allow us to overcome the outdated planning schemes based on conflict hypotheses

[592] In this regard, it is worth highlighting the recent issuance of the second NDPD through Decree 2645 of 2014, thus initiating a new Planning Cycle that should conclude with a Military Capabilities Plan

[593] National Congress The Argentine Constitution establishes the prerogatives of the National Congress, which in matters of defense are: to authorize the Executive Branch to declare war or make peace and to order reprisals; to establish the armed forces in times of peace and war, and to dictate the rules for their organization and government; to permit the introduction of foreign troops into the nation's territory and the withdrawal of national forces from it

[594] In the event of an external attack, it is the exclusive prerogative of the Senate of the Nation to authorize the declaration of a state of siege in the Republic

[595] It also approves, through its Agreements Commission, promotions to the rank of senior officers in the armed forces

[596] For its part, the Chamber of Deputies is exclusively responsible for initiating laws on contributions and troop recruitment

[597] Parliamentary participation in the Defense System is also exercised through the request for reports from the national Executive Branch

[598] As an integral body of the Defense System, CODENA is chaired by the person who legitimately holds the Executive Branch of the Nation and is made up of the head of the Senate – Vice President of the Nation –, the ministers of the national cabinet, the head of the national intelligence agency at the highest organic-institutional level, the legislators who chair the Defense Committees of the Senate and the Chamber of Deputies of the Nation, and two members of said committees – one from the majority bloc and another from the first minority bloc – and, when the Minister of Defense deems it necessary, the Head of the EMCO and the Chiefs of the General Staff may also be summoned

[599] CODENA's mission is to assist and advise the President of the Nation in determining conflicts and preparing plans and coordinating the actions necessary for their resolution

[600] Its responsibility is to provide assistance and advice on matters related to determining the basic guidelines of national defense policy, through the design and preparation of reports, evaluations, opinions, or periodic or special projects to identify risk situations that may affect national sovereignty and independence

[601] The Council is also responsible for preparing diagnoses of the national strategic situation, specifying and describing actors, situations, and trends that, whether at the regional or global levels, are of interest to national defense

[602] The diagnostics will seek to identify areas or spheres of interest for the development and design of projects and proposals for joint work with the various departments of the State on matters related to national defense, which, given their nature, require an interdisciplinary approach from the national State

[603] Within the framework of these procedures, the final preparation of documents is the responsibility of MINDEF, which acts as executive secretariat of CODENA

[604] This ministry is responsible for the direction, organization and coordination of the activities of national defense that are not reserved or carried out directly by the citizen or legitimate holder of the Executive Power, or that are not attributed by law to another body, organization or official

[605] The MINDEF, through its participation in CODENA, assists and advises the President of the Nation in the overall conduct of the war, and only on its own initiative in the military conduct of war

[606] It is responsible for developing and implementing Defense Policy and Military Policy, particularly those relating to the organization, operation, deployment, human resources, infrastructure, logistics, material, information, training, and doctrine of the military instrument

[607] The Ministry also establishes the qualifications required to serve as Chief of the Joint Chiefs of Staff of the Armed Forces and Chief of the General Staffs of each of the forces

[608] Its responsibilities also include developing the fundamental principles, standards, and guidelines that govern the exercise of the functions conferred on the EMCO, approving Military Strategic Planning, and adapting the forces' organic and functional structures and creating new operational units

[609] Likewise, it also formulates and submits to the head of the Executive Branch and the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces proposals for promotion, continuation in rank, retirement, or discharge of senior military personnel (officers) of the three armed forces, following an evaluation of their background, qualifications, and professional performance

[610] It is also a ministerial responsibility to submit to the President of the Nation the evaluation of the background, qualifications, and professional performance of those members of the armed forces who meet the requirements to occupy the positions of Chief of the EMCO or Chief of the General Staff of each of the armed forces

[611] As a specific clarification of the powers and responsibilities of the MINDEF, the general regulatory body of the State also establishes that the "war powers – of the President of the Nation, in his capacity as Commander-in-Chief of the armed forces – and his constitutional powers in this matter will correspond to the office of the Minister of Defense

[612] Other ministerial powers specified in the Argentine regulatory framework are the following: Political responsibility as an organ of the national Executive Branch for the organization and operation of the Defense System and its component agencies

[613] Responsibility in the senior management of the operation and general organization of the armed forces, the execution of the Defense Planning Cycle and the implementation of the corresponding military policy

[614] • Responsibility in the systemic and comprehensive management of national defense resources, maximizing efficiency in their use, and achieving effective joint military action

[615] • Responsibility for the military instrument to adopt the organizational and functional forms required by military strategic planning or by decisions issued by the National Executive Branch

[617] Joint Chiefs of Staff of the Armed Forces The Joint Chiefs of Staff (EMCO) advises the Minister of Defense on military strategy

[618] It covers military strategic planning, joint military planning, the formulation of joint military doctrine, the direction of joint military training, and the control of operational strategic planning and the effectiveness of joint military action

[619] It is also responsible for the use of the armed forces' resources in times of peace

[620] To this end, it has a permanent operational command responsible for the direction and coordination of operational activity (Decree 727/2006) and has functional control over the armed forces, with the authority to issue orders

[621] According to the provisions of Decree 727/2006, the Argentine Army (EA), the Argentine Navy (ARA) and the Argentine Air Force (FAA) make up the Argentine military instrument, which is conceived as a single integrating body of the action modalities of each of the forces

[622] Military action must be understood as necessarily integrated, even in those cases in which, due to the characteristics of the operation, the This assumption has not occurred on any occasion since the sanction of the referred law until the publication of this book

[632] The organizational structure of the Ministry of Defense has been modified on several occasions since the early years of the 21st century in order to strengthen the political leadership of the Defense System

[633] The ministerial organizational structure approved in February 2000 by Decree 134 comprised, at the political level, two secretariats (Military Affairs and Planning) and one undersecretariat (Coordination), while the technical advisory body comprised a total of eight general directorates, six of which were for technical advice and two for administrative support

[634] Subsequently, by Administrative Decision JGM 21, in 2002, a national directorate (Intelligence) was incorporated, a general directorate of administrative support was added, and two technical advisory directorates were reduced

[635] In 2003, two undersecretariats (Institutional Strengthening and Technical-Military Affairs) were created by Decree 1,336, and in 2006, in accordance with the provisions of Decree 1,648, a new national directorate (Human Rights) was formed

[636] The following year, in 2007, by Decree 788, a new secretariat (International Affairs) was established and two existing undersecretariats were modified to create two new ones (Training and Research and Development

[637] At the technical level, the general support directorates were maintained and five new technical advisory units were created, covering management areas such as peacekeeping operations, training, research and development, and logistics and industrial planning

[638] Subsequently, in 2008, a general advisory directorate (Planning and Strategy) and the general directorate of the Defense Logistics Service (Decree 1,451) were added

[639] In mid-2013, the National Executive Branch decided to prioritize the coordination of various state agencies in response to emergency situations. For this purpose, the Secretariat of Military Coordination for Emergency Assistance was created, along with its corresponding Undersecretariats for Executive Coordination in Emergencies and Planning for Emergency Assistance, through Decree

[640] On the other hand, the same regulatory instrument consolidated the political and bureaucratic leadership of the national effort in defense research, production, and development with the creation of the Secretariat of Science, Technology, and Defense Production

[641] As a result of this latest change, the Directorate General of Military Manufacturing was transferred from the Ministry of Planning to the Ministry of Defense

[642] In 2014, the opening of lower-level positions for the most recently created secretariats and undersecretariats was approved, while the rank of the Defense Logistics Service director was changed, becoming an undersecretariat in accordance with Decree

[643] This new decree intensified the trend toward specialization by thematic area by establishing six technical assistance units for emergency coordination (all general directorates); eight for scientific and technological research and development (two national directorates and six single directorates); four for resource management (all national directorates); and seven for logistics services (one national directorate, one general directorate, and five single directorates

[644] The current structure of MINDEF was finally defined with the creation of the General Directorate of Cyber Defense, dependent on the Ministerial Unit

[645] Cyber defense is becoming increasingly important as a state capacity for sovereign protection and use of cyberspace quotas that are essential, vital, or necessary for the functioning of the military instrument, the components of the Defense System, and critical national infrastructures

[646] Cyberspace, as an area or object of interest for Defense, has received various attention, approaches, and proposals within the Ministry of Defense since 2006, with the creation of an Information Security Committee and the establishment of working groups to analyze its strategic and regulatory implications for the National Defense System

[647] The South American Defense Council of UNASUR, for its part, established a working group in 2012 to establish a regional policy and mechanisms to address cyber threats

[648] In this context, Mindef decided to participate in the national policy on the matter in two simultaneous dimensions: Adherence to the National Program for Critical Information and Cybersecurity Infrastructures (JGM Resolution 580/2011), with the aim of achieving the minimum information security standards required by the jurisdiction and its decentralized agencies

[649] Coordination of the various capabilities and specialized units generated within the Ministry of Defense and the Armed Forces, in order to design a comprehensive policy, an organizational-institutional proposal, and develop integrated response mechanisms

[650] Thus, through Ministerial Resolution 385 of October 22, 2013, the Cyber Defense Coordination Unit was created within the Office of the Chief of Staff of the Minister of Defense, with the function of coordinating the policies and performance of the actors linked to cyber defense in the jurisdiction

[651] In this way, MINDEF integrated the efforts made to date, developed a work plan for 2014-2015, and designed the necessary organizational proposal

[652] The plan of activities included the following priority objectives: - Improve infrastructure and security levels, including standardization and technical aspects

[653] Generate dissemination strategies through training and awareness-raising tools within and outside the ministry; - Develop exchange and cooperation links with academia, science, business, and other government agencies

[654] Promote specific relations on this matter, both at the CDS-UNASUR level and bilaterally with the member countries, as well as with the OAS and countries of the European Union

[655] The Joint Cyber Defense Command was created by Resolution MD 344/2014 and depends organically, functionally and operationally on the EMCO, being headed by a senior EA officer

[656] Its main objective is to generate the capacity to ward off and repel cyberattacks against critical information infrastructure and assets of the National Defense System and its military instruments

[657] The command's activities have focused primarily on determining equipment, communications, and network needs; assessing the capabilities of each force; analyzing research and development projects in this area; and coordinating related training courses

[658] The General Directorate of Cyber Defense was created by Administrative Decision 15/2015 within the structure of the Ministry of Defense

[659] Its primary responsibility is to intervene in the planning, formulation, direction, supervision, and evaluation of cyber defense policies for the jurisdiction and for the military instrument

[660] Its functions include coordination with other state agencies and authorities and promoting exchanges and cooperation in the academic, scientific, and business sectors

[661] Both agencies, the Joint Cyber Defense Command and the General Directorate of Cyber Defense, operate jointly and are headquartered at the Cyber Defense Center

Historical overview The current Joint General Staff of the Armed Forces (EMCO) has its origin in Law 13,234 passed by the National Congress on September 9, 1948, which established the general guidelines regarding national defense based on new concepts in force in the world on this topic after the experience of the Second World War

[686] From an administrative point of view, the constitution of EMCO was established by Decree 1,775 of January

[687] Its organization, missions, dependencies and other functional aspects were established by the regulations of the Coordination General Staff (Decree 1,776 of the same date

[688] These rules responded to the need to clarify and regulate the aforementioned law

[689] By Resolution of the EMCO itself dated August 29, 1951 (23/951), signed by the ministers secretaries of State for National Defense, Army, Navy and Air Force, and on the occasion of the creation of the MINDEF, the dependence of this General Staff on this ministry was established, and aspects relating to its mission, relations, functions and tasks were modified

[690] On February 3, 1967, National Defense Law 16,970 was enacted. Article 55 of the Law established that the National Executive Branch would regulate by decree "the basic organizational composition and operating procedures of the agencies created within the National Security Planning and Action System

[691] Decrees 738/67 and 739/67 of the same date established the bodies of the National Security Planning and Action System, either by creating new units or by organically modifying existing ones

[692] Among the latter was the Coordination Staff, which was then renamed the Joint Staff of the Armed Forces

[693] Mission and Functions The EMCO is the highest military authority for advice and assistance to the head of the MINDEF in matters of military strategy

[694] It is also responsible for: - Formulating joint military doctrine

[695] Develop joint military planning

[696] Direct joint military training

[697] Control operational planning and the effectiveness of joint military action

[698] The EMCO strives for maximum integration and standardization of the set of rules, processes, procedures, functions, services, and activities related to the efficient use or employment of military assets, as well as the strengthening and consolidation of operational capabilities

[699] The Joint Chiefs of Staff of the Armed Forces is responsible for formulating joint doctrine, developing joint military planning, directing joint military training, and overseeing and controlling operational planning

[700] It is the body responsible for the use of military resources in peacetime, and to this end, it exercises functional control over the General Staffs of each of the Armed Forces, and operational control over their elements

[701] October

[702] The head of the EMCO is responsible for the use of military assets in peacetime, having functional control over the armed forces, with the authority to issue orders and dispose of such assets to carry out the missions assigned within the framework of military strategic planning

[703] For the purposes of joint military action, it maintains a functional relationship with the Chiefs of Staff of each of the armed forces, who advise it on joint military planning

[704] The Joint Operational Command's missions are to direct and coordinate the operational activities carried out by the armed forces in peacetime; propose and develop operational planning; and conduct military operations in crisis and conflict situations until the Theater of Operations Operational Command is established

[705] These missions are intended to contribute to the fulfillment of the peacetime operational responsibilities assigned to EMCO with respect to joint military planning and the effectiveness of joint actions

[706] The functions of the Operational Commander are: To exercise operational command over joint commands/joint task forces (or specific) to accomplish the missions assigned to him. To propose to the head of the EMCO the incorporation of resources outside the armed forces that may be necessary to carry out the assigned operational missions. To perform the functions of the National Electoral Commander on occasions designated by the national government

[707] • Conduct joint military civil protection operations when the Ministry of Defense authorizes the use of armed forces, both in the country and abroad. • Exercise operational command over emergency zone commands when a national emergency is declared

[708] The Joint Cyber Defense Command Cyberspace has become a new, man-made domain where social interactions occur with increasing frequency and where international armed conflict, as a social phenomenon, could develop

[709] Cyberspace is not a specific operational military domain, but rather an operational dimension that cuts across traditional operational environments and in which military operations can be carried out, which requires joint military planning

[710] Under these considerations, through Resolution MD 343 of May 14, 2014, the Ministry of Defense created the Joint Cyber Defense Command

[711] Its commander was put into office on the following June

[712] This new command, under the EMCO, is tasked with conducting ongoing cyber defense operations to ensure the military operations of the nation's military instrument in accordance with the guidelines established in military strategic planning

[713] Likewise, it must be capable of warding off and repelling cyberattacks against critical information infrastructure and assets of the National Defense System and its dependent military instrument

[714] From a planning perspective, the Joint Cyber Defense Command is responsible for developing the Cyber Defense Employment Plan, following the directives issued by the EMCO, which is responsible for submitting the Plan to the MINDEF for consideration and eventual approval

[715] For their part, the General Staffs of the armed forces are responsible for developing cyber defense capabilities that contribute to the mission assigned to the Joint Cyber Defense Command

[718] For this reason, the land component of the military instrument is conceived according to three types of military force: The Regional Response Forces, composed of those organizations pre-positioned and adapted to the geostrategic space where they will normally be employed: the mountains, the hills and the Patagonian plateau

[719] The Main Defense Forces, composed of elements of the Force prepared to execute decisive military operations for the defense or recovery of areas under their jurisdiction. The Rapid Intervention Forces, comprised of organizations with great strategic, operational, and tactical agility, with flexible characteristics, a high degree of preparation, and available to be deployed in areas of jurisdiction and interest

[720] Argentine Navy Just as with land spaces, maritime areas under national jurisdiction are of enormous proportions

[721] Added to this is an extensive river network that constitutes an important communication route to and from the interior of the continent

[722] This has created a historic need to operate in the maritime, river, and island operational spheres with an adequate deployment of support bases, both for the technical support of naval units and for coastal surveillance for national defense purposes

[723] The size of the areas involved and the importance of maritime and waterway routes for international trade, regional productive development, and communications in general, highlight the need for naval forces with sufficient operational capabilities to adequately fulfill their role as a naval component of the military instrument

[724] Through the National Maritime Search and Rescue Agency (SAR), the Argentine Navy (ARA) fulfills its responsibilities to safeguard human life at sea within the framework of the 1979 Hamburg SAR Convention of the International Maritime Organization (IMO

[725] Argentine Air Force The dimensions of the airspace in its correspondence with the Earth’s surface and from there to outer space, and the dynamics that develop and project onto that space, generate an undeniable impact on matters of national defense

[726] This raises the need for its permanent strategic monitoring and control in relation to both its uses and the denial and prevention of such uses through an effective aerospace defense system, as determined by joint military planning

[727] The deployment, readiness conditions, technological and operational quality of the resources, and the control capacity of the spaces—including the satellite segment—determine the level of capability the system requires to meet the employment forecasts outlined in the aforementioned planning

[728] The design of the aerospace component of a military instrument, within the framework of adequate operational, logistical, and technological performance, must consider the capacity for networked and real-time planning, the integration of surveillance and control systems from the various operational areas in the areas of interest, joint and combined interoperability standards, the flexibility to modify the defensive axis, and precision in engagement

[729] The organization of each of the Argentine armed forces has a similar senior leadership structure, headed in each case by the respective Chief of the General Staff, and which includes a support structure dependent on the Deputy Chief of the General Staff and a Readiness and Training Command on which the operational units depend

[730] These commands are tasked with planning and conducting the preparation and training of operational and support resources within the framework of joint military planning

[731] The support structures common to all three forces include the areas of organization and doctrine, research and development, materiel, intelligence, education, health, personnel and welfare, and communications and information technology

[732] Argentine Army The Army Operational Force is under organic or functional dependence of the Army Readiness and Training Command (CAAE

[733] This is basically composed of three large battle units (army divisions) and a Rapid Deployment Force (RDF), in turn made up of brigades (large combat units), and these by Units, and Subunits and Independent Sections

[734] Brigades respond to the concept of combined arms systems, since the combat, fire support, combat support and logistics, and occasionally special operations elements that comprise them perform their specific functions synergistically to fulfill their mission

[735] The RDF is distinguished from the Army Divisions by the speed and flexibility of its forces, as well as by its projection capacity in the face of a crisis situation

[736] The Brigades that make up the Operational Force are the following: IV Airborne Brigade: It is made up of airborne tactical units capable of being used primarily by parachute drop or air assault with rotary-wing aircraft

[737] It has the ability to project forces over the longest distances, with a high degree of readiness, combat power, strategic and tactical speed, and relative autonomy

[738] IV, VI and VIII Mountain Brigades: These are organized with tactical units to operate in the mountain environment (puna, high mountains, medium and low forested mountains), against troops of similar specialty, being highly versatile to reconfigure their means and organization for the execution of various missions

[739] They can also be used as light troops in other specific environments. The 3rd and 12th Mountain Brigades are made up of tactical units highly adapted to mountain terrain, capable of carrying out operations to open or close spaces within it

[740] They can also be used as light troops in other particular environments

[741] IX, X and XI Mechanized Brigades: integrated on the basis of mechanized tactical units equipped with vehicles with armored protection and tracked and/or wheeled tracks

[742] They have the capacity to carry out operations on the plains, desert areas and eventually at the mouth of low mountains

[743] They are especially suitable for combating mechanized forces and for conquering ground objectives

[744] I and II Armored Brigades: They are basically made up of wheeled or tracked armored tactical units

[745] They have the capacity to carry out operations on the plains, desert areas and eventually at the mouth of low mountains

[746] They are especially suited to carrying out rapid, mobile and deep operations with great firepower

[747] The Task Force also includes groups that bring together elements with similar characteristics and high specificity, both from the weapons, special operations troops, and technical troops

[748] These include: Special Operations Forces, Anti-Aircraft Artillery, Engineers, Communications, and Army Aviation

[749] Argentine Medium Tank (TAM

[750] The organization of the armed forces has a common senior leadership structure, headed by the Chief of the General Staff

[751] Mountain troop

[752] The Readiness and Training Commands are tasked with planning and conducting the readiness and training of operational and support assets within the framework determined by joint military planning

DIRECTORATE OF ADMINISTRATION AND FINANCE GENERAL DIRECTORATE OF LEGAL AFFAIRS 2.2 Argentine Navy The ARA Readiness and Training Command is composed of two types of groups: the force commands for the different operational environments (sea fleet, naval aviation, marine infantry, and submarine) and the naval areas

[754] The aforementioned commands administer the forces and units under their command: surface ships, submarines, aircraft, and marine infantry units

[755] Its purpose is to be able to provide and sustain the resources required for operational naval training, the composition of the required joint or joint-combined forces, and the execution of naval operations ordered by the EMCO Operational Command

[756] Naval areas are responsible for providing logistical support from their bases to operational assets based within their jurisdictions or carrying out operations in their areas of responsibility

[757] Some naval areas have permanently assigned resources appropriate to the area

[758] Force Commands The Fleet Command is responsible for integrated naval training

[759] It also has attached naval and air infantry units

[760] It is composed of: - A division of destroyers for anti-surface, anti-submarine, anti-missile defense and electronic warfare actions

[761] A division of corvettes for sea control tasks and anti-surface, anti-submarine, missile defense, and electronic warfare actions

[762] The Naval Amphibious and Logistics Command is responsible for planning and executing amphibious operations, air defense tasks, and logistical support for the Naval Fleet

[763] The Naval Aviation Command is composed of: Naval Air Force No. 1, with its main headquarters at the Punta Indio Naval Air Base (Buenos Aires province, Punta Indio District

[764] Composed of a maritime surveillance squadron, a training and improvement unit, and a mobile logistics support squadron with its logistics support workshop, based at the Ezeiza Naval Air Station

[765] Naval Air Force No. 2, based at the Comandante Espora Naval Air Base (Buenos Aires province, Bahía Blanca

[766] It houses the combat units that make up the Naval Air Group of the Fleet: an attack squadron; a reconnaissance and anti-submarine warfare squadron; and two helicopter squadrons, one for reconnaissance and attack and the other for anti-submarine warfare and maritime rescue

[767] Naval Air Force No. 3, based at the Almirante Zar Naval Air Base (Chubut province, Trelew

[768] It has a reconnaissance and logistical support squadron

[769] The Río Grande Naval Air Base and the Ushuaia Naval Air Station (both in the province of Tierra del Fuego, Antarctica and the South Atlantic islands) are also dependent on it as territorial deployment points for naval aviation

[770] The Marine Infantry Command is made up of: - Marine Infantry Force of the Sea Fleet: composed of the 2nd Marine Infantry Battalion, the Command and Logistics Support Battalion, the Amphibious Vehicle Battalion, the Field Artillery Battalion, the Anti-Aircraft Artillery Battalion, the Communications Battalion, the Amphibious Command Group and the Amphibious Engineer Company

[771] Southern Marine Infantry Force (Tierra del Fuego): composed of the 4th and 5th Marine Infantry Battalions, assigned to operations in cold zones and specific terrains of the region, and, additionally, a naval detachment

[772] Marine Infantry Battalion No. 3 (Zárate, Paraná de las Palmas River, Buenos Aires Province): assigned to river and riverine operations

[773] Baterías Marine Infantry Base (Punta Alta, Bahía Blanca): which provides fixed logistical support to the Marine Infantry Training and Evaluation Command and operational units, both from the ARA and from other forces operating in the area for training purposes

[774] The Submarine Force Command (Mar del Plata): is comprised of submarine units with anti-surface, antisubmarine, coastal reconnaissance, intelligence gathering, and tactical diver projection capabilities, as well as amphibious commands

[775] River Naval Areas: based in the city of Zárate, it is the headquarters of the River Squadron composed of surface units such as river patrol boats, multipurpose vessels and a patrol boat

[776] Atlántica: based in the city of Mar del Plata, it is responsible for the Maritime Patrol Division, composed of surface units of the corvette and aviso types

[777] Austral: based in the city of Ushuaia, it commands the Fast Boat Group, composed of fast boats, patrol boats, and an A.T.A.-type notice

[778] The Naval Operations Command is completed by the Naval Transport Command, composed of a tanker and transport vessels

[779] CHIEF OF THE GENERAL STAFF OF THE AIR FORCE INSPECTORATE GENERAL SECRETARIAT ASSISTANT SECRETARIAT HEADQUARTERS DEPUTY CHIEF OF THE GENERAL STAFF OF THE AIR FORCE TRAINING AND READINESS COMMAND General Directorate of Organization and Doctrine General Directorate of Intelligence General Directorate of Research and Development General Directorate of Communications and Information Technology General Directorate of Education General Directorate of Health General Directorate of Material General Directorate of Quartermaster General Directorate of State Airlines PREVAC Directorate Directorate of Land Security and Defense General Directorate of Aeronautical Service General Directorate of Military Airworthiness General Directorate of Personnel and Welfare 1st Air Brigade 2nd Air Brigade 3rd Air Brigade 4th Air Brigade 6th Air Brigade 7th Air Brigade 9th Air Brigade 5th Air Brigade CONTRACTING EVALUATION COMMITTEE GENERAL DIRECTORATE OF PLANS, PROGRAMS AND BUDGET DIRECTORATE GENERAL OF ADMINISTRATION AND FINANCE GENERAL DIRECTORATE OF LEGAL AFFAIRS GENERAL DIRECTORATE OF EDUCATION GENERAL DIRECTORATE OF AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL PERSONNEL OFFICE 2.3 Argentine Air Force The Argentine Air Force (FAA) provides resources for carrying out operations in the strategic, aerospace defense, tactical transport and special areas

[780] The FAA's Readiness and Training Command is comprised of eight air brigades and three air bases, organized into technical support and logistical support groups or squadrons

[781] It also includes an electronic warfare group

[782] The General Directorate of Material, for its part, constitutes the technical and logistical support of the FAA

[783] Their role is to plan and manage the logistics of institutional material

[784] It is made up of four units: Río IV Material Area (Córdoba province): major maintenance planning, research and development, repair and manufacturing of aeronautical material

[785] Quilmes Material Area (Buenos Aires province): repair and maintenance of airplanes and helicopters (engines, propellers, instruments, accessories and electronic equipment), and of automobiles and heavy vehicles

[786] Palomar Logistics Area (Buenos Aires province): reception and delivery of FAA supply materials (including spare parts for aircraft, engines, electronic and communications systems, and personal equipment for personnel

[787] Logistics Area Córdoba (province of Córdoba): control and monitoring of the work carried out by the Argentine Aircraft Factory Brigadier San Martín (FAdeA

[788] Its routes in 2014 State Airlines (LADE) is the only state air transport agency exclusively for development, and it depends on the FAA

[789] It utilizes its expertise in the areas of aeronautics, maintenance, operational and administrative support for its personnel and its fleet of transport aircraft, providing a public and community service that links densely populated centers with remote towns in our territory lacking rapid and regular means of communication, thus creating new air routes and contributing to regional promotion and the presence of the national State in remote areas

[790] LADE offers scheduled passenger flights with Fokker F-28, Saab SF-340, and DHC-6 Twin Otter aircraft, and non-scheduled passenger and cargo flights with C-130 Hercules aircraft

[791] All services are provided in accordance with the allocation of resources and the guidelines of the national government

[807] Consequently, the length of service for Subordinate Military Personnel in active service was set at THIRTY SIX years of simple military service completed, so that after THIRTY FIVE years, SIX months and ONE day, the mandatory retirement process begins, in order to maintain a tight staff

[808] Material means 4.1 Argentine Army The Army is composed of command elements, combat elements and logistical support elements

[809] Regarding command elements, it has materials that facilitate the management of the eventual Land Component Command, the Army Division Commands, the Rapid Deployment Force, as well as the Brigade Commands

[810] Within the combat elements, the Army's tactical units are equipped with material means for the various functions, according to the following classification: - The basic combat elements, with infantry and cavalry with means suitable for direct combat

[811] Special operations elements (commandos, mountain and forest hunters, army divers, and special forces) with highly specialized and technologically advanced equipment

[812] Field artillery and anti-aircraft artillery fire support elements with surface-to-surface and surface-to-air fire support means

[813] Combat support elements with means that have technical and tactical capabilities that allow them to facilitate, through the execution of specific tasks related to such capabilities, the action of the basic combat elements, increasing their combat power

[814] They are comprised of: the engineering branch, with the means to facilitate its own mobility, restrict the adversary's mobility, and protect personnel and resources; the communications branch, with the means to facilitate its own communications and hinder the adversary's; the technical intelligence troops, with the necessary materials to produce strategic, tactical, and technical intelligence; and the army aviation, with the necessary materials to carry out airmobile operations, through specific combat, combat support, and logistical functions, as well as other general functions

[815] Likewise, logistical support elements for personnel, material, and finances (arsenals, quartermaster, health, veterinary, and justice, among others) are available to support the logistics of all forces

[816] These are executed with materials that allow for the supply of goods, their maintenance, the transportation of personnel and cargo, the execution of temporary and/or permanent constructions, the preservation and recovery of personnel health, and the supply and maintenance of livestock, among the most significant

[818] Argentine Navy The extent and diversity of the Argentine maritime and river spaces in which the ARA fulfills its surveillance and control responsibilities require that naval assets be capable of carrying out a wide range of operations

[819] The objective is the protection of the nation's vital interests, both at sea and on land, and this implies the eventual need to use force from the sea to territories under national jurisdiction

[820] Integrated naval power involves the coordination of all naval, air, and marine components necessary to meet the demands of a military conflict at sea

[821] Within this framework, the different platforms may be oriented to perform specific tasks, but the whole constitutes a balanced naval force suitable for: - Command and control

[822] Anti-surface, anti-aircraft and anti-submarine defense

[823] Tactical operations of attack, exploration and air defense

[824] Amphibious operations, with limited objectives and on poorly defended coasts

[825] Submarine attack operations

[826] Coastal and port defense operations based on mining and anti-mine capabilities

[827] Mobile logistics support (air and water

[868] Surveillance and reconnaissance operations in national airspace 1.1 Joint Task Force for Aerospace Control “Fortín II” President Cristina Fernández de Kirchner launched Operation Escudo Norte with the aim of increasing surveillance and control of land, river and airspace under national jurisdiction on the country’s northwest and northeast borders

[869] By Decree 1.091/11 (Article 5), the Ministry of Defense was instructed to adopt, within its jurisdiction, all necessary administrative, operational, and logistical measures to intensify surveillance and control of areas under national jurisdiction by the armed forces, collaborating in this case with the Ministry of Security

[870] Within this framework, Resolution MD 590/11 established Operation Fortín II and instructed the Joint Chiefs of Staff of the Armed Forces to increase aerospace surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities on the northern border

[871] Military operations are activities that employ the means of the military instrument to accomplish the missions assigned to it

[872] Operations can be carried out both within the national territory, within the framework of the national defense policy and other provisions of the National Executive Branch, and abroad, based on agreements reached with the United Nations or for humanitarian assistance and support to communities in friendly countries

[873] Types of military operations according to participating means Participation Participation of means Of an armed force Of two or more armed forces Participation of forces from the same country Specific operation Joint operation Participation of two or more countries Specific and combined operation Joint and combined operation For this purpose, the Joint Task Force for Aerospace Control “Fortín II” was created

[874] The armed forces, with the coordination and direction of the Joint Chiefs of Staff's Operational Command, deployed additional resources to increase radar coverage and interception capability in the airspace of the Northern Border

[875] The deployed resources include radars and their auxiliary equipment, aerial resources, ground mobility resources, and the personnel required for continuous operations

[876] The specific radar locations cover the border and the main approach routes for irregular air traffic identified by the National Gendarmerie

[877] In 2011, an AN-FPS 113/90 radar and the Posadas Aerospace Control Station were installed at Posadas Airport, Misiones province

[878] Later, in 2014, the first domestically manufactured radar, RPA3D LRA (Argentine Primary 3D Long-Range Radar), was installed in the town of Las Lomitas, Formosa province, and the Las Lomitas Aerospace Surveillance Station was created

[879] Civil works were also carried out for the installation of a radar tower, and an RPA radar was installed in Ingeniero Juárez, Formosa province

[880] Civil works have begun to reinforce and adapt the radar tower that will be installed at the Aerospace Surveillance and Control Directorate

[881] Likewise, work on installing a radar in Pirané, Formosa province, is scheduled to begin in

[882] It is also worth noting that the first TPS radar upgraded to MTPS began operational service. It was used operationally at the Summit of Heads of State of MERCOSUR and Associated States held in the city of Paraná, Entre Ríos province, in December

[883] The ground component of the Joint Task Force for Aerospace Control "Fortín II" has as its main activity patrolling the assigned area of responsibility

[884] These tasks materialize the operational activities of ground surveillance and control

[885] All information obtained and transmitted as a result of the operation of the Radar Groups falls within the concept of "neutral data" established in the current legal framework (Joint Resolution 821/2011 "Interministerial Protocol for the Transfer of Neutral Data on Land Movements to the Security Forces" and the orders and directives issued by the different levels of command

[886] The surveillance and control of areas under national jurisdiction contribute to the fulfillment of the primary mission, as they are intended to guarantee the sovereignty, independence, self-determination, territorial integrity of the Nation, and the life and liberty of its inhabitants, as vital interests to be preserved by the National Defense System

[887] The legal basis is found in Article 2 of Law 23,554 on National Defense, as regulated by Decree 727/06 and Decree

[888] They may also have contributing side effects on the primary tasks and responsibilities of other state agencies such as security forces and police forces

[889] Deployment in Defense Zones: collaboration in the protection of Presidential Summits Collaboration and support to the security system for the protection of presidential summits is one of the activities assigned to the military instrument

[890] The Argentine defense system, through the Joint Chiefs of Staff, deployed various weapons systems for the presidential summits held across the country

[891] In the period 2011-2014, the armed forces' resources responded to the demands of the following summits: XLIII MERCOSUR Summit (Mendoza, June 2012): a TPS 43E radar, four A4 AR Fightinghawk aircraft, four IA-58 Pucará aircraft and four IA-63 Pampa aircraft were deployed

[892] • XLVII MERCOSUR Presidential Summit (Paraná, December 2014): Operations Escudo Norte and Fortín II represent the coordination between the Ministry of Defense and its armed forces and the Ministry of Security and its security forces

[893] A TPS 43 E radar, three A4-AR Fightinghawk aircraft, three IA-58 Pucará aircraft, a Bell-212 helicopter and a Bell UH-1H helicopter were deployed. Aerospace Command Taking into account the need to maintain the concept of indivisibility of airspace, the importance of protecting national sovereignty in this area and considering that it is an activity that is developed from peace, the MINDEF, through Resolution 230/14, created the Aerospace Command within the scope of the EMCO

[894] The agency is responsible for exercising command over surveillance and control operations in airspace under national jurisdiction and declared of interest by the National Executive Branch

[895] It is led by a senior FAA officer

[896] The mission of this command is to exercise leadership over the fulfillment of its responsibilities on a permanent basis and in accordance with the guidelines established by the National Defense Planning Cycle and its Subordinate Military Strategic Planning, within the framework of the primary and complementary missions of the military instrument

[897] The basis of the integrity and indivisibility of the aerospace field is its three-dimensionality, which knows no geographical boundaries but rather the continuity of its three-dimensional volume (altitude, longitude and distance), thus differentiating itself from the limits that restrict surface forces

[898] Conceptually and operationally, airspace is an indivisible block in which, through different instruments, the State exercises its sovereign rights during peace and denies its use in periods of crisis or conflict, deterring, nullifying, neutralizing, attenuating or minimizing the effects of the aggressor, including the execution and advice on passive aerospace defense actions and permanent assistance to civil protection and defense agencies

[899] Integrated aerospace defense helps ensure the nation's vital interests based on new technologies and capabilities derived from aerospace weapons systems, while also controlling the pace of armed confrontations, increasing the likelihood of success and limiting socioeconomic and military damage

[900] The objective of comprehensive airspace management is to regulate and regulate its use, increasing operational effectiveness and ensuring that all civilian and military users can operate in a coordinated, integrated, and effective manner, with maximum safety, minimal mutual interference, and the fewest possible restrictions. This allows for dynamic adaptation to unforeseen changes in the situation through a fluid exchange of information between the various interested agencies at the national and international levels, as well as ensuring joint and combined interoperability

[901] In this scenario, the FAA (Federal Aviation Administration), as an integral part of the military instrument of national defense and responsible executor of the National Aerospace Surveillance System, is empowered to perform all the tasks required for the design, development, implementation, and subsequent maintenance of the administration of national airspace, allowing the Aerospace Command to exercise the comprehensive aerospace defense of the Nation

[902] Sea control and maritime patrol operations The Operational Command has resources provided by the ARA assigned to two naval areas to carry out sea control and maritime patrol tasks

[903] The ARA Training and Readiness Command assigns functions to the Atlantic Naval Area and the Southern Naval Area, which carry out operations aimed at fulfilling the assigned mission

[904] The Atlantic Naval Area was created in March 2000 with the task of optimizing sea control functions and understanding all matters related to maritime interests

[905] Its area of responsibility extends from Cape San Antonio, in the province of Buenos Aires, to the city of Comodoro Rivadavia, in the province of Chubut

[906] Its command is based at the Mar del Plata Naval Base

[907] The Maritime Patrol Division, whose units include the corvettes ARA "Drummond," ARA "Guerrico," and ARA "Granville," the avisos ARA "Gurruchaga" and ARA "Suboficial Castillo," the patrol boat ARA "Punta Mogotes," the Comodoro Rivadavia Naval Detachment, and the Puerto Madryn Naval Station, are under this area

[908] The Southern Naval Area Command was created on December

[909] The geographic area of its jurisdiction includes the southernmost tip of the Argentine mainland, the Argentine sector of Tierra del Fuego Island and the Isla de los Estados, as well as the vast southern maritime spaces that reach the 60th parallel south. Its natural seat is the Naval Base near the city of Ushuaia

[910] The importance of the Southern Naval Area's strategic geographic location is evident in the tasks it performs, such as safeguarding the bioceanic passages and Argentina's expansion to Antarctica

[911] To accomplish these goals, the Southern Naval Area Command comprises a Fast Boat Group, the Ushuaia Naval Hospital, the Naval Quartermaster, the Ushuaia and Río Grande naval air bases, the Puerto Deseado Naval Station, and the Southern Marine Infantry Force
