[914] Logistical support operations for Antarctic activities The Ministry of Defense contributes to the National Antarctic Policy through a Joint Antarctic Command (COCOANTAR) dependent on the Operational Command

[915] This Joint Command is responsible for ensuring support for the "Annual Antarctic Scientific, Technical, and Services Plan," developed by the National Antarctic Directorate under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Worship

[916] It must also guarantee the logistics and operation of the national Antarctic bases in support of the national and international scientific community and the provision of services and commitments assumed by the National State

[917] It assumes all logistical and support tasks for the scientific, technical, and service activities to be carried out during the summer campaign, and those to be sustained permanently or scheduled for outside the summer period

[918] Every year, COCOANTAR plans and executes the replacement and resupply of permanent and temporary bases

[919] Furthermore, during each of the 2013/2014 and 2014/2015 Antarctic Summer Campaigns, more than 1,500 armed forces personnel were mobilized and different logistical means were deployed - such as Mi-17 and Bell-212 helicopters, C-130 Hercules and Twin Otter aircraft, and ARA ships - to ensure the supply of the thirteen bases in a timely manner

[920] There are scientific and military personnel at all Argentine bases

[921] With logistical support from armed forces personnel, the scientific team is the foundation of Argentina's presence in Antarctica

[922] Following the success of the 2013/2014 and 2014/2015 CAVs, Argentina continues to maintain an active presence in Antarctica, defending its national strategic interests and contributing to the maintenance of a peaceful zone through respect for international agreements

[923] Mil-Mi 17 transport helicopter providing logistical support to Antarctic activities

[924] The presence of the Argentine Republic in Antarctica has been consolidated through 13 bases, 6 permanent (Orcadas, Marambio, Carlini, Esperanza, San Martín and Belgrano II) and 7 temporary (Brown, Matienzo, Primavera, Cámara, Melchior, Decepción and Petrel

[925] Antarctic Defense System Activities • Logistics support and infrastructure development activities: operation of the Matienzo base; development of a new alternative energy system based on hydrogen storage at the Esperanza base; relocation of facilities to the Belgrano II base; construction of infrastructure for educational and scientific activities (Esperanza and Carlini bases

[926] • Contribution to scientific activities: supply flights, relief flights, and personnel redistribution to and between Argentine Antarctic bases and, if necessary, those of other countries; medical evacuation, search and rescue flights; reconnaissance and support flights to other countries; transport of general and scientific cargo, personnel transfer, search and rescue, deployment and withdrawal of scientific and technical personnel using the Navy's naval and air-naval resources

[927] • Joint-combined military action: Over the last decade, agreements have been made with the Plurinational State of Bolivia and the Republic of Peru to exchange and train military personnel in Antarctic matters

[928] Argentine personnel share their experience with colleagues in neighboring countries, thus facilitating their use of Argentine bases in Antarctica

[929] In the same spirit, the Combined Antarctic Naval Patrol (PANC)—with human and material resources from the Argentine and Chilean Navies—conducts combined operations to safeguard human life at sea, control and combat pollution, and provide mutual support to address maritime emergencies in the waters surrounding the Antarctic continent

[930] Similarly, the Antarctic Land Patrol, comprised of resources from the Chilean O'Higgins base and the Argentine Esperanza base, is supported by air resources from the Marambio base

[946] The Joint Logistics Antarctic Base Petrel will be intended to ensure the logistical link between national and foreign Antarctic bases, with the ports and airports located in the Argentine South American territory

[947] Secondarily, it will have the capacity to support scientific capabilities, land, sea, and air search and rescue (SAR) operations, and activities related to Antarctic tourism

[948] The design will prioritize its use as a logistics and services hub, allowing for the eventual modernization of its specific systems as a result of technological advancement or configuration changes

[949] The base will operate year-round with fixed-wing aircraft and helicopters, weather permitting

[950] Likewise, it will have port facilities for the operation of ships and smaller vessels during the period in which glacial conditions are adequate for the polar classification of the means employed, providing the possibility of horizontal transfer of passengers and cargo between air and naval means

[957] Operations within the framework of international peace missions At the international level, Argentine Defense policy maintains its firm conviction of cooperation in defense matters as a means of building and consolidating confidence, peace and international security

[958] Within the framework of these principles, it adopts as its general objectives the contribution to efforts aimed at the extension and maintenance of international peace and security advocated by the United Nations Organization

[959] Military peacekeeping operations act as areas of international cooperation

[960] The most relevant advances made in this regard include: The “Cruz del Sur” Peace Force, which constitutes a binational military integration undertaking with the objective of promoting mutual trust, interoperability and complementarity between the armed forces of Chile and Argentina

[961] • The “Libertador Don José de San Martín” Engineering Company, which forms a Combined Binational Peruvian-Argentine Peace Force

[962] It was created to be made available to the United Nations Mission in Haiti (MINUSTAH) through a Memorandum of Understanding signed by both Ministries of Defense in October

[963] • Combined exercises in military peace operations, both military and cabinet-level

[964] • The Latin American Association of Peacekeeping Operations Training Centers (ALCOPAZ), an Argentine initiative whose purpose is to promote the standardization of a doctrine for military peacekeeping operations in the region, the establishment of a regional perspective, and the exchange of lessons learned

[965] Our country is also committed to cooperating with countries in the region by using its human and material resources in the area of humanitarian assistance

[966] Thus, in recent years it has contributed to alleviating serious situations resulting from natural disasters by channeling requests for assistance

[967] The most recent and notable examples of such aid are those provided to Haiti and Chile following the earthquakes that occurred in both countries in

[968] Latin American Association of Peace Operations Training Centers (ALCOPAZ) In 2008, ALCOPAZ was formed as a result of an Argentine initiative

[969] This entity is made up of training centers for peacekeeping missions in Latin American and Caribbean countries and is intended to promote the standardization of training and education in Peacekeeping Operations, for greater effectiveness and efficiency in the preparation of personnel serving in these operations

[970] Processing of Annual Combined Exercise Programs Argentina has traditionally conducted a series of combined exercises with different countries with the aim of strengthening bilateral and multilateral cooperation between national and foreign armed forces

[971] In this regard, we have intervened in all aspects inherent to National Law 25,880 and its regulatory decree to authorize the entry of military personnel into national territory and the departure of national forces outside of it, also supervising the execution of combined military exercises

[972] The Argentine Republic has demonstrated an active commitment to peace in Latin America through its participation in various United Nations missions in the region

[973] More than fifty years of Argentine participation in United Nations Peace Missions Our country has participated in peace missions in different parts of the world since

[974] In response to the conflict that broke out in Lebanon in June 1958, the United Nations created UNOGIL (United Nations Observation Group in Lebanon

[975] On this occasion, our country is sending a group of military observers for the first time

[976] That first mission was followed in July 1960 by ONUC (United Nations Operation in the Congo), where a group of Air Force pilots joined General Staffs and Air Transport Squadrons

[977] In 1992, under the flag of UNPROFOR (United Nations Protection Force), our country sent, for the first time, a large contingent called the "Argentine Army Battalion" to Croatia, where it was initially based

[978] The mission's main objective was to monitor the demilitarization of the assigned areas

[979] Argentina demonstrated an active commitment to peace in Latin America by participating in numerous United Nations missions in the region, and in most of the missions in the Republic of Haiti: the United Nations Mission in Haiti (MINUH) from 1993 to 1996, the United Nations Transitional Mission in Haiti (UNTMIH) from 1997, and the United Nations Civilian Police Mission in Haiti (MIPONUH) from 1997 to

[980] From 2004 to 2014, Argentina was one of the countries with the largest presence in MINUSTAH (United Nations Stabilization Mission in Haiti

[981] The largest national contingent abroad is deployed on this mission

[982] In 1993, our country joined UNFICYP (United Nations Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus) in support of the United Nations Security Council's initiative to seek solutions to the conflict in Cyprus

[983] In recent years, the Argentine Contingent has become the largest

[984] Since 1994, we have had female members of the armed forces participate in various peacekeeping operations

[985] Current defense policy is based on a firm determination to promote the effective implementation of a gender perspective in these operations, in line with UN Security Council Resolution 1325 of 2000, entitled "On Women, Peace and Security

[986] Currently, Argentina has a presence with military forces in missions under the United Nations flag in Haiti (MINUSTAH) and Cyprus (UNFICYP), as well as Military Observers in Western Sahara (MINURSO) and the Middle East (UNTSO

[987] United Nations Stabilization Mission in Haiti (MINUSTAH) MINUSTAH was created on April 30, 2004 by Resolution 1542 of the United Nations Security Council to address the complex social, political and economic situation affecting that country

[988] The pillars on which the international presence was established were to provide a safe and stable environment, guarantee respect for human rights, and support the process of democratic consolidation on the island

[989] Argentina has participated through the deployment of military personnel since the beginning of the mission, which has represented a significant challenge due to its scope and significance, considering that this was the first mission in which the country assumed full responsibility for providing logistical support through complete self-sustainment

[990] The tasks carried out by the military forces fall within the framework of deterrence—through presence—in support of the reestablishment of the rule of law and public order

[991] Likewise, protect UN personnel, facilities and equipment

[992] Regarding the provision of humanitarian assistance and facilitating access to it for the Haitian population, military personnel have coordinated cooperation between the Haitian government and the international organizations that provide it

[993] In turn, MINDEF has also participated in other cooperation initiatives with Haiti, through political, diplomatic, and technical coordination channels alongside other national government agencies

[994] By 2015, the Argentine Joint Contingent for Haiti (CCAH), made up of 561 blue helmets from the EA, the ARA and the FAA, was fully deployed

[995] The troops were deployed in the cities of Gonaïves, where the Argentine Joint Battalion is located, and Port-au-Prince, where the Field Hospital and the Air Unit composed of FAA Bell 212 helicopters operate

[996] United Nations Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus (UNFICYP) UNFICYP is the main mission in terms of the number of Argentine troops deployed and was created in 1964 by UN Security Council Resolution

[997] The conflict between Greek Cypriots based in the south and Turkish Cypriots based in the north of the Mediterranean island in 1974 determined the need to establish a buffer zone in which UNFICYP is tasked with maintaining peace and stability

[998] Our country's participation there began in 1993 with the deployment of the Argentine Task Force, whose main objective is to prevent the resumption of fighting between the Cypriot National Guard and the Turkish Army by verifying the ceasefire and respecting the resolutions of the United Nations Security Council

[999] In the second half of 2014, the Argentine Task Force 44 (FTA 44), made up of 249 personnel (14 of them women) from the Army, Navy, Air Force and South American military personnel (one from Brazil, 14 from Chile and 13 from Paraguay), was deployed on this mission

[1000] Also in Cyprus is the UNFIGHT Air Unit, composed of around thirty FAA personnel and their Bell 212 and Hughes 500 D helicopters. 5.4 United Nations Truce Supervision Organization (UNTSO) Among the ongoing missions, UNTSO is the oldest with national participation

[1001] Created in May 1948 by the UN Security Council through Resolution 50, its purpose was to call for a cessation of hostilities in Palestine through a group of military observers assisting the UN mediator who was to monitor and supervise the truce between the Arab states and Israel

[1002] Beginning in 1969, Argentina participated with military observers deployed in Jerusalem, the Golan Heights, and the Suez Canal

[1003] This observation mission is unique in that it is located above other missions with a presence in five Middle Eastern countries: Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Lebanon, and the Syrian Arab Republic

[1004] The Mission in Western Sahara was established in April 1991 by UN Security Council Resolution 690, and is located in the former Spanish Sahara

[1005] This territory, following Spain's withdrawal in 1976, is currently almost entirely occupied by Morocco, although Moroccan sovereignty over it is not recognized by the United Nations and is rejected by the Polisario Front independence movement

[1006] Since its establishment, MINURSO has been mandated to ensure a transitional period for the preparation of the referendum in which the Sahrawis will decide between independence or integration into Morocco

[1007] To this end, rounds of negotiations have been held between the parties to the conflict for more than two decades

[1008] Argentine participation began in 1991, with the deployment of military personnel to the region to carry out observation tasks to separate opposing forces

[1010] Training and capacity building for peace: the contribution of the Argentine Joint Training Center for Peace Operations (CAECOPAZ) CAECOPAZ was created in 1995, constituting the first joint training center for peace operations on the continent

[1011] The center offers an average of nearly 40 international courses annually, which have been attended by personnel from nearly 30 nations over the years

[1012] The importance of training in peacekeeping operations is also reflected in the large number of Argentine instructors who teach in countries such as Brazil, Canada, Chile, France, Germany, Guatemala, India, Mali, and the United States

[1013] Additionally, as part of an exchange policy, this center has visiting instructors from those same countries, as well as Belgium and Bolivia, with the exception of Guatemala and Mali

[1014] CAECOPAZ is part of the Latin American Association of Peace Operations Training Centers (ALCOPAZ), an association promoted by Argentina as an entity that brings together and connects the various training centers with similar objectives in the region, in accordance with UN standards and with a view to establishing a regional perspective on peace operations and the regional exchange of experiences

[1015] Similarly, the Argentine center for this field has been a founding member of the International Association of Peacekeeping Training Centers (IAPTC) since 1995, the first in the region with a distinguished track record and having held the presidency of the aforementioned association in

[1016] Drawing on its experience, production, doctrine development, and relationships with other centers worldwide and with the United Nations itself, all enriched by specific courses in addition to its current curriculum, the Argentine MINDEF is working to consolidate CAECOPAZ as the first Regional Center for Advanced Training in Peacekeeping Operations. That is, taking a qualitative leap by transforming it into a regional center for higher and specialized education that does not replace national centers but rather complements them

[1017] Gender Perspective in the Framework of Peace Operations The scope of military performance represented by United Nations Peace Missions has enabled the recognition and full exercise of equal professional rights for women

[1018] The Argentine Republic has implemented several initiatives aimed at recognizing the gender perspective in the area of national defense, including the United Nations "Action Plan for the Implementation of the Gender Perspective in the Framework of Peacekeeping Operations," approved in October 2008 through MD Resolutions 1,226 and

[1019] An International Seminar on Gender in Peacekeeping Operations was held in September 2011, an unprecedented initiative in the region

[1020] Joint Binational Forces for Peace Combined Joint Peace Force “Cruz del Sur” Given the agreements reached between the governments of Chile and Argentina through their Ministries of Defense – Memorandum of Understanding that entered into force on January 1, 2007 – the Peace Force “Cruz del Sur” was created with the mission of serving in United Nations Peace Operations

[1021] This unprecedented alliance made it possible to establish a joint and combined peacekeeping force, involving personnel and resources from the three armed forces of both countries

[1022] This character applies to all components of the “Southern Cross”: land, naval, and air forces, military hospital, and engineering corps

[1023] As stated in Law 26.560 of 2009, the purpose of the FPCC “Cruz del Sur” is to act in Peace Operations at the request of the UN, and may

[1024] Provide a UN presence in a crisis area by mediating a Security Council resolution. Prevent escalation of violence. Assist, monitor, or facilitate a ceasefire. Secure an area that allows for the subsequent deployment of other UN forces

[1025] • Provide “safe areas” for individuals and groups whose lives are at risk due to the conflict

[1026] • Ensure humanitarian emergency aid operations

[1027] • Collaborate on specific activities that require strengthening the security of a mission in progress

[1028] Combined Engineer Company “Libertador don José de San Martín” This company is a Peruvian-Argentine binational peacekeeping force created in 2008 to be made available to the United Nations Mission in Haiti

[1029] Their specific capabilities and profiles were defined according to the specific conditions of the Haitian situation to facilitate the collection, purification, and distribution of water in densely populated areas; improve road and housing infrastructure in the most vulnerable areas; provide public schools and medical centers for the Haitian people, among other urgent needs identified in the Caribbean nation

[1030] The earthquake that struck Haiti in January 2010 further highlighted the need for and use of this South American binational instrument to contribute to peace and reconstruction

[1031] Argentine and Chilean military personnel in operation

[1032] Combined Joint Peacekeeping Force “Southern Cross”

[1033] Participation in operations to support the national or international community in the event of natural disasters is a subsidiary mission of the Argentine military instrument

[1034] At the national level, its armed forces can respond to adverse events of natural or man-made origin once the resources of the federal system are deemed insufficient, and they act in the response, mitigation, and reconstruction stages

[1035] At the international level, our country is committed to cooperating with countries in the region in the area of humanitarian assistance, employing human and material resources

[1036] In recent years, it has contributed to alleviating serious situations resulting from natural disasters by expeditiously processing requests for assistance and authorizing the deployment of troops to provide that aid

[1037] The most notable examples are the cases of Haiti and Chile in 2010 due to the earthquakes that occurred in both countries

[1038] The armed forces' participation in civil protection operations includes fire management in large fires, operations in response to natural disasters (floods, volcanic emergencies, tornadoes), and health emergencies

[1039] Some examples of these actions carried out between 2011 and 2014 at a purely national level are the assistance provided in the province of Neuquén in response to the seismic activity of the Puyehue and Copahue volcanoes, the assistance provided during the floods in the provinces of Buenos Aires and Chubut, the numerous operations to search for shipwrecked people and aerial evacuations of personnel from fishing vessels and coastal cleanups, all carried out with Navy personnel and resources, and the rescues of people from explosions (Santa Fe province, Rosario) or collapses (collapse of the internal structure of a supermarket in the city of Neuquén), the last two carried out by EA personnel

[1040] Among the similar actions carried out at the international level, it is worth mentioning the rescue operation carried out in May 2013 by personnel from the Carlini Base in Antarctica to assist the fishing vessel "Betanazos", belonging to the company Antartic Sea Fisheries (under the Chilean flag), whose propulsion and command system suffered a breakdown that caused it to be left without propulsion near the coast, having to endure storms with winds of up to 180 kilometers per hour

[1041] Another notable activity was the collaboration in the search for the Argentine sailboat Tunante II, which disappeared in August 2014 in the Atlantic Ocean off the southern coast of Brazil

[1042] In April 2014, following forest fires near the Chilean city of Valparaíso, FAA SAAB 340 aircraft based in Comodoro Rivadavia, Chubut, along with their respective personnel, were made available to the authorities of the Republic of Chile to transport firefighters and brigade members

[1043] Finally, it is worth mentioning the logistical support provided to the organization of the international Dakar Rally, which took place between January 3 and 14 in Argentina, Bolivia, and Chile

[1044] The Joint Task Force "Dakar 2014" was formed with personnel and resources from the FAA and the EA

[1045] Military exercises are significant activities in both the defense policy and the international relations policy of each country

[1046] Specific and joint exercises of the Argentine Armed Forces promote the increase in the operational capabilities of the national military instrument, and combined exercises contribute to the increase and consolidation of mutual trust among the participating states

[1047] CHAPTER IX MILITARY EXERCISES

[1048] Within the framework of training, military exercises are activities developed through the application of techniques, skills, and abilities to increase, verify, and consolidate the level of acquired capabilities

[1049] The exercises carried out by the Argentine armed forces in recent years are classified, depending on whether or not they involve the use of operational capabilities, as desk exercises or simulation exercises and field exercises

[1050] In turn, ground forces can be defined as specific, joint or combined depending on the composition and origin of the forces involved

[1051] Regarding joint military exercises, the prioritization criteria and general guidance relate to: - Achieving, maintaining, and consolidating optimal levels of training and operational readiness to enable the effective fulfillment of the main mission and complementary missions of the military instrument

[1052] Optimization of joint action standards, joint employment doctrine, and operational integration of armed forces capabilities, as well as planning, conducting, and executing operations

[1053] Prevalence of those exercises in which the necessary resources for their execution—already deployed on the ground—allow for their parallel use to carry out support work for the community where the exercises are conducted

[1054] Deepening and consolidating joint activities between the forces and national civilian agencies and organizations that have direct responsibility for supporting the community in disaster situations, with the goal of achieving greater levels of organizational coordination

[1055] Regarding combined military exercises (bilateral or multilateral, specific or joint), the criteria and guidelines that have guided their prioritization in recent years have been: - Promotion and strengthening of mutual trust and deepening of the levels of interoperability with other armed forces at the regional and subregional levels

[1056] Development and consolidation of skills related to the primary mission of the military instrument and participation in multilateral exercises within the framework of the collective security system (peacekeeping operations in their various forms), and further development in operations to support the national community or friendly countries in the event of catastrophes or natural disasters

[1057] Concrete increase and verification of our own capability levels and degrees of military interoperability with regional and subregional nations, and the incorporation of recently created operational codes and procedures and the promotion of the development, modernization, and consolidation of combined operational doctrine with those nations

[1058] Optimization of the capabilities required for combined activities involving planning, management, and execution of operations

[1059] Obtaining specific parameters for the design and determination of military instrument capabilities

[1060] Parameters that refer to the achievement and consolidation of minimum interoperability standards for efficient military interaction of an expanded and multilateral nature

[1061] Consolidation of codes and procedures aimed at promoting greater levels of understanding and coordination in the event of crises or contingencies

[1062] Specific military exercises are those in which the means of a single armed force participate

[1063] They are planned and executed by that single force within the framework duly defined by Joint Military Planning

[1064] From 2011 to 2014, the Argentine armed forces have conducted important exercises of this nature to maintain the specific skills required by military personnel to operate the various weapons systems they deploy

[1065] Joint military exercises Joint exercises involve personnel and material from two or more armed forces of the same country

[1066] In Argentina, joint exercises are planned, supervised, and executed under the purview of EMCO

[1067] Considering the vital importance of joint military action in fulfilling the primary mission assigned to the military, the Argentine armed forces train jointly through exercises carried out in the various geographical areas of the vast national territory

[1068] Examples of these include the exercises “Immediate Response” and “United for Defense.”

[1069] Immediate Response is a joint military training exercise aimed at completing tasks assigned under the scope of complementary missions

[1070] It consists of a training exercise in support of civil authorities in response to natural and/or man-made disasters

[1071] Specific exercise in the mountains

[1072] In 2011, this exercise was carried out in the coastal city of Caleta Olivia, in the province of Santa Cruz

[1073] personnel from the three forces participated, along with personnel from municipal and provincial agencies

[1074] Later, in 2012, the exercise was held in Posadas, capital of the province of Misiones

[1075] For five days, personnel from the Armed Forces Operational Command and 350 troops from the three branches of the armed forces participated

[1076] The joint military exercise Immediate Response 2013 took place in the province of Chaco

[1077] More than 500 members of the armed forces participated, along with provincial security forces and Civil Defense personnel, interacting with each other to train for natural disasters

[1078] During the drill, participants performed rescue and evacuation tasks, firefighting, distribution of supplies, reception of donations, and aerial cargo delivery, among other operations

[1079] The "Glacier" course is another clear example of the need for joint training to effectively operate in the diverse geographic environments of our territory

[1080] This special training—also known as PreAntarctic—enables personnel to apply procedures for air transport and supply tasks, while also acquiring knowledge applicable to survival situations in cold areas and perfecting search and rescue techniques

[1081] This promotes, in a simulated Antarctic scenario, the exchange of experiences between personnel from different forces and specialties, contributing to mutual understanding and strengthening joint military action

[1082] Specific combined exercise Viekaren

[1083] The 2014 edition of the exercise took place in September in the Caviahue-Copahue area, Neuquén province

[1084] On this occasion, AAF and AE personnel trained in the boarding and disembarking of personnel and equipment from rotary-wing aircraft in the Antarctic geographic environment

[1085] The "United for Defense" (UNIDEF) exercise has several objectives, including joint training of the three forces in the development of various amphibious, naval, land, air, infiltration, helicopter landing, and reconnaissance combat operations, among others; increasing joint operational capabilities—technical, procedural, and tactical; evaluating the interoperability and suitability of the forces' equipment for joint action; and developing greater mutual understanding of the different specificities and operational needs of each force

[1089] The 2011 exercise, held at the Puerto Belgrano Naval Base in Bahía Blanca, involved 3,815 personnel and various materials from the EA, the ARA, and the FAA

[1090] A year later, in 2012, a similar number of troops from the three forces participated in the same operation, along with material components: aircraft, ships, tanks, other ground vehicles, and communication systems

[1091] In 2013, during the month of November, the exercise took place in the so-called Battery Zone, in the same naval unit, and consisted of a Joint Task Force (Army, Navy, and Air Force) in which nearly 4,000 troops also participated in a defensive operation

[1092] UNIDEF 2014 was held at the Adalid General Training Camp in the province of Santa Cruz

[1093] Participating were AA units belonging to the XI Mechanized Infantry Brigade "Brigadier General Juan Manuel de Rosas", ships from the Sea Fleet, elements of the Marine Infantry and personnel and resources from the V Brigade of the FAA and its similar IX Brigade

[1094] Furthermore, exercises related to the main mission of the armed forces, which are carried out at the operational level by the various joint commands, are of particular importance

[1095] Among them we can name the Petrel exercise, in which a schematic campaign plan for a theater of operations is carried out

[1096] Other operational commands, such as the Territorial Command of the Interior Zone, the Joint Transportation Command, the Joint Cyber Defense Command, and the Joint Aerospace Command, are also participating in this exercise, under the criteria of simultaneous, concurrent, and recurring planning

[1097] Within the framework of what was planned for Exercise Petrel, the foundations and guidelines for Exercise Mastín emerge, which corresponds to the planning of protection operations and territorial affairs in the so-called inland zone, and Exercise Mara, which trains the strategic mobility required for maneuvers to and from the theater of operations

[1098] The Castor exercise is also being carried out with special troops, aimed at verifying interoperability and specific training in the various capabilities specific to this type of troops

[1099] In short, military exercises adhere to joint military action as a basic and essential criterion for achieving maximum operational capabilities, based on the employment of specific forces, used under a single operational leadership, with unified procedures and mutual support criteria to achieve greater efficiency and effectiveness

[1100] Combined military exercises Combined exercises involving the armed forces of two or more countries under a centralized command and with a common purpose are planned and coordinated by representatives of the participating forces and carried out under the direction of a centralized combined command

[1101] In the decisions taken during these exercises, the Argentine side acts within the framework duly defined by the Joint Military Planning

[1102] Joint-combined exercises involve personnel and material from two or more forces of one country with two or more forces from other countries

[1103] In 2014, three major exercises of this kind took place: UNASUR IV, Solidaridad, and Cruz del Sur II

[1104] The fourth edition of the UNASUR exercise was held in November in Buenos Aires, with Peacekeeping Operations (PKO) as its central theme

[1105] The purpose was to promote combined interoperability standards in planning and management with the participation of the twelve member states of the Union of South American Nations

[1106] The main aspects considered during the exercise were the structure of a PKO (Chapter VI of the UN Charter: Pacific Settlement of Disputes); the application of UN-standardized policies and procedures for PKOs; the command and control of a UN mission at the strategic military and national levels; and interoperability among participating countries

[1107] Specific-combined exercise Salitre

[1108] Argentine Air Force

[1109] The joint-combined exercise Solidarity has been conducted by Chile and Argentina since 2004. Its fundamental objective is to strengthen the integration ties between the armed forces of both countries for combined action in the event of a catastrophe, promoting the operation of a civic-military integration model in the event of an emergency of this nature

[1110] The 2014 exercise, which took place between October 13 and 17 in the Chilean region of Los Ríos, whose capital is Valdivia, involved 1,584 Chilean and 157 Argentine armed forces personnel, supported by land, naval, and air resources

[1111] It consisted of joint training on catastrophes and natural disasters to optimize the procedures agreed upon by both countries

[1112] The Chilean Joint Chiefs of Staff served as exercise director during the simulation of an earthquake and subsequent tsunami

[1113] There were land search and rescue exercises in collapsed structures, salvage work in damaged structures, sea rescue, and a demonstration of the operation of a mobile water purification plant

[1114] The armed forces of both nations collaborated with the regional Emergency Operations Committee to coordinate and direct the work of various specialized emergency and disaster response entities

[1115] Within the framework of the Combined Joint Peacekeeping Force Cruz del Sur, the joint-combined exercise Cruz del Sur II was carried out in the city of Peldehue, Chile

[1116] The exercise took place during the last half of November 2014, with the participation of 754 Chilean and 186 Argentine armed forces personnel

[1117] With the support of ground and air resources, various procedures and techniques were implemented by the peacekeeping forces deployed under UN mandate

[1118] Combined specific exercises are those in which personnel and material from a specific armed force participate and are used, along with personnel and material from one or more forces of the same nature and from one or more other countries, with the main objective of increasing mutual confidence and achieving interoperability between the forces of different nations

[1119] Within this category are, among others, the "Salitre" exercise between the region's air forces, the "Fraterno" exercise between the Argentine and Brazilian navies, and "Operation Guaraní," which brings together personnel and equipment from the Brazilian and Argentine armies

[1120] STRATEGIC PLANNING AND DEFENSE RESOURCE MANAGEMENT Within the framework of a defensive strategic positioning and attitude, the military strategic planning of the Argentine Republic has been oriented towards providing the country with a modern military instrument capable of executing the full range of operations that most effectively ensure the fulfillment of the missions assigned to national Defense

[1121] CHAPTER X THE NATIONAL DEFENSE PLANNING CYCLE The progressive configuration of the South American region as a zone of peace, the increase in cooperation in matters of Defense and the consolidation of various measures of mutual trust, have led the Argentine Republic to suppress the historical hypotheses of military conflict with the countries of its immediate geographical environment that constituted the organizing criterion of military strategic planning in past decades

[1122] Within the framework of a defensive strategic positioning and attitude, military strategic planning has been oriented, since the sanction of Decree 1,729/2007 on the "National Defense Planning Cycle," to provide the country with a modern military instrument that will allow the national State to confront an increasingly uncertain and complex international scenario

[1123] Based on the principle of civilian governance of defense, this regulatory instrument prescribes increasingly sophisticated intervention against threats that may affect the vital interests of the Argentine Republic

[1124] Consequently, the National Defense Planning Cycle allows for the rational design of the military instrument necessary to autonomously execute the full range of operations required by all generic forms of aggression manifested in conventional war conflicts of external origin generated by state actors

[1125] Following the enactment of the aforementioned decree that created it, the first National Defense Planning Cycle was undertaken, directed entirely by the political power

[1126] It began with the issuance of the first National Defense Policy Directive (DPDN) through Decree

[1127] In it, for the first time in the country’s democratic history, the State's civilian leadership fully expressed its appreciation of the global and regional defense scenario, and the strategic conception and positioning, clearly defining the main mission and the complementary missions of the military instrument of national defense, as well as the actions that must be carried out to fulfill them in accordance with the provisions of sections 12 and 14 of article 99 of the National Constitution

[1128] This 2009 directive marked the beginning of the first National Defense Planning Cycle, launching military strategic planning itself

[1129] Based on the National Strategic Level political guidelines established in the DPDN, the EMCO developed the force planning

[1130] To this end, the EMCO initially formulated the Directive for the Development of Military Strategic Planning (DEPEM), which, after receiving ministerial approval, became a guiding document between the DPDN and military strategic planning

[1131] Later, at the military strategic level, the Planning Cycle materialized in a sequence of three documents: 1) The Military Strategic Assessment and Resolution (AREMIL

[1132] The Military Strategic Directive (DEMIL

[1133] Short, medium and long term military plans

[1134] Based on the Medium-Term Military Plan, the EMCO developed the Military Capabilities Project (PROCAMIL), which consolidated the "desirable" model of forces that aspires to fully fulfill the mission assigned to the nation's military instrument

[1135] In a next stage, and using PROCAMIL as an input, MINDEF developed the Military Capabilities Plan (PLANCAMIL

[1136] This document outlined the "possible" and "necessary" force model for all components of the military instrument: material, infrastructure, human resources, information, logistics, training, doctrine, and organization (MIRILADO

[1137] The first National Defense Planning Cycle was completed with the corresponding supervision stage through two bodies: a military strategic supervision—carried out by the EMCO—and a ministerial supervision

[1138] Thus, the procedure to establish the first National Defense Planning Cycle concluded in 2011 with the approval of PLANCAMIL, thus materializing the possible and necessary military instrument to fulfill the main mission assigned through the development of military capabilities that allow, in the medium term – from four to twenty years (2012-2032), to produce the desired military effects against potential external military state threats

[1139] In turn, PLANCAMIL is the guiding input of the Comprehensive Defense Investment Management System (SIGIDII), approved by Resolution MD 626/2007, which integrates both public investment projects in the sector and those specifically for military purposes

[1140] Thus, PLANCAMIL established, from a technical military perspective, the model that most adequately embodies the conception and paradigm of the Nation's military instrument, which over the course of two and a half decades had been defined by the legal system and by the determinations and provisions of the National Executive Branch, without any rational procedure conducted by the civilian branch having intervened at that time

[1141] In this regard, the jurisdiction's planning process identified and formulated, in PLANCAMIL, the model of military instrument necessary and possible for the Argentine Republic that most effectively ensures the fulfillment of the missions assigned to national defense

[1142] The necessary condition of said model of military instrument lies in that NATIONAL DEFENSE POLICY DIRECTIVE (DPDN) Diagnosis and assessment of the global and regional defense scenario Conception and strategic positioning in matters of Defense Guidelines for the implementation of the Defense policy and the Military policy Defense planning cycle MINDEF: Ministry of Defense EMCO: Joint Staff Determines / Evaluates Formulates / Elevates Source: Ministry of Defense

[1149] Defense Resource Planning System (SIPRED) Based on the experience accumulated after the creation of tools aimed at optimizing the use of resources, SIPRED was created in 2011, which defines the main normative and procedural axes of the implementation of the Planning, Programming, Budget and Execution System (S-3PE) through Resolution MD

[1150] Comprehensive Defense Investment Management System (SIGID) The SIGID summarizes the set of principles, standards, and procedures that regulate the planning, execution, and evaluation processes of investments in the sector

[1151] Its main annual product is the Defense Investment Plan (PIDEF), which regulates the financing for the period

[1152] Currently, the SIGID is undergoing a review and update process, aimed at promoting the formation of structures responsible for the leadership, management, and participation in activities arising from the respective stages of the SIGID

[1153] Likewise, regulations related to the Defense Resource Planning System, the Military Capabilities Plan, and experience in investment management are incorporated

[1154] Additionally, work began to review and deepen the methodology used to evaluate projects within the jurisdiction

[1155] The revised proposals from both bodies are currently being evaluated by MINDEF authorities prior to their approval

[1156] Armed Forces Maintenance Capabilities System (SICAMAN II) This system operationally links the material maintenance infrastructures of each of the three armed forces

[1157] In this way, we seek to optimize the use of total installed capacity in terms of human and technological resources, as well as resources and facilities

[1158] SICAMAN II promotes the provision of services among the armed forces that are, a priori, less expensive than those available on the commercial market

[1159] This system promotes the integration of the armed forces' maintenance capabilities, facilitates their joint use, and helps strengthen those capabilities that enable the maintenance of common systems

[1160] Its implementation has allowed the three forces to perform maintenance and recovery tasks at each other's facilities, generating a growing process of synergistic use of such capabilities

[1161] Likewise, as a result of the system’s evolution and in order to expand its reach, the Naval Hydrography Service, the Institute of Scientific and Technical Research for Defense (CITEDEF), the National Meteorological Service, Military Manufacturing, the National Geographic Institute, the Argentine Aircraft Factory (FAdeA), and the Argentine Naval Industrial Complex (CINAR) have joined the system as service providers

[1164] CHAPTER XI THE MANAGEMENT OF NATIONAL DEFENSE RESOURCES In order to deepen the optimization of the Defense resource management system, progress was made in consolidating the tools and systems created to maximize the generation and maintenance of military capabilities that are determined by their strategic planning

[1165] To this end, a series of measures were implemented to achieve the articulation of an integrated resource management system, enabling the transformation of military capabilities into infrastructure, materials, and human resources in an effective, efficient, and transparent manner

[1166] Defense Airworthiness System (SADEF) This system aims to standardize the principles and procedures that govern the common certification and maintenance standards applicable to aircraft in the armed forces, increasing their operational safety

[1167] The Military Airworthiness Regulation (RAM) – Resolution MD 18/2007 and EMC Joint Publication PC 14-05 – constitutes the normative axis of the SADEF and is regulated by the control bodies in the Ministry of Defense, in the Joint Staff and the Superior Airworthiness Regulation Bodies (OSRA) in each force and executed by the Superior Logistics Maintenance Bodies (OSLM) and the Technical Aeronautical Maintenance Bodies (OTMA) created for such purposes in each of the three armed forces

[1168] The RAM establishes the governing criteria and general guidelines to ensure the airworthiness of military aircraft, helping to ensure their continued airworthiness in a manner similar to that established for civil aviation

[1169] In addition to its implementation in the armed forces, through an agreement with the Military Household of the Presidential Office, the Presidential air assets have been incorporated into the SADEF

[1173] Defense Means Approval System Established by Resolution MD 136/2011, the Defense Means Approval System aims to integrate and systematize the jurisdiction's own approval capabilities in pursuit of common guidelines and standards stipulated based on the priorities set by Military Strategic Planning

[1174] The means of mandatory approval are established by ministerial resolution

[1175] Once approved, users stipulate Specific Approval Programs, which must meet a series of specific requirements

[1176] Once these requirements are met, the Defense Approval Program is drawn up, which leads to the convening of technicaladvisory committees made up of the user and an independent third party or specialists from the jurisdiction, who validate the actions taken or to be taken

[1177] The technical and operational requirements and acceptance test protocols that are proposed or have been carried out are analyzed, and after the relevant evaluations and possible corrective or complementary actions are taken, the approval certificate is issued

[1178] The technical advisory committees, created specifically for those products, processes, or services that are to be approved, are the operational pillars of the system and base their definitions on agreed-upon technical opinions

[1179] Among the various projects underway, the most notable are the approval of newly developed and modernized radars, the restoration of the icebreaker Almirante Irízar and the submarine San Juan, and the design and manufacturing updates of the Pampa aircraft and the Argentine Medium Tank

[1181] The Ministry of Defense (MINDEF) established this system with Resolution MD 901/2011, the objective of which is to standardize products and processes commonly used by the armed forces, seeking greater homogeneity and achieving economies of scale

[1182] Its function is to determine and maintain updated technical standards through the work of specialist committees and based on criteria of efficiency, safety, and interoperability, thus ensuring an adequate logistics chain for spare parts and minimum quality standards for the equipment to be acquired

[1183] The governing body of the system is the Higher Standardization Committee, composed of the highest logistics authorities from the Ministry of Energy and Mines (MINDEF), the Ministry of Defense (EMCO), and the three armed forces

[1184] The "DEF Standards" are mandatory and have been issued and registered following established procedures based on analyses and proposals from civilian and military specialists in the field of national defense

[1185] Standardization covers all areas involving national defense

[1186] Among these, the development of DEF Standards for clothing, healthcare, automobiles, communications equipment, food, and weapons used by the armed forces stands out

[1187] The DEF standards were developed and registered based on analysis by civilian and military specialists in the field of national defense and are mandatory

[1188] The Defense Means Cataloging System – Resolution MD 144/2011 – identifies, classifies and codifies the means used by the armed forces in accordance with rules and procedures from international sources, providing a unique and unequivocal identity for their recognition and use by supply agencies or agents

[1189] Technically qualified personnel (identifiers, catalogers, and administrators) interact with a single national and international database through a dedicated computer system, identifying and cataloging the material

[1190] Cataloging thus becomes a fundamental tool for inventory control and the international identification of Argentine products

[1191] Furthermore, cataloging allows local manufacturers (of both military and civilian materials) to enter the international market by offering their products to the armed forces of other countries, since by being part of the database they are easily identified by potential buyers

[1192] The Argentine National Cataloging Office is at the forefront of South America and serves as a training center not only at the national level, but also trains military personnel from Chile, Peru, and Uruguay in courses offered by our country

[1194] This was reflected in the signing of agreements between the various levels of government, aimed at regularizing specific situations, promoting the growth of urban infrastructure, and fostering the development of housing policies

[1195] These agreements are then submitted to the State Property Management Agency for formalization

[1196] Likewise, in order to achieve the best operational use of military installations, their relocation is in progress, promoting urban redevelopment

[1197] Among these initiatives, it is worth highlighting the efforts made with the municipality of Esquel, in the province of Chubut, where a reforestation plan is being implemented on 420 hectares of the EA). This implies a commitment to respect forest growth until pruning time, coordinating military operations to avoid disrupting objectives, and contributing to national defense

[1198] The activities are carried out in conjunction with the Social Security and Insurance Institute of the province of Chubut, the Ministry of Territorial Development and Productive Systems of the same province, the Andean-Patagonian Forestry Research and Extension Center, the National Institute of Agricultural Technology, and the Chubut Province Development Corporation

[1199] On the other hand, an agreement was reached with the province of San Juan to undertake efforts to address the need for orderly urban expansion planning, as well as the essential infrastructure projects to meet the current and future demands for basic services for San Juan residents. This includes the land known as Campo Sarmiento, which is under the jurisdiction of the EA (Argentine Army). Furthermore, on FAA land in the Morón district, an agreement was reached to finalize the transfer of rights to subdivisions located within the Morón Military Air Base to the municipality of that jurisdiction, along with a commitment to use the land to provide housing

[1206] Management of building infrastructure The importance of managing the buildings assigned to the Defense System and the plans for the conservation, restructuring, and modernization of their structures and equipment was prioritized

[1207] Given the magnitude of this, it is necessary to join forces with other organizations and institutions that are able to contribute to the expansion and improvement of this infrastructure's capabilities

[1227] The current stage of implementation of the results-oriented management approach in the Ministry of Defense requires a technical integrative support body for the joint analysis of the design, implementation and evaluation of all those actions that are oriented towards that objective and, especially, for the monitoring and control of the execution, evaluation and optimization of the management results commitments

[1228] Since 2009, MINDEF has implemented results-based management, and since 2012, a "Committee for the Implementation of Results-Based Management in the Defense Jurisdiction (CGR)" has been in operation to evaluate this development, created by Resolution MD

[1229] The CGR takes into consideration the resolutions and directives of the Executive Branch for National Defense, military strategic planning, specific planning documents prepared by the General Staffs of the armed forces, and the current national public administration budget to fulfill the following functions: a. To be aware of and provide an opinion on the actions undertaken within the scope of MINDEF with the aim of improving the preparation of the program budget, and especially those that are oriented toward the evolution towards a results-based budget

[1230] b. Understand the monitoring of compliance with Results-Based Management Commitments from both an operational and technical-budgetary perspective, as well as operational readiness

[1231] c. Understand and provide input on the optimization of Results-Based Management commitments, with special emphasis on improving the management indicators used by the armed forces to measure the operational readiness of selected units or organizational elements

[1232] d. Promote, especially with regard to budget administration and operational readiness, the ongoing exchange of information on results-oriented management

[1233] e. Promote the training and development of MINDEF, EMCO, and armed forces personnel on issues related to results-based management

[1234] This Committee operates under the purview of the Secretariat of Science, Technology and Production for Defense, is chaired and convened by the Undersecretariat of Resource Management and Budgetary and Operational Planning of Defense, and is made up of permanent members from the General Directorate of Budget of the Ministry, the General Inspectorate, the 4 Headquarters of Logistics, the 3 Headquarters of Operations and the 5 Headquarters of Strategic Planning of the EMCO, the General Directorates of Plans, Programs and Budget and the Training and Readiness Commands of each of the armed forces

[1235] To fulfill its functions, the CGR is based on the following principles: a. Ongoing exchange of information related to the degree of implementation of results-based management commitments, their evaluation and optimization

[1236] b. In accordance with the above, maintaining fluid communications and links using technical and direct coordination channels

[1237] c. Analysis of the process of formulating, programming, executing, and evaluating the jurisdictional budget with the aim of identifying areas for improvement aimed at results-based management

[1238] d. Encouragement of the unification of policies, procedures, and best practices among the armed forces, the EMCO, and the strategic leadership of the MINDEF in all matters related to results-based management

[1239] The CGR's executive and advisory bodies are the working committees that must carry out any other activities assigned to them in addition to their general and specific functions

[1240] The members of the Working Committees are top-level specialists in the topics to be discussed, and are empowered to make decisions

[1241] These Working Committees report directly to the CGR, to whom they must report on the progress of the assigned activities. They are chaired by the Committee's Executive Secretary or a designated representative

[1242] The Ministry of Health (MINDEF) is developing a plan to optimize the health services provided by military hospitals under the auspices of the armed forces

[1243] An initial study of the hospital complex revealed a shortage of personnel, infrastructure, and biomedical equipment, which clearly constitutes a limitation on systemic capabilities

[1244] Likewise, the objective defined by the Armed Forces Health Coordination is to gradually move the armed forces' health systems closer to a networked service model

[1245] The results-based management tool can be used in two dimensions: objectives (performance indicators) and capabilities (public offering indicators

[1246] Based on this, a plan is implemented to measure the actual supply of hospital services, based on demand

[1247] The resulting imbalances reflected in the aforementioned diagnosis make measuring the differences between hospital supply and demand a priority

[1248] Determining the imbalances between supply and demand for hospital services will allow the jurisdiction to seek synergies that make it possible to leverage existing resources and promote a process of strategically defining improvements in equipment, infrastructure, and personnel within the framework of the strategic objective of generating, as stated, a networked service model

[1249] The second stage of the plan will seek to measure not only the quantitative offering but also the qualitative one—that is, the quality of services. To this end, we will work in coordination with the military hospital management to develop quality indicators, with a view to improving both the process structure and the organizational and resource planning

[1250] Thus, the proposal is structured around two important aspects: The development of systemic capacity indicators, which in the initial stage will focus on indicators of supply and demand for hospital services, to determine imbalances (excess supply or demand) in each service, hospital, and region of the country

[1251] The development of quality indicators, seeking a specific model for evaluating hospital services that enables continuous improvement

[1252] Among the most notable milestones in results-based management at the Ministry of Defense are: Standardization of sub-jurisdictional budgets

[1253] Development of operational readiness indicators

[1254] Subscription of results-based management commitments

[1255] Creation of the Committee for the Implementation of Results-Based Management in the Defense Jurisdiction

[1256] Development of indicators for military health. [1294] Since the Defense System requires adequate equipment that can be used according to the nation's needs, this constitutes a fundamental aspect of safeguarding sovereignty

[1295] In other words, industrial and technological sovereignty is a fundamental aspect of national sovereignty

[1296] Since the mid-2000s, the Argentine Republic has undertaken the task of recovering its productive capacity to provide strategic defense inputs and increasing its levels of scientific and technological autonomy

[1297] The pillars of this transformation include the integration of the scientific and technological system into the strategic defense planning process, the coordination of defense research, development, and production organizations, and the coordination of these organizations with the entire National Scientific and Technological System

[1298] Within this framework, the National Defense Strategic Planning Cycle was developed, established by Decree 1,729 of 2007 and intended to organically and institutionally integrate both research and development efforts and medium- and long-term equipment programs to obtain defense resources

[1299] Furthermore, progress was made in consolidating a political leadership body at the head of the scientific and technological system and defense production programs

[1300] INVAP—whose name is an acronym composed of the first syllables of the words “applied research”—is a state-owned company created in the 1970s through an agreement signed between the Argentine National Atomic Energy Commission (CNEA) and the government of the province of Río Negro

[1301] Its headquarters, laboratories, and manufacturing plant are located in the city of San Carlos de Bariloche. It employs more than a thousand workers, including highly experienced professionals in the development of technological systems as well as in the management of highly complex projects

[1302] In addition, it has a functional quality system that meets the most demanding national and international standards, technical and administrative systems for project control, and more than 30 years of successful experience in applied research

[1303] Its products and services include nuclear reactors, siting studies, fuel and radioisotope plants, plant maintenance, satellites, radars, wind turbines, robots, special machines, and chemical process engineering

[1308] With the creation of the SCTP and the transfer of the General Directorate of Military Manufacturing (DGFM) to the orbit of the MINDEF, the aim is to promote integration and coordinated planning within the framework of the Industrial-Technological Pole for Defense, made up of said directorate, the Argentine Naval Industrial Complex (CINAR) and the Argentine Aircraft Factory "Brigadier San Martín" (FAdeA) SA, together with the Institute of Scientific and Technical Research for Defense (CITEDEF), the National Geographic Institute (IGN), the Naval Hydrography Service (SHN) and the National Meteorological Service (SMN

[1310] The institutions of the Industrial-Technological Center for Defense have unique potential to drive knowledge creation, innovation, and the implementation of highly complex projects across the country

[1311] Within this framework, the essential conditions are created for the research, development, and production of dual-use technologies (i.e., civil and military) through projects that, given their scale, technical complexity, and strategic nature, could not be developed without clear direction from the national government

[1312] Within this framework, the Hub's coordination with the private sector, the generation of synergies with the national scientific system, and the achievement of concrete results are essential

[1313] These results translate into goods and services whose provision directly or indirectly benefits the entire population

[1314] The Defense Industrial Technological Center includes research institutes and three industrial conglomerates—Fabricaciones Militares (FM), the Argentine Aircraft Factory (FAdeA) SA, and the Argentine Naval Industrial Complex (CINAR)—which comprise a network of seven factories with a total of thirty production plants

[1315] This entails the direct employment of more than 4,500 workers, in addition to the indirect employment generated through private supplier networks, which include numerous SMEs

[1316] So far this century, the national government has made enormous efforts to reverse the consequences of the economic policies implemented during the 1990s, which involved the privatization, liquidation, or closure of the vast majority of state-owned enterprises, particularly those in the defense-industrial complex

[1317] Highlights in the current recovery process include the acquisition of new capabilities in the design and production of high-tech products like radars and satellite systems, and the opening of new FM plants, such as the San José de Jáchal Explosives Factory in the province of San Juan

[1318] Fundamental to all of this is the Hub's coordination with the private sector, the generation of synergies with the National Scientific System, and the achievement of concrete results, which translate into goods and services whose provision directly or indirectly benefits the entire population

[1319] Military Manufacturing With over seventy years of service to national defense and strategic industrial development, studying the history of the Directorate General of Military Manufacturing makes it possible to analyze and understand the process of loss of capabilities of the national technological and productive framework throughout the last quarter of the 20th century and its recovery so far in the 21st century

[1320] The FM industrial complex once had fourteen production facilities and also held stakes in ten industrial companies, including SOMISA, ATANOR, and Petroquímica Río Tercero

[1321] By the end of the 1990s—following an aggressive process of closing and selling plants and companies that led to the loss of thousands of jobs—only four establishments remained, amid a situation of extreme competitive vulnerability in both the national and regional markets

[1322] Since 2003, and as an expression of the socially inclusive development model that was initiated, FM's historical capabilities have been increasingly recovered, while new ones have been developed in line with the demands of the current context

[1323] The transfer of FM from the Ministry of Federal Planning, Public Investment and Services to MINDEF, through Decree 636 of 2013, allowed for the deepening of the recovery and development process, linking FM with all the productive units belonging to the Industrial-Technological Pole for Defense, thus integrating planning aimed at meeting the needs of defense and the production of goods and services for dual use (civil and military

[1324] In this regard, it is worth highlighting the continuity of the 2012-2016 Strategic Plan in its fundamental lines, with new projects having been added following the institutional integration of FM into the aforementioned IndustrialTechnological Hub

[1345] Spine Wagon, specifically designed for the transport of containers in various load configurations

[1442] Once CINAR joined the Consolidation Roundtable convened by the National Mining Secretariat, and together with YPF Tecnologia, actions began to be developed for the manufacture of mining and oil drilling equipment, promoting the recovery of productive capacities in sectors sensitive to national development

[1445] Since 2008, more than 800 vessels have been repaired at the Argentine Naval Industrial Complex, including the iconic ARA San Juan submarine

[1446] Mid-life tasks on the ARA “San Juan” submarine When the need to carry out mid-life repairs on the ARA “San Juan” arose, the Submarine Management was created at CINAR with the aim of forming a specialized team and recovering capabilities that the country had lost decades ago

[1447] The submarine “San Juan” entered CINAR on December 19, 2008, and a total of 625 projects and works were carried out, of which almost four hundred were carried out in the Almirante Storni workshops

[1448] The tasks exclusively involved sixty specialists and skilled workers, which involved more than five thousand hours of training and half a million man-hours of direct labor

[1449] The decision to carry out the mid-life repair of the ARA San Juan in Argentina allowed for the recovery of critical capabilities in the Naval Industry

[1450] One of the main difficulties of the project was that in order to replace the engines and heavy parts of a submarine, due to the impossibility of removing them through the hatches, it was inevitable to open the hull of the vessel using oxy-cutting procedures and then reassemble it

[1451] This process was extremely arduous, including the careful planning of the engineering work to carry it out

[1452] The main tasks carried out were related to the replacement of the four 1,200 kW 16-cylinder MTU diesel engines

[1453] of power each, the renewal of the four electric generators for charging batteries, the electric propulsion motors and auxiliary mechanisms and the comprehensive repair of each of the 960 batteries necessary for the operation of the submarine

[1454] Reconstruction and modernization of the icebreaker “Almirante Irízar” The decision to repair and modernize the icebreaker ARA “Almirante Irízar” in the CINAR workshops constitutes a historic and unprecedented event for the Argentine naval industry

[1455] For the first time in our country, and in all of Latin America, a complete reconstruction of an icebreaker is taking place, which involves the incorporation of high technology and the development of new capabilities

[1456] The challenge of modernizing a symbol and cornerstone of the Antarctic Campaign to the highest international standards is the most complex undertaking in Tandanor's more than 130-year history

[1457] Reconstruction, modernization and redesign of the oceanographic vessel Dr. Bernardo Houssay On September 27, 2011, the oceanographic vessel “Dr. Bernardo Houssay” was launched at the CINAR facilities

[1458] Originally built in Denmark between 1929 and 1930, this motor-sailer served the National Scientific and Technical Research Council (CONICET) for over forty years in oceanographic research, until its ownership was transferred to the Argentine Naval Prefecture in 2001 and renamed in honor of Dr. Bernardo Houssay

[1459] Given the wear and tear and technological obsolescence of the ship's equipment, as well as the necessary modifications to carry out the activities inherent to its role for the Naval Prefecture, the reconstruction and redesign process involved replacing entire sections of the ship, such as the bow and stern, which were built entirely at the Almirante Storni Shipyard facilities

[1460] After its modernization, the “Bernardo Houssay” can transport up to thirty scientists and is equipped with facilities for research work

[1461] To this end, a wet lab with its own cold storage and a dry lab were added to the facility

[1462] In addition, the motor sailboat was equipped with a continuous water flow system that allows for the coupling of temperature, conductivity, fluorescence, and dissolved oxygen sensors, among other parameters, to achieve continuous recording of information that is automatically and geographically referenced 24 hours a day

[1463] Construction of a tugboat for the Argentine Navy Through an agreement signed between TANDANOR and the ARA at the end of 2014, and after almost thirty years without building a new vessel for this force, a tugboat of national design and engineering will be manufactured

[1464] It is a vessel with a naval steel structure and hull designed for towing operations in ports, coastal and offshore, as well as for salvage tasks

[1465] The project, coordinated by TANDANOR, will include other privately owned national shipyards

[1466] Construction of a SWATH vessel for the Naval Hydrographic Service Through an administrative agreement signed in December 2014 with the National Hydrographic Service (SHN), a Small Waterplane Area Twin Hull (SWATH) will be built in TANDANOR

[1467] It's a combination of a boat and a catamaran capable of varying the submersion of its floats to reduce oscillations, making it easier to operate in high seas with intense waves, both while sailing and stationary

[1468] The engineering of this type of ship was developed worldwide during the 1960s and 1970s based on a 1940 Canadian design

[1469] The joint initiative between SHN and TANDANOR represents a turning point in the gradual recovery of the national naval industry, as it embodies a fully national development of naval engineering from conception to final product
