[1494] Internal and external coordination of the Science and Technology for Defense agencies The scientific and technological research and development activity for Defense is conducted by the Secretariat of Science, Technology and Production for Defense and is inserted within the National System of Science, Technology and Innovation (SNCTI) created by Law

[1495] The SCTP is responsible for formulating the Multiannual Scientific and Technological Plan for Defense, as the Ministry of Defense is also responsible for preparing the proposal for the sectoral chapter of the National Science, Technology, and Innovation Plan

[1496] This National Plan establishes national policies and priorities, proposes the annual income and expenditure budget for science, technology, and innovation, and evaluates the Plan's implementation based on its degree of compliance

[1497] One of the central objectives of the Scientific and Technological System for Defense is to achieve close coordination with the National System, with the aim of strengthening cooperation and coordination among organizations that carry out research, development, and innovation activities, promoting the efficient use of available resources at the national level, and achieving higher levels of planning and control of scientific and technological activities

[1498] The National Defense jurisdiction proposes this articulation through different initiatives and under different dimensions

[1499] The integration and participation of the entities that make up the Defense Scientific and Technological System in the Interinstitutional Council for Science and Technology (CICYT) is one of the main objectives of the STCP

[1500] The CICYT brings together the main national organizations in science, technology and innovation and functions as a forum for the coordination and connection of organizations that carry out scientific and technological activities, oriented towards the design of common policies for the system and a closer relationship with society in general and the productive sector in particular, as well as public or private institutions dedicated to the same activity together with rectors of national universities from each of the country's regions

[1501] In its role as coordinator of the Defense Science and Technology System, the SCTP represents the Defense Science and Technology Council (COCITEDEF) at the CICYT (National Council of Science and Technology of the Republic of Moldova) and participates in the work of the Laboratory Accreditation Committee, the Safety and Hygiene Committee for Research and Development Laboratories, and the Committee for Large Institutes

[1502] The bodies that perform scientific and technological functions in the field of national defense are evaluated, controlled, and coordinated by the SCTP

[1503] Research and technological advancement in the defense industry are essential for safeguarding Argentina's national sovereignty and strategic resources

[1504] Defense development takes on the challenge of spearheading the progress of society as a whole through projects that drive capacity building, knowledge, and innovation

[1505] The Institute of Scientific and Technical Research for Defense The Institute of Scientific and Technical Research (CITEDEF) was created in 1954 on the basis of the technical department of the General Directorate of Military Manufacturing

[1506] Still known by the acronym CITEFA, in 1969 its laboratories, workshops and administrative areas were concentrated and located on a 19-hectare site in the town of Villa Martelli – in the metropolitan area of Buenos Aires – where it currently occupies an installed surface area of thirty thousand square meters, in addition to having a test bench in the province of Córdoba on the grounds of the Villa María military factory

[1507] Currently, under the purview of the Undersecretariat of Defense Research, Development, and Production, CITEDEF conducts applied research and development of weapons systems, subsystems, and components up to the prototype level, seeking to subsequently validate and transfer these components to industry for mass production

[1508] This technology transfer occurs both to the public and private sectors

[1509] Another of the institute's functions is the certification of equipment according to the needs of the Ministry of Energy and Mines (MINDEF). Its extensive experience in handling sensitive materials and military-standard certifications enable it to generate dual developments that ensure operability and performance under a variety of conditions

[1510] Another strategic area of CITEDEF is missile repowering, which involves validating and extending the lifespan of ammunition, as well as reengineering certain components of sensitive weapons systems

[1511] The Institute not only provides support for the specific scientific and technological needs of MINDEF, its military instrument, and the specific productive sector, but also provides foresight in these areas

[1512] In this sense, the concept of jointness not only includes the armed forces, with the aim of ensuring their systems are interoperable, but also adds two additional factors: one, the country's capacity to develop technologies that meet these needs, and two, the capacity to massproduce them in order to achieve complete technological autonomy, from demand to production, including development

[1513] SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY SYSTEM FOR DEFENSE Core R&D Programs Funding Mechanisms R&D Organizations for Defense Defense Research and Development Program (PIDDEF) Regime for Research and Development Personnel of the Armed Forces (RPIDFA) CITEDEF DIGID EA SMN DIGID FAA IGN DIGID ARA SHN DIGID EMCO University Institutions 1.1 Rockets and missiles: Gradicom III sounding vector In 2009, Gradicom I (PCX 2009), a single-stage sounding vector with a composite propellant engine, was launched, reaching an altitude of thirty kilometers carrying a warhead weighing one hundred kilograms

[1514] This experience was complemented by the launch of the Gradicom II probe vector in July 2011, which, with a warhead of equal weight, reached an altitude of over ninety kilometers

[1515] The two-stage configuration of the Gradicom II vector required the development of module separation systems, hypersonic flight, ground data reception from considerable distances, and transmission tests in the S band (1.5 to 5.2 GHz), located between the high and very high frequencies

[1516] Since 2011, the Gradicom III probe vector has been under development, seeking to improve overall aerodynamic performance, add research experiments with the participation of various national organizations, and improve vector application technologies within CITEDEF

[1517] This includes the design of new components, an aluminum head and nozzle assembly, changes to the thermal protection, a roll-speed reduction system, and payload recovery with the ability to transport modules with experiments

[1518] It constitutes a fundamental step in the development of micro and nano satellite launchers, contemplated in the different stages of strategic planning by capabilities

[1519] Weapon Systems LVC Project CP30: The “LVC” or “VC Lance” system has been designed taking as reference the technical and operational requirements established by the Army

[1520] It is a surface-to-surface weapons system designed to saturate terrain areas, based on a 127 mm caliber rocket with a range of approximately thirty kilometers

[1521] This modular system, combined with the rapid docking of the modules to the platform and the self-supporting crane, allows for reloading in a short time and with a limited number of personnel. The “Base Bleed” project aims to increase the range of field artillery, particularly the army's 155 mm caliber L33 cannons (CITER and SOFMA

[1522] To this end, the proposal is to develop technology for the manufacture of a bleed base gas generator that will allow for, with high operational reliability and maintaining the precision inherent in gyroscopically stabilized projectiles, an extension of approximately fifteen to twenty percent over the current range

[1523] This will allow for coverage over larger areas, resulting in increased military capabilities

[1524] VCA Palmaria Cannon Maintenance Project: In the area of weapons systems, work is also being done to develop instruments for evaluating the various systems possessed by the armed forces, such as the inspection and digital recording of the bore of 155 mm caliber cannons

[1525] This development was incorporated under the name IMVA to be later used in the study of the remaining useful life for the VCA Palmaria weapons system

[1526] CITEDEF is primarily responsible for the execution of research and development plans, programs, and projects within the framework of scientific and technological policies for Defense. It is the only organization in the sector capable of engineering highly complex products, their subsequent development, prototype construction, and approval

[1527] Radar Q5 - Modernization and commissioning of Plessey AWS-2 Radar on board the Icebreaker “Almirante Irizar” Since 2011, progress has been made in the modernization of the Plessey AWS-2 radar installed on board the “Almirante Irizar”

[1528] The modernization and commissioning of the same included activating the primary and secondary radars (IFF system), the modernization of the technologically obsolete parts, the replacement of the old operating console with one using digital technology, the conversion of the two transmitters to operate on the same frequency ensuring their duplication, the preparation and generation of durable inputs (batch of spare parts), the training and training of the personnel necessary for the operation and support during the effective employment phase

[1529] Following satisfactory factory acceptance tests at CITEDEF and the installation of new wiring, the radar was reinstalled on board the Icebreaker in 2014 and is now operational

[1530] Stabilized Naval Observation System (SEON) This is a project started in 2009 consisting of the development of a system of cameras and rangefinder stabilized on three axes to be installed initially in the ARA “Indómita” speedboat and then in other ARA units

[1531] It is a gyro-stabilized platform for naval use that includes two optoelectronic instruments, one for day vision and one for night vision, plus a laser rangefinder

[1532] The project is part of the Fire Control System for Naval Units, which, in principle, has a dual purpose, serving as a fire control system and data acquisition element for a more complex weapons system, as well as for the rescue of shipwrecked sailors

[1533] LIDAR Project It is the most notable product of the Laser System, a historical line of the institute initiated in the sixties

[1534] The LIDAR project emerged in response to the need for precision equipment for airspace surveillance and protection

[1535] LIDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) are laboratories for monitoring suspended particles in the atmosphere from both natural and anthropogenic agents

[1536] This technology has a significant and direct impact on aviation, as the information collected by these sensors facilitates decision-making, allowing for early warnings, for example, about the presence of volcanic ash in the surrounding atmosphere that could cause problems on flights

[1537] There are currently five LIDARs installed in our country that are used in conjunction with the National Meteorological Service

[1538] Modernization and commissioning of the radar of the Icebreaker Ship ARA “Almirante Irízar”

[1539] Specific projects The following projects reflect the joint intervention of various areas, institutes and companies of the Industrial-Technological Pole for Defense, in addition to the general directorates of Research and Development of the armed forces

[1540] In November 2010, through Resolution 1,484, the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MINDEF) highlighted the need to equip itself with unmanned aerial systems – or unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) –, given that their development would result in the development of high technology of national origin

[1541] Because these aircraft can perform a variety of missions simply by modifying their equipment, a tripartite contract was signed in July 2011 between the Ministries of Defense and Security, and the state-owned technology company INVAP, to promote the development of the Argentine Robotic Aerial System (SARA

[1542] The project focuses on the development and domestic manufacturing of Class II UAVs (50 kg payload capacity and 12 hours of flight endurance) and Class III UAVs (250 kg payload capacity and 20 hours of flight endurance), as well as technologies that enable the development of high-speed aerial targets for antiaircraft targeting

[1543] Each SARA system consists of three or two aerial elements (depending on whether the UAVs are class II or III, respectively, with their sensors and communications systems), a ground element (a mobile control station with its communications system), and another logistics element, providing operational support, spare parts, maintenance tools, personnel training, and technical documentation

[1544] In August 2014, the first SARA (Technology Assessment Model 1) was successfully tested, with Army technical personnel operating a functional UAV model on the outskirts of the city of Córdoba

[1545] With the aim of deepening the national production of components for the local industry, it is expected that the technologies and elements will be developed and manufactured by INVAP or by other industrial suppliers of national origin, as well as incorporating those developments made by universities, university institutes or research centers and that are applicable to the system, prioritizing such institutes, centers, and the companies belonging to the Industrial and Technological Pole for Defense

[1546] Finally, the intellectual property, patents, utility models, trademarks, copyrights and know-how arising as a result of this project, as well as the knowledge, engineering and documentation of systems, components and subsystems developed, as well as the marketing of the products involved in the SARA System, the subsystems, components and their spare parts, will be the exclusive property of two companies under the jurisdiction of MINDEF: the elements corresponding to Class II and III UAVs will remain in the hands of FAdeA and the elements corresponding to the enabling technology for the development of the Aerial Target will remain in the hands of the DGFM

[1547] The development of second- and third-generation unmanned aerial systems aims to optimize border and natural resource control

[1548] Radars Experimental Medium Radar (RAME) and Long Range 3D Primary Radar (Argentine Primary Radar) In

[1549] Decree 1497 established the creation of the National Aerospace Surveillance and Control System (SINVICA), a radarization strategy aimed at covering the entire national territory through the development of radars with national technology and industry

[1550] To this end, Fabricaciones Militares signed an agreement in 2007 with the state-owned technology company INVAP to develop the Long-Range 3D Primary Radar, or Argentine Primary Radar (RPA

[1551] FM assumed project management and became the patent holder for the product, while INVAP contributed its technological capabilities in radar systems

[1552] Primary radars operate independently of any cooperation that may be provided by the objects under observation or their crews (whether air, sea or land), that is, they do not expect an active response from such objects but rather emit radio frequency pulses that, upon impact with the surface of the objects, are reflected and detected by the radar

[1553] Once the data has been processed, it is possible to obtain precise information about the distance at which the object in question is from the radar, its azimuth angle, elevation, speed, etc

[1554] Thus, they constitute the appropriate radar format for the detection of targets that are not necessarily friendly

[1555] In 2010, the first operational model resulting from the RPA development process was installed in the province of Santiago del Estero and was called the "Experimental Medium Radar

[1556] The following year, 2011, in the province of Formosa, the town of Las Lomitas was chosen as the location for an active model of the Argentine Long-Range 3D Primary Radar as part of the Northern Shield Operation

[1557] In September 2014, the homologation process for the Argentine Long-Range 3D Primary Radar was completed at Morón Air Base, Buenos Aires province, by the FAA's Directorate General of Research and Development (DIGID). This process involved analytical studies on different test scenarios and empirical verifications, using PA-28 and A-4 aircraft from the 5th Air Brigade

[1558] The approved Long Range 3D Radar (Radar) is a sophisticated device for detection, surveillance and control with a coverage radius of 400 kilometers (250 miles), excellent performance and low maintenance costs, easily adaptable to different geographical and climatic scenarios

[1559] All these features make it a technological product with great prospects for international marketing

[1560] The approval of the Argentine Primary Radar is a significant milestone for both the national industry and the defense of sovereignty, as it constitutes the starting point for the serial production of a radar whose technological heritage is entirely national

[1561] Argentine Long Range 3D Primary Radar

[1562] Town of Las Lomitas, Province of Formosa

[1563] In September 2014, the approval process for the Argentine Primary 3D Long-Range Radar, a sophisticated technological device for detection, surveillance, and control, was completed

[1564] Argentine Monopulse Secondary Radar Designed and manufactured by INVAP, the Argentine Monopulse Secondary Radar (RSMA) responded to a common requirement of the FAA and the National Civil Aviation Administration (ANAC) with the objective of strengthening air traffic control

[1565] Secondary radars require automatic responses via a “transponder” device (a specialized transceiver that acts by receiving and transmitting) installed in aircraft and used for commercial aviation control

[1566] The secondary radar located on the ground transmits interrogations directed at the aircraft in question, and the latter responds by returning signals to the radar. These signals are then interpreted and converted into specific data: azimuth angles and distance between the flying object and the radar

[1567] The manufacture and installation of the RSMA in different parts of the country began with the signing of a contract between INVAP and the MINDEF in 2006, in which the Bariloche company committed to the development and construction of eleven units (an operational prototype followed by a series of ten), which resulted in the location of the first RSMA: one in Bariloche (Río Negro province) and the remaining ten in Quilmes and Bahía Blanca (in the province of Buenos Aires), Santa Rosa (La Pampa province), Neuquén (Neuquén province), in the city of Córdoba and in Morteros (Córdoba province), in San Miguel de Tucumán (Tucumán province) and in the three homonymous capitals of the provinces of San Luis, La Rioja and Salta

[1568] Since the National Government, through Decree 239 in 2007, transferred responsibility for airspace control from the FAA to ANAC, the contract with INVAP was transferred to the aforementioned administration in 2009 by MINDEF

[1569] A year later, in 2010, ANAC signed a new contract with INVAP for the provision of eleven more identical secondary radars that have already been installed in Comodoro Rivadavia, Río Gallegos and Gobernador Gregores (in the province of Santa Cruz), in Ushuaia (province of Tierra del Fuego, Antarctica and the South Atlantic Islands), in Trelew and Esquel (province of Chubut), in Posadas (province of Misiones), in Corrientes (province of Corrientes), in Sáenz Peña (province of Chaco), in Malargüe (province of Mendoza) and in Pehuajó (province of Buenos Aires

[1570] Modernization of TPS-43 radars In 2011, the Ministry of Energy and Mines signed a contract with INVAP, this time for the modernization of a Westinghouse TPS-43/W-430 radar belonging to the Air Force

[1571] The agreement is part of the modernization program undertaken in response to the advanced technological obsolescence faced by these systems

[1572] While the modernization of the first radar is being completed, the modernization of three other radars with the same characteristics is planned, thus completing the process with the four of the same make and model that the FAA has

[1573] MEKO 360 AND TR1700 The Project consists of the modernization and updating of the MEKO 360 ship and the San Juan TR1700 submarine through the Development, provision and integration of the Operational Prototypes of the Integrated Command and Control System of Sensors, Weapons and Communications for Naval Systems

[1574] The project development, which will involve the Ministry of Defense, the Argentine Navy and INVAP SE, comprises two phases: the first aims to develop the System Requirements, Conceptual Engineering and Implementation Plans, and the second includes the manufacturing, installation of the Operational Prototypes and Testing in a MEKO 360 type Surface Unit and a TR 1700 type Submarine Unit

[1575] However, this modernization will be capable of being incorporated into other naval units of the Navy, constituting a strategic development project for Defense

[1576] The work to be carried out includes the repair and modernization of systems that present various deficiencies and are generally more than 30 years old, updating and enhancing their original performance

[1577] One of the main advantages of the project is that it will allow for the development of a chain of local suppliers of advanced defense technology, which will not only meet the needs of the local market but also open new markets for the export of products with significant added value

[1578] Likewise, it was agreed to incorporate into the equipment and systems those developments carried out by Universities, University Institutes, or National Research Centers that are applicable to the systems covered by the Contract

[1579] Additionally, priority will be given to contracting with the Institute of Scientific and Technical Research for Defense (CITEDEF) and other institutions or companies within the Ministry of Defense to develop work packages in areas within their jurisdiction

[1580] Other advantages of being able to contribute, through Research and Development (R&D), to present an alternative solution to the systems of Naval Units with national technology are the following: Increase technological independence from foreign suppliers, with knowledge of the functions and embedded programs or part of the systems

[1581] The fact that the project is being carried out by INVAP rather than a foreign company allows our country to regain technological independence in the defense sector, importing only what cannot be produced locally, and also makes it possible to preserve the knowledge and capabilities developed as a result of the project

[1582] • Greater development of local industry, given that it involves the local design and manufacturing of equipment and systems, not just their assembly and commissioning. • The adoption, in every possible case, of mature technologies existing in Argentina and/or guaranteed commercial availability for system design, based on their local development level and promoting their development to the appropriate level to meet requirements

[1583] The Defense Research and Development Program aims to promote, coordinate, and evaluate projects from both the public and private sectors

[1584] Modernization of the Argentine Medium Tank (TAM

[1585] Modernization of the Argentine Medium Tank Developed in the 1970s and produced by the company Tanque Argentino Medio Sociedad del Estado (TAMSE), the Argentine Medium Tank (TAM) is an armored combat vehicle characterized by its high maneuverability and speed, its ability to be operated in all geographical conditions present in the national territory and a 105 mm cannon

[1586] Given the technological obsolescence of this vehicle, it was planned to upgrade it towards the first decade of the 21st century to adapt it to new needs

[1587] Since 2011, in agreement with the State of Israel and the Israeli firm Elbit Systems Ltd

[1588] Progress was made on the modernization of a prototype called TAM2C, which was completed in

[1589] This led to the achievement of the following results, among others: a complete modification of the turret, including thermal and night vision cameras for the driver, to enable both day and night use of the vehicle; a transition from a hydraulically stabilized turret to an electronically stabilized one; the addition of various types of electronic optics and a laser rangefinder for the gunner and tank commander positions; the addition of a thermal coating on the barrel; and the addition of an auxiliary power unit, allowing the TAM to operate with the main engine off

[1590] Throughout 2013, progress was made in the technical and operational evaluation of TAM2C, verifying the satisfactory operation of the newly installed systems

[1591] The evaluation included static and dynamic operational tests, determination of the probability of impact on the first shot under various firing conditions, and firing execution in simulated combat situations

[1592] Given the aforementioned satisfactory results of the modernization, its extension to an initial series of 74 tanks is planned for the 602nd Arsenal Battalion (Boulogne-Sur-Mer, Buenos Aires province), in a production process that will involve national labor at all stages and foresees the incorporation of national suppliers

[1593] Additionally, an Argentine-designed and manufactured auxiliary power unit will be incorporated into the project and produced under Fábrica Militar's direction

[1594] In 2013, the modernization of the prototype of the Argentine Medium Tank TAM2C was completed, an armored combat vehicle characterized by its high maneuverability and speed

[1595] Image Acquisition System (SAI) for Lockheed P3 Orion aircraft Through an agreement between the ARA and INVAP, a project was started in 2013 to obtain an electro-optical system for image acquisition

[1596] The SAI-Orion consists of a sphere containing a gyro-stabilized platform on which electro-optical sensors, a processing and control unit, and a command and display unit are mounted, designed to be mounted on P3 Orion aircraft

[1597] The system features a panoramic camera, a night vision camera, and a target identification camera

[1598] The first stage of the project was successfully completed in 2014, with a technological demonstration model successfully tested on one of the naval aviation's P3 Orion aircraft

[1599] A prototype Stabilized Optronic System is expected to be developed, consisting of a visible camera, a high-definition infrared camera, and a laser rangefinder that can operate both day and night

[1600] “Centenary Experience” Probe Following the successful experience of the Gradicom I and II Probe Vectors, and on the occasion of the centenary of Argentine military aviation, in December 2013 the FAA launched the “Centenary Experience” Probe Vector with satisfactory results, thus reactivating space activity at the Chamical Military Air Base, in the province of La Rioja

[1601] The team of engineers and technicians from the Applied Research Center of the Air Force's Research and Development Directorate-General was involved in this project

[1602] The launch also reflected the collaborative efforts of the FAA, CITEDEF, and the FM, with the participation of the Aeronautical University Institute (IUA) of the Air Force, the National University of La Plata (UNLP), the National Technological University (UTN), the National University of Comahue (UNCo), and national companies involved in the field to develop knowledge, new technologies, and innovative resources that will facilitate greater competitiveness for Argentine industry

[1603] The Space Access Plan includes a series of milestones, including the launch of the FAS 1500 rocket, a joint development that integrates the capabilities of FM, CITEDEF, and the FAA

[1604] By Resolution 549 of 2008, the Ministry of Defense created the PIDDEF (Research and Development Program for Defense) with the purpose of promoting, coordinating and evaluating efforts in research and development for Defense, developed within the framework of the agencies and institutes of the areas dependent on the Ministry and even other public or private entities, which “tend to maintain, update, increase or acquire an operational capacity for the military instrument.”

[1609] CHAPTER XVI SPECIALIZED SERVICES The Scientific Technological System for Defense has specialized services: the National Meteorological Service, the National Geographic Institute, the Naval Hydrography Service and the Defense Logistics Service

[1610] The National Meteorological Service The National Meteorological Service (SMN) has the mission of observing, understanding and forecasting the weather in the national territory and adjacent oceanic zones, with the aim of contributing to the protection of the life and property of its inhabitants and to the sustainable development of economic activities sensitive to climate conditions

[1611] In addition, it represents and addresses the obligations assumed by the country before international meteorological organizations

[1612] This scientifictechnical organization had its origin in the more than century-old National Law 559 promulgated in 1872 by President Domingo Sarmiento, when the Argentine Meteorological Office (OMA) was created under the Ministry of Justice, Worship and Public Instruction. This was the first public meteorological organization in the southern hemisphere and the third in the world, after the Hungarian one in 1870 and the American one in

[1613] The SMN was transferred to the Ministry of Economy and Finance's Planning Secretariat by Decree 1,432 of 2007 and to the Ministry of Science, Technology and Production for Defense by Decree 636 of 2013, which gave it the status of a decentralized body with a Technical Advisory Council, with financial and economic autonomy, its own legal personality, and the capacity to operate in both public and private law

[1614] The network of meteorological observation stations As an active member of the World Meteorological Organization and following international standards and procedures, the SMN has designed and maintains operating a vast network of meteorological stations throughout the national territory

[1615] These 67 stations are part of the Regional Basic Synoptic Network (RSBR), which is used for the international and regional exchange of meteorological data through the Buenos Aires Regional Telecommunications Center, as a direct contribution to World Meteorological Watch programs

[1616] Five surface synoptic stations have been installed at Antarctic bases operated by the Argentine Republic, three of which (Orcadas, Esperanza, and Marambio) have been internationally recognized as reference stations due to the quality of their data and the length of their time series

[1617] There are currently 16 strategically located automatic stations that allow data to be obtained for synoptic purposes and transmitted via satellite

[1618] Among them, the Punta de Vacas station in the province of Mendoza stands out, due to its location at 2,400 meters above sea level, and the recently installed stations on Martín García Island and Pontón Recalada, due to their importance for navigation on the Río de la Plata

[1619] The Synoptic High Altitude Observation Network is composed of 8 stations on the continental territory

[1620] Some of these stations, based on their extensive record and the quality of their observations, are part of the network of reference climate stations that form the basis of the Global Climate Observing System (GCOS

[1621] The SMN operates six meteorological observatories: the Buenos Aires Central Observatory (in Villa Ortúzar, Autonomous City of Buenos Aires), those in the cities of Córdoba and Pilar (Córdoba Province), La Quiaca (Jujuy Province), Mendoza City (Mendoza Province), and the Orcadas Antarctic Base

[1622] The role of the SMN in the emergency: the meteorological alert Providing alerts and warnings of possible areas of development of meteorological phenomena with a high impact on the population is a responsibility of the SMN

[1623] This responsibility is centered on its strategic mission to contribute to the protection of life and property of residents in the event of meteorological phenomena

[1624] The National Meteorological Service has a network of centers, offices, meteorological observatories, and stations located in more than 140 locations across the country: surface synoptic stations, Antarctic stations, automatic stations, and GPS upper-air observation stations, meteorological monitoring offices, aerodrome meteorological offices, and observatories

[1625] These alerts and warnings are disseminated to registered users, such as Civil Defense, social media, national agencies with jurisdiction over climate emergency issues, and the general public

[1627] The role of the SMN in civil aviation: aeronautical meteorology The SMN, through the Aeronautical Meteorology Department, is responsible for providing real-time meteorological information and forecasts to all aeronautical users so that they can carry out their functions efficiently and safely

[1702] The Defense Logistics Service The process of modernizing Defense Logistics, which began in the middle of the first decade of this century and was characterized by the systematization of resource management and its centralization under a specialized area of the Ministry of Defense, continued to deepen, giving rise to new material and institutional milestones

[1703] The Undersecretariat of the Defense Logistics Service is responsible for managing consolidated contracts that integrate common requirements of the armed forces

[1704] Through a new and broader institutional organization, the actions to be developed by the different directorates and departments that make up the Undersecretariat of the Defense Logistics Service are articulated according to the following guidelines: • Vision: lead the logistics systems for obtaining and distributing resources for the armed forces

[1705] • Mission: To obtain goods, services, and weapons systems to meet national defense needs

[1706] The actions include: • Coordinating the identification and consolidation of requirements for goods and services commonly used by the armed forces

[1707] Carry out operational management of the consolidated procurement of goods and services referred to in the previous item. Create and maintain an updated statistical record of the consumption of all goods and services of the armed forces, covering, among other parameters, contracting units, contracting methods, volumes, award prices, and frequency

[1708] • Establish the internal rules and procedures that will govern the preparation of the annual procurement plans for the armed forces

[1726] MILITARY COORDINATION OF EMERGENCY ASSISTANCE On May 31, 2013, through Article 4 of Decree 636, the Argentine government established the Secretariat of Military Coordination of Emergency Assistance (CME) within the Ministry of Defense (MINDEF), as a civil coordination body for the deployment of the armed forces in tasks of prevention, immediate response and reconstruction in emergency or disaster situations

[1727] In recent history, these forces have accumulated experience in civil protection actions in the most important emergencies that affected the national territory, including the floods on the river coast in 1998 that afflicted cities and towns in the provinces of Chaco, Corrientes, Formosa, Santa Fe, Entre Ríos and Misiones, and in 2001 in the central region of our geography, in the provinces of Buenos Aires, Córdoba, La Pampa and Santa Fe, and in the city of Santa Fe itself, capital of the province of the same name, in

[1728] In all these cases, the intervention of the armed forces was an emergency measure implemented in the face of the magnitude of the events, as the response capacities and resources of the municipal and provincial governments were overwhelmed

[1729] The flood that affected the capital city of Buenos Aires province, La Plata, and its surrounding areas in April 2013 marked a turning point

[1730] The material inability of state agencies to respond immediately to an event of such exceptional magnitude revealed the usefulness of the armed forces' participation, which demonstrated their logistical deployment capacity to complement the work of other actors, both in receiving and distributing humanitarian aid, as well as in the various reconstruction tasks

[1731] Given these experiences, the national government decided to optimize the deployment and coordination of military resources, as well as the assessment of equipment and technology needs for immediate response, rehabilitation, and reconstruction in the face of these adverse events

[1732] President Cristina Fernández de Kirchner then took the initiative to improve the use of public resources by carrying out a strategic reorganization that, among other changes, involved the creation of the CME

[1733] The Military Emergency Assistance Coordination Secretariat was established within the Ministry of Defense in 2013 as a civilian coordination body for the deployment of the Armed Forces in emergency prevention, response, and reconstruction tasks

[1734] With respect to the previous normative and doctrinal order, the role of the Armed Forces in community support actions in emergency and disaster situations has been prioritized, given the consideration and inclusion of this complementary mission in military planning and capacity development. To frame the creation of the CME, it is important to begin by highlighting the significance of the sanction of the aforementioned decree

[1735] The National Defense Law 23.554, sanctioned in 1988 during the government of Raúl Alfonsín, in its Art

[1736] characterizes Civil Defense and defines it as an essential issue of national Defense

[1737] Decree 727/06, which regulated the law eighteen years later, establishes that the fundamental primary mission of the military instrument is to "ensure national defense against situations of external aggression perpetrated by armed forces of other State(s

[1738] This provision is complemented by Decree 1,691 of the same year, which also defines four subsidiary missions of the armed forces, including "participation in operations to support the national community or friendly countries

[1739] This standard establishes that the military instrument must be "structured doctrinally, organically, and functionally according to the primary mission" and, consequently, stipulates that community support operations "will be carried out based on the remaining capabilities

[1740] The role of the armed forces in community support actions in emergency and disaster situations has been strengthened by the National Defense Policy Directive issued in December 2014 by Decree 2,645 of the President of the Nation, which established that “as a Complementary Mission, it be taken into account during the planning process, so that the generation of military capabilities during the process allows the military instrument to address these issues.”

[1741] Undoubtedly, these guidelines for regulation and doctrine prioritize the complementary role assigned to them with respect to the previously existing framework

[1742] From an operational perspective, the provisions referred to reinforce MINDEF Resolution 121 of 2006, which placed the responsibility of liaising with the Civil Protection Directorate, then under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of the Interior, under the Secretariat of Military Affairs, and defined the head of the EMCO Community Support Department as the technical advisor to the civil liaisons

[1743] In this way, coordination with the civil protection system was delegated to the military authorities

[1749] In contrast to this legal framework, the aforementioned Article 4 of Decree 636 of 2013 – which among other measures created the CME – formally implied three substantial innovations: - It prioritized the participation of the MINDEF and the armed forces in actions of support and assistance to the community by assigning the attention of this problem with the rank of Secretary of State

[1750] Laid the groundwork for providing organizational coordination between MINDEF and the entire set of agencies that make up the national civil protection system

[1751] It consolidated the paradigm of political control by incorporating a civilian leadership body between the armed forces and other state agencies involved in civil protection tasks

[1752] In this regard, it is important to note that while the notions of "civil leadership" or "civil control" refer to the institutional framework that guides national defense policies, the notion of "civil coordination in emergencies" designates a specific task that is carried out within that institutional framework

[1753] Along with these regulatory and institutional changes, it is necessary to highlight some historical and contextual aspects that are relevant to understanding the hierarchical role of the armed forces in civil protection tasks beyond specific incidents

[1754] The creation of the CME is based on two complementary factors: national and international

[1755] The flood in the city of La Plata In April 2013, an event occurred that marked a turning point in state policies regarding emergencies and in the perception of the need to enhance the institutional role of the participation of the armed forces in civil protection tasks

[1756] On the evening of April 2, 2013, in the city of La Plata, capital of the province of Buenos Aires, and in surrounding towns, a rainstorm occurred that specialized agencies described as a historic record: 300 millimeters of rain fell in just four hours over an area of 3,500 urbanized hectares

[1757] The outcome was dramatic: eighty-nine people lost their lives, more than two thousand five hundred were evacuated, and two hundred thousand were affected to varying degrees

[1758] One thousand two hundred troops from different Army units were employed in evacuation tasks, food distribution, administration and delivery of donations, water purification and distribution, and tele-computer support

[1759] The Military Emergency Assistance Coordination Secretariat draws on experiences in which the armed forces have demonstrated their aptitude, logistics, capacity, and commitment when responding to emergencies

[1763] At the national level, the evolution of the armed forces' participation in civil protection tasks was linked to the role they played at different times in Argentine history

[1764] This can be seen in the shift from the "double taxation theory," which has guided the armed forces' intervention in emergencies and disasters since 1939, to a critical perspective of the "securitist" vision of defense, as embodied in the National Defense Law, which, among other aspects, replaced the concept of Anti-Aircraft Defense with that of Civil Defense, thus redefining the role of the armed forces in their relationship with the various state actors involved in the civil protection system

[1765] At the international level, meanwhile, there is a trend toward the organization of disaster risk management systems as a means of institutionalized state response to the increasing occurrence of adverse events, within which military resources acquire operational and logistical importance

[1766] In this sense, the participation of military resources in civil protection tasks must be understood in the context of the development of public policies for disaster risk management

[1767] Institutionally, this means that in Argentina the role of the CME can only be fully understood if we consider, at the same time, its functions within the Defense System and its coordination with other state agencies and at all levels of government

[1768] The involvement of military resources in civil protection tasks must be understood within the context of developing public policies for disaster risk management

[1769] Background of the participation of the armed forces and the Ministry of Defense in civil protection tasks In the Argentine Republic, the participation of the armed forces in the response to disasters or emergencies recognizes two major periods

[1770] The first runs from 1939 to 1988, and the second from 1988 to the present

[1771] The intervention of the armed forces in emergencies dates back to 1939 with the creation of the Passive Air Defense Command, the first national agency responsible for emergencies and disasters that operated within the framework of the then Ministry of War

[1772] This agency had a dual mission, borrowed from the North American model of what was then known as the "double taxation theory," which proposed applying the same system to two different situations: reducing the effects of situations arising from war, and responding to disasters caused by natural phenomena or human action

[1773] During the dictatorial period that began in 1955, the self-proclaimed liberating revolution issued Decree Law 6,250 of 1958, introducing a change: within the scope of the then Ministry of Aeronautics, it added to its territorial Passive Anti-Aircraft Defense responsibilities the responsibility to intervene to limit risks and reduce the effects "in the event of damage caused by natural agents

[1774] In 1967, when another dictatorship appointed General Juan Carlos Onganía as President of the Nation, the functions of Passive Anti-Aircraft Defense became directly dependent on the Minister of Defense, creating a Civil Defense Service (Law 17,192), whose functions were prevention and preparation of response actions to the effects of disasters

[1775] In 1969, the name "Passive Air Defense" was changed to "Civil Defense," introducing conceptual changes that would later be refined by current laws and decrees

[1776] The return to the rule of law after the last Argentine dictatorship of the 20th century (1976-1983) created the conditions for the constitutional authority to rethink the National Defense System, defining a new institutional framework for the armed forces

[1777] Thus, civilian and political control over these forces was consolidated, ending the tutelary imprint that the military had assumed over the political system, replacing that totalitarian and "security-oriented" vision and establishing a sharp distinction between matters of "defense" and "internal security," resulting in the demilitarization of civilian functions still under the jurisdiction of the military

[1778] This orientation was embodied in a new body of legislation, beginning with the National Defense Act of

[1779] The National Defense Law replaced the concept of "anti-aircraft defense," which had guided military participation in emergency support tasks, with that of "civil defense

[1780] Its passage was a historical turning point, as it gave democratic support to the concept of national defense by eliminating the guiding role previously played by the so-called National Security Doctrine, demilitarizing internal security, and strengthening the political leadership of national defense and the armed forces

[1781] Regarding civil protection actions, the law introduced a substantial conceptual change, definitively replacing the concept of "anti-aircraft defense," which for decades had guided military participation in emergency support tasks, with that of "civil defense

[1782] Regarding the role of the military in this regard, the legal modifications first involved the transfer of civil protection to the Ministry of the Interior and finally to the Ministry of Security (Decree 636 of

[1783] In relation to this institutional process, it is worth mentioning that the Internal Security Law 24,059 of 1992 transferred responsibility for Civil Defense from the exclusively military sphere to the sphere of the security forces. This provision was complemented by Decree 660 of 1996, which advanced the jurisdictional separation of powers in matters of defense and internal security, thus transferring the Argentine Naval Prefecture, the National Gendarmerie, and the National Directorate of Civil Defense from the Ministry of Defense to the Ministry of the Interior

[1784] Since Law 24,948 on the Restructuring of the Armed Forces, passed in 1998, a distinction has been made between the scenarios for the use of military instruments and those of "operations in support of the national community or friendly countries

[1785] This initial distinction was later expanded in Annex I of Decree 1,691 of 2006, which approved the Directive on the Organization and Operation of the Armed Forces

[1786] This annex defines the main mission and subsidiary missions of the military instrument and their respective areas of action

[1787] The decree links community support efforts to "disaster situations, natural disasters, or any other circumstances determined in accordance with current laws

[1788] On this issue, the 2010 edition of the White Paper on Defense refers to "the participation of the armed forces in civil protection operations" under three modalities: a) Humanitarian aid, which is activated in the country in cases of emergencies, disasters, and critical social limitations

[1789] b) Humanitarian assistance provided to materialize federal support provided by the National government in other countries

[1790] Community support encompasses tasks that, without an emergency, are carried out by the armed forces with the aim of promoting or facilitating the social and economic development of an area

[1791] The preceding description has attempted to facilitate the appreciation of the changes that have occurred throughout the 20th century in the state management of civil protection actions in Argentina, from an initial approach framed within strictly military principles to the creation of specialized civilian bodies

[1792] The conceptual modification surrounding “civil defense” was also presented, initially treated as a problem addressable under military criteria, until the present, when the concept is conceived in its own specificity

[1793] The role of the Ministry of Defense in civil protection At the end of the 20th century, the accumulated experience – both in the development of regulations and in the treatment of adverse events – led to a new institutional arrangement for civil protection tasks in Argentina

[1794] This section briefly reviews this experience to explain in detail the practical changes that have been brought about by the creation of the CME under the purview of the Ministry of Defense (MINDEF

[1795] In 1999, Decree 1,250 created the Federal Emergency System (SIFEM) as an organizational framework designed to articulate the relevant national public agencies and coordinate their actions with the provinces, the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires, and the municipalities, in order to efficiently prevent and manage emergencies and disasters caused by natural phenomena or human activity

[1796] However, in recent years the SIFEM has not functioned as an operational instrument

[1797] For various reasons, his presence has been rather formal

[1798] Therefore, Decree 636 of 2013 should be understood as a step forward in the institutional reorganization of the emergency system

[1799] In this regard, the Decree incorporated important modifications to the national civil protection system: It transferred from the Ministry of the Interior and Transportation of the Nation to the Ministry of Security the "duties related to the implementation of actions aimed at resolving extraordinary situations or emergencies that occur in the territory of the Nation, as well as the coordination of the SIFEM

[1800] The National Directorate of Civil Protection was transferred from the Ministry of the Interior and Transport to the Ministry of Security

[1801] The CME was created under the authority of MINDEF, whose function within the National Civil Protection System is to "intervene, within its scope of competence, in the prevention and response actions required for the civil protection of inhabitants in the face of man-made and natural disasters, coordinating its actions with the Ministry of Security and the relevant agencies

[1802] Emergency Committee (COE) meeting in the city of Concordia, Entre Ríos province, during the floods of July

[1803] Later, Decree 48 of 2014 further structured the Ministry of Security's civil protection functions by creating the Undersecretariat of Civil Protection and Comprehensive Emergency and Disaster Response under the Ministry of Security and establishing the National Civil Protection Directorate within its jurisdiction

[1804] Its primary function is to coordinate the national government's intervention in emergency assistance, risk management, and recovery of disaster-affected areas

[1805] The same decree specifically mentions the CME as a collaborative body for the coordination of federal aid

[1806] From the above, it is clear that the Ministry of Security, through the Undersecretariat of Civil Protection and Comprehensive Response to Emergencies and Disasters, leads and coordinates the National Civil Protection System

[1807] The CME intervention occurs according to two criteria and in relation to the magnitude of the adverse event

[1808] In the event of an emergency, the CME may intervene at the direct request of municipal authorities through the Ministry of Security

[1809] In the event of a major disaster, when the national government has already assumed responsibility for the response, the CME coordinates the deployment of the armed forces at the request of the Ministry of Security, which will then coordinate the necessary efforts with other agencies in the system to achieve a comprehensive approach

[1810] Formally, the creation of the CME involved the analysis and review of regulatory aspects that guide MINDEF's actions in civil protection tasks

[1811] National Defense Law 23,554 and its regulatory Decree 727 of 2006 establish that the armed forces' primary mission is to repel and ward off all external state military aggression against the nation's vital and strategic interests

[1812] This legal framework defines Civil Defense as the "set of non-aggressive measures and activities aimed at avoiding, nullifying, or reducing the effects that war, natural disasters, or any other disaster may have on the population and their property, contributing to restoring the normal rhythm of life in the affected areas, as established by the respective legislation

[1815] Law 24,948 on the Restructuring of the Armed Forces and Decree 1,691 of 2006 established a set of subsidiary missions for the armed forces, including operations to support the national community or friendly countries in situations of catastrophe, natural disaster, or any other circumstance determined in accordance with current laws

[1816] Decree 727 of 2006 establishes in its Article 19 that the EMCO is the body responsible for the functional control of military means and operational control over the elements of the armed forces that, based on the missions assigned to them, are relevant to use

[1817] Following the creation of the CME, work began on adapting the EMCO's civil protection directives with the aim of providing an operational conceptual basis for the CME's actions as a civil body for strategic leadership in emergencies

[1818] As a result of this process, Resolution MD 297 of 2014 emerged, which instructed the head of the EMCO to convene a Technical Advisory Commission composed of representatives from the CME, the EMCO itself, and the General Staffs of the armed forces to draft a Directive for the Military Coordination of Emergency Assistance

[1819] The directive established the general direction for the use of military instruments in emergency situations under the guiding principle of "dual employment" and a Military Emergency Assistance Coordination Plan to standardize the functioning of the armed forces and their role in the event of emergencies or disasters

[1820] The CME worked closely with the EMCO to develop the new directive, which formalizes civilian leadership in the deployment of the armed forces, defines the geographic location and equipment of the Military Emergency Response Units (UMRE), and provides specific training for their personnel

[1821] The Directive, numbered 11/2014, determined that the EMCO will conduct joint civil protection operations through the Military Emergency Assistance Directorate of the Operational Command "when the Ministry of Defense, through the Secretariat for Military Emergency Assistance Coordination, orders or authorizes the use of the armed forces both within the country, to ensure the life and liberty of its inhabitants, and abroad, to provide support in disaster situations

[1822] Formation of Military Emergency Response Units Since the creation of the CME, the central proposal was defined as the formation of thirteen Military Emergency Response Units (UMRE) distributed geographically throughout the national territory according to the main existing threats

[1823] Resolution MD 297 of 2014 institutionalized its creation, supporting the strategic decision to strengthen MINDEF's resources and means to plan for and respond to adverse events

[1824] The UMRE are modular units that perform basic functions to address different types of emergencies, with more limited territorial responsibility than the Emergency Zone Commands

[1825] They are deployed immediately to assess the situation in the affected area, inform the Secretary of Military Emergency Assistance Coordination, and provide initial support

[1826] This is accomplished by identifying existing resources, strengthening logistical capabilities, and professionalizing specialized teams. Anticipating the most frequent risks and incidents associated with their mission in the areas where the UMREs are located, a specific training program was planned for armed forces personnel on forest fires, search and rescue in collapsed structures, search dogs, and handling incidents involving hazardous materials and cargo

[1827] In addition to these training sessions, the UMREs are expected to be provided with the necessary equipment to efficiently respond to emergencies and disasters

[1828] The Comprehensive Risk Information Management System as a contribution to the National Civil Protection System This computer system implemented by the CME has as its main function to provide location information for emergency or disaster situations using geographic coordinates (generally expressed as "georeferencing

[1829] It is a highly effective tool for both emergency prevention and simulation, as well as for developing effective management during the occurrence of incidents

[1830] Since the beginning of its management, the CME has oriented its work in three strategic directions that complement its fundamental responsibility of coordinating the deployment of Armed Forces resources in cases of emergencies or disasters: the formation of Military Emergency Response Units (UMRE), the development of a Comprehensive Risk Information Management System (SIGIR) and the design and implementation of specific training for members of the Armed Forces

[1831] Data are also presented on emergency operations in which the CME has participated and on social and health operations carried out between 2013 and

[1832] The system brings together a wide variety of information databases that provide insight into the topographic, road, general infrastructure, building, administrative, health, educational, and population characteristics of the national territory, as well as the existing capacities to respond to an emergency wherever it occurs

[1833] Considering that the CME is incorporated into the response under the coordination of the Undersecretariat of Civil Protection and Comprehensive Emergency and Disaster Response of the Ministry of Security, the aforementioned information system is an important tool available to the National Civil Protection System, which includes data from various public and private organizations

[1834] Among the public institutions, the National Institute of Statistics and Census, the Ministry of Federal Planning, Public Investment and Services, and the Ministry of Social Development, Health, and Defense stand out

[1835] This system is very useful for planning the deployment of resources in emergency situations, paying special attention to serving the population and avoiding overlapping resources

[1836] Considering that it allows for the creation of diverse types of thematic maps, its potential includes the production of management reports on current and addressed needs, the analysis of the historical evolution of the emergency, and the simulation of possible scenarios for better decision-making

[1837] It is currently used in emergencies in which the CME participates, as well as in planning tasks

[1901] Health campaign Stage 1 May - June 2014 Stage 2 November 2014 The international Defense policy of a country constitutes the projection of the values and objectives of its national policy, and is complementary and consistent with the guidelines of its foreign policy

[1902] The Argentine model proposes an autonomous yet cooperative defensive framework that seeks to achieve adequate capabilities for legitimate defense while proposing, through bilateral and multilateral cooperation, to contribute to building a regional—and, if possible, global—scenario where mutual trust and transparency foster better protection of the national interests of each society in an environment of freedom, peace, and justice, thus strengthening institutions and international law

[1903] To implement this concept, there is a political leadership body within the ministerial organization: the Undersecretariat of International Defense Affairs

[1904] Its mission is to assist higher authorities in planning and implementing, in a coherent and coordinated manner, political and institutional ties with the Ministries of Defense and the armed forces of other nations and with multilateral defense forums, as well as to optimize and adapt ministerial and military international cooperation activities following the guidelines determined by the national strategic leadership

[1905] The international dimension of national defense is in harmony with the essential principles and values that inspire the internal order and foreign policy of the Argentine Republic

[1906] Within the framework of these principles, Argentina's international defense policy adopts two general objectives: • The promotion and consolidation of South America as a zone of peace and the progressive construction of a subregional defense system

[1907] • Contributing to efforts aimed at extending and maintaining international peace and security—including non-proliferation—based on respect for international law, the multilateral order, and the collective security system represented by the United Nations

[1908] Based on the conception, positioning and strategic attitude of a defensive nature and character, supported by an autonomous yet cooperative model, and considering the objective of promoting and consolidating authentic "zones of peace" in priority geostrategic spaces for the Argentine Republic, the international Defense policy supports the following key guidelines: Within the framework of the Defense policy modernization process that the Argentine Republic has been implementing for a decade now, its international facet is based on an autonomous yet cooperative model that guarantees our right to legitimate defense, complements our own capabilities and at the same time promotes cooperative actions with the Ministries of Defense and the Armed Forces of friendly countries, prioritizing subregional ties, especially within the framework of the South American Defense Council, understanding that the consolidation of South America as a zone of peace contributes to Defense objectives

[1909] CHAPTER XIX INTERNATIONAL DEFENSE POLICY • Project, together with neighboring countries, a subregional defense system that promotes and consolidates interdependence, interoperability, mutual trust and, therefore, the political conditions that ensure the consolidation of the region as a zone of peace and cooperation

[1910] In this context, South America and the South Atlantic are priority areas for international defense policy

[1911] Contribute to the construction of an international security environment that enables conflict prevention, peacekeeping, the non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, and cooperation and transparency in defense matters

[1912] • Coordinate and provide coherence at all levels of the defense system—MINDEF, Joint Staff, and General Staffs of the Armed Forces—in the management of international defense relations

[1913] • Contribute to the development of regional scientific and technological autonomy by promoting complementary efforts among the countries in the subregion to achieve increasing levels of scientific and technological sovereignty

[1914] • Collaborate with multilateral efforts for international peace and security through multiple actions, including participating in UN-mandated Peacekeeping Operations and monitoring the non-proliferation and control of transfers of key materials and technologies for the manufacture of nuclear, chemical, biological, or dual-use weapons

[1915] The implementation of these guidelines is expressed in the following policies: Consolidation and qualitative progress of cooperation between the nations of Latin America in general and South America in particular, with the creation of the South American Defense Council and the scientific, technological and production complementarity projects for Defense

[1916] • Fluid dialogue at the highest strategic political and military level and effective and regular functioning of permanent institutional mechanisms with the Ministries of Defense and armed forces of the countries in the region

[1917] • Updating existing bilateral agreements and signing new agreements with countries with which such instruments were not registered

[1918] • Implementation of unprecedented global experiences of complementarity and integration, such as the Chilean-Argentine Combined Binational Peace Force “Cruz del Sur” and the Peruvian-Argentine Combined Engineering Company “General San Martín.”

[2057] CHAPTER XXII THE MALVINAS AND THE SOUTH ATLANTIC (ANTARCTIC SECTOR AND ARGENTINE CONTINENTAL SHELF) The Argentine Republic rejects the unilateral British acts in the disputed area, as they are contrary to the provisional understandings under the formula of sovereignty; and urges the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland to abide by the relevant UN resolutions calling on the two parties to resume negotiations aimed at resolving the sovereignty dispute; and, in particular, Resolution 31/49 of the General Assembly of that international organization, which urges the parties to refrain from adopting decisions that entail the introduction of unilateral modifications to the situation while the Islands undergo the process recommended by the organization in its Resolutions on the “Question of the Malvinas Islands.”

[2058] Such unilateral actions could pose an immeasurable risk to the defense of the South American region, given that the illegal and illegitimate development of hydrocarbon exploration and exploitation activities by companies licensed by the United Kingdom could trigger environmental catastrophes and affect the marine ecosystem as a result of the uncontrolled unilateral issuance of fishing permits

[2059] Likewise, the failure to exercise oversight and control mechanisms for weapons systems and activities that demonstrate increasing British militarization in the Islands are completely misguided and unjustified actions in the face of Argentina's commitment and desire to reach a peaceful solution to the sovereignty dispute, in full compliance with resolutions emanating from international law

[2060] This concern for regional defense, which could affect the South American peace zone given the possibility of nuclear weapons or devices entering the South Atlantic, is shared by the member countries of UNASUR, which, faced with this scenario, have agreed to adopt "the necessary measures to demand respect and compliance with this commitment [the prohibition of use, stockpiling, installation, deployment or any other form of possession of any nuclear weapon] by other states, especially the Nuclear Weapon States, including the collective demand that they withdraw the Interpretative Declarations to Protocols I and II of the Treaty of Tlatelolco and, thus, guarantee that the territories of the member states of UNASUR, including those under dispute, such as the Malvinas Islands, South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands, remain free of nuclear weapons

[2061] Another demonstration of support from the South American region took place in November 2010, when the UNASUR member countries, meeting in Georgetown, expressed their commitment to adopt, in accordance with international law and their respective domestic legislation, all measures that can be adopted to prevent the entry into their ports of vessels flying the illegal flag of the Falkland Islands

[2062] Furthermore, they committed to informing the Argentine government, within the framework of current international agreements, about any vessels or naval vessels sailing to the Falkland Islands, South Georgia, and the South Sandwich Islands, carrying cargo destined for illegal hydrocarbon or mineral activities on the Argentine continental shelf

[2063] More recently, the Latin American Energy Organization (OLADE) declared its recognition of the Argentine Republic's authority to take legal action against unauthorized hydrocarbon exploration and exploitation activities in the Malvinas, South Georgia, and South Sandwich Islands and the surrounding maritime areas

[2064] At the same time, in September 2011, and for the first time, the Group of 77 and China devoted an exclusive paragraph to the Malvinas Question in its final declaration

[2065] The more than 130 foreign ministers of the Group of 77 member countries plus China called on the United Kingdom to comply with the international community's demands and resume negotiations with Argentina regarding the Falkland Islands

[2066] The document states that the decision is being taken "in order to find a peaceful solution as soon as possible" and that "governments must refrain from taking unilateral decisions

[2067] The Malvinas Islands are today a matter of state, not only because our National Constitution so states, but because the national government pursued an active policy in every area of action that placed this issue at the top of the national, regional, and international public agenda

[2068] Satellite image of the Falkland Islands

[2069] This is demonstrated, as has been pointed out on numerous occasions, by the declarations adopted within the framework of MERCOSUR, UNASUR, and CELAC on the need for the governments of the Argentine Republic and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland to resume dialogue in order to find a peaceful and definitive solution to the sovereignty dispute over the Malvinas, South Georgia, and South Sandwich Islands, as requested by the United Nations General Assembly through various resolutions

[2070] And, in a similar vein, the declarations adopted by other extra-regional forums and organizations, such as the African Union and the Arab countries, are also echoed

[2071] The support for Argentina's constant call to resume dialogue by groups of intellectuals, artists, legislators, and personalities from all over the world, including the push by young Britons, demonstrates the anachronistic position of the United Kingdom government as a colonial power and the legitimate action of the Argentine State to present to the world, in each of its actions and declarations, its legitimate and peaceful claim on the Malvinas Question

[2072] The United Kingdom has consistently ignored the international community's countless calls to resume bilateral talks aimed at resolving the sovereignty dispute in the South Atlantic

[2073] Furthermore, there has been a succession of unilateral British actions regarding fishing licenses and oil exploration

[2074] Five years ago, the Argentine Republic reacted forcefully to the usurpation of national economic resources by passing Decree

[2075] According to the law and its regulations, any vessel or naval vessel intending to transit between ports located on the Argentine mainland and ports located on the Malvinas, South Georgia, and South Sandwich Islands, or to cross Argentine jurisdictional waters in the direction of the latter, or to load merchandise to be transported directly or indirectly between those ports, must request prior authorization issued by the competent national authority

[2076] The Argentine Navy already fully implements this regulation within its jurisdiction to control national maritime space, notifying the established coordinating authority of any developments

[2077] The ongoing British military deployment on the islands is regrettable, including the introduction of sophisticated weapons that run counter to the United Nations General Assembly resolution urging the two parties to the sovereignty dispute to refrain from unilateral changes to the situation

[2078] In 2013, Argentine President Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, through Decree 2251, created the Secretariat for Affairs Related to the Malvinas, South Georgia and South Sandwich Islands and the Surrounding Maritime Areas in the South Atlantic within the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Worship. This Secretariat will implement foreign policy strategies and actions in relations with all countries to better defend Argentine rights and interests regarding the Malvinas Question and to coordinate relevant multilateral courses of action

[2085] The Navy's active participation in the activities carried out within the forum of countries that constitute the South Atlantic Zone of Peace and Cooperation (ZPCAS), which includes twenty-one African countries and three South American countries – Brazil, Uruguay and Argentina – from the eastern and western basins of the South Atlantic

[2086] The “Declaration on the Denuclearization of the South Atlantic” was adopted at a summit of the zone's member states held in Brasilia, Brazil, in September

[2087] All of these actions aim to contribute to maintaining the South Atlantic as a zone of peace and cooperation, rejecting the United Kingdom's growing militarization of the Malvinas Islands, and consistently calling for an end to the colonialism that still encroaches on part of our territory and endangers regional peace and security
