[2090] DEFENSE TRAINING The guidelines for training the permanent cadres of the Argentine armed forces take into account the changes in the new contexts in which nations interact in the 21st century: the growing appreciation of natural resources, the development of science and technology, the global strategic relevance of SouthSouth relations, digital globalization and, among others, also the new ways in which armed conflicts unfold

[2091] Within this framework, a series of actions were developed aimed at building institutional capacities to ensure the continuous improvement of the training of civilians and military professionals

[2092] Design of a model for evaluating the quality of the educational system for Defense Since 2012, work has been carried out on the redesign and implementation of new evaluation criteria and improvement of curricular reforms in four main aspects: a) curriculum, b) transformation of the study regime of cadets, c) teaching practices, and d) institutional capacity to lead the modernization process of military education

[2093] An initial assessment concluded with the production of a report on the strengths and weaknesses of the reforms' implementation

[2094] Based on this experience, progress was made in the development of a "Defense Education System Quality Assessment Model" between 2013 and 2014. This model aims to further integrate the academic units of the Defense education and training system into the conceptual, regulatory, and procedural framework developed by the National Commission for University Evaluation and Accreditation (CONEAU) and the Argentine university system

[2095] This, without losing sight of the fact that defense is a specialized professional field that operates within the context of specific policies, and that these are the framework within which the training and development of the armed forces is carried out

[2096] We are working on a model that prioritizes ideas of improvement and the provision of useful tools for the academic and institutional management of university life

[2097] That is, by developing evaluation processes that serve to energize necessary changes and enhance decision-making processes for improvement, and by valuing the participation of stakeholders in all evaluation processes as a guarantee of accurate diagnoses and sustainable improvement projects

[2098] The need to document institutional life through information about teachers, students, curricula, and teaching and learning processes was also emphasized among participants

[2099] For all these reasons, the transparency provided by the information dimension acquires fundamental importance

[2100] Ensuring the quality of training is an institutional policy adopted by the armed forces

[2101] Based on all of the above, the implementation processes for curricular reforms in officer training schools were evaluated in 2012, and improvement plans were designed

[2102] In the second half of 2014, the three Initial Officer Training schools and the National Defense School were evaluated

[2103] For the first time, a technical working committee was formed, composed of members of the Undersecretariat of Training, the General Directorates of Education of each of the armed forces, and external university experts

[2104] Defense training includes both military and civilian training

[2105] In Argentina, the Armed Forces personnel training system is undergoing a process of reform and modernization with the goal of consolidating highly qualified professionals in their specialty and as military citizens and public servants competent to effectively and efficiently perform their primary mission

[2106] Military training must also address other issues in which the State also requires the commitment of its Armed Forces: participation in United Nations peacekeeping missions and cooperation in the event of humanitarian emergencies and natural disasters

[2107] Strengthening information systems for planning and strategic decision-making As part of the methodological update in the planning and strategic decision-making of public policies for the sector, the information management system was redesigned, in which data relating to the educational institutions of the armed forces converge

[2108] The project includes the implementation of a regularly updated database that consolidates information from the Defense Education System, along with an interface for analyzing and visualizing the data. Together, the two can generate reports relevant to academic and institutional management

[2109] The combination of these two approaches will make it possible to offer a set of tools that will enable goals to be defined and evaluated over time, while also setting new ones

[2110] During 2013, the first data upload was carried out, collected over two periods and covering a large portion of the Defense's tertiary and university education and vocational training services, as a pilot test of the information management model and its respective upload interfaces

[2111] During 2014, meanwhile, progress was made on the corresponding updates and on data cleansing and analysis

[2112] Important changes were also made to the definition of the aspects to be continuously evaluated, and the data model variables to be considered in future updates were nominally and operationally redefined

[2113] Certification of Trades for Volunteer Troop Sailors

[2114] The comprehensive reform of the curricula for the armed forces' officer training schools and institutes was the result of a collaborative effort between specialists from the ministry's training departments, authorities and teachers from those institutes, along with education directors and chiefs of staff from each service

[2115] This effort, which resulted first in the implementation of a common core of subjects for officer training (Resolution MD 827/2007) and the introduction of three common curricular axes for the training of non-commissioned officers, was finally embodied in Resolutions MD 20/2011 and 1371/2011, which approved the curricula for the initial training of officers at the Naval Military School, the National Military College and the Military Aviation School

[2116] The reform focused on three major aspects: the curriculum, the study regimes for the cadets, and the renewal of teaching practices

[2117] The curricula were designed around the following axes: a) competency-based curriculum design; b) integration of theory (identified with academic training) and professional practice (identified with military instruction); c) defining a single officer profile for the nation's military and specific profiles for each armed force; d) a common training curriculum (eight subjects) to guarantee legal, scientific, organizational, contextual (historical and contemporary), and deontological training for both military personnel and public officials; e) current and diverse perspectives in knowledge (which consequently includes bibliography); and f) specific training in human rights and gender issues

[2118] Regarding the transformation of the cadets' study regime and behavior, the recommendations focused on promoting practices specific to the university system: a) responsible use of study and leisure time and the development of methodical study habits; b) the development of critical thinking, a plurality of analytical perspectives, and reasoned argumentation; and c) the accreditation of abilities through performance tests prior to admission or during training

[2119] The issue of revamping teaching practices, meanwhile, was geared toward producing innovations consistent with competency-based curriculum design: a) ensuring that teaching is organized around course projects rather than content programs; b) revamping teaching strategies geared toward competency acquisition; and c) revamping programs and bibliographies, coordinating departments, and orienting academic subjects toward developing effective skills for professional performance

[2120] The Ministry of Defense continues to develop a process of reform and modernization of military training to achieve and consolidate the required profile, both in terms of technical-military and civic training, under the concept of professional public service implied by military status and within the framework of the democratic conception of national defense

[2172] The National Defense School's objective is to train civilians who are competent in the specific themes presented by the various responsibilities of the political and strategic leadership of Defense, and to provide them with the technical and administrative skills to interact with military personnel and political officials of the State

[2173] Their programs provide interdisciplinary graduate-level training through tuition-free programs aimed at students from the public and private sectors of the Argentine, Latin American, and other countries around the world, promoting a framework of academic and professional integration and cooperation among different sectors of the community and the region

[2174] The Advanced Course in National Defense, created in 1952, trains students in the relevant aspects of defense

[2175] The Specialization in Defense Management, meanwhile, is a professionally oriented postgraduate program created through a framework agreement for cooperation and academic exchange between the National University of Tres de Febrero and the Ministry of Education and Culture

[2176] This university trains specialists in international security and government, as well as defense organization and administration, with theoretical, methodological, and instrumental skills for the design, implementation, and evaluation of public policies in this field

[2177] Furthermore, the Master's Degree in National Defense is a postgraduate program associated with the Army University Institute (IUE), which trains graduate students in the analytical understanding of the aspects involved in national defense, in scientific research, and in academic production aimed at expanding general knowledge on the subject

[2178] With their diverse missions and visions, these programs train students to recognize Defense as a specific field of knowledge that requires not only management approaches but also training and research, which understand and articulate the civilian governance of Defense, public administration, the diverse social and cultural realities, the connection with human and natural resources, and the ongoing challenges that reality imposes for the protection of the Nation

[2179] With the goal of expanding the training tools available to its students and faculty, EDENA develops research programs on national defense, strategy, strategic planning, regional integration, geopolitics, defense production, and natural resources

[2180] These activities are coordinated by renowned professionals and scientists who coordinate their activities with all the programs and courses offered by the institution and the ministry itself

[2181] The National Defense School is an academic unit within the Ministry of Defense whose primary responsibility is the training of civilian defense specialists, with the understanding that training civilians is a fundamental pillar in strengthening the civilian governance capacity of national defense policy

[2182] Disciplinary courses of both a face-to-face and virtual nature, covering general studies on national defense, cartography, natural resources, international relations and strategy, and specific topics on the organization and management of defense production, the study of the Antarctic region, the defense of local and regional natural resources, comprehensive training on the Malvinas archipelago, training in human rights and international humanitarian law, and action in disaster situations

[2183] Regional projection of the defense education system Based on the hierarchical nature of the defense training policy, a series of actions were implemented at the regional level with the aim of strengthening the South American region as a zone of peace based on dialogue, consensus, and cooperation

[2184] These actions, coordinated by the member countries of UNASUR's South American Defense Council (CDS), are aimed at building a South American vision of defense that contributes to consolidating regional identity while respecting national uniqueness

[2185] Since 2011, the Argentine Republic has organized and taught the South American Defense Training Course, structured in two stages

[2186] The first is developed in the distance learning modality in the virtual environment of the University of Southern Patagonia (UNASURMODAL

[2187] After completing this stage, the students with the highest GPA from each country travel to Argentina to participate in various academic activities as well as visits to departments and agencies of the Ministry of Defense and the Armed Forces

[2188] Over the course of four editions, the program's content and dynamics have been redesigned, fostering the development of an experience for training, specialization, and updating in the design, planning, execution, and oversight of defense policy

[2189] The course has established itself as a space for exchange and joint participation of civilians and military personnel from the CDS member states

[2190] In November 2012, the CDS ministers, at the initiative of the Argentine Republic, decided to form a Working Group with the mission of developing a proposal to create the South American Defense School (ESUDE

[2191] Argentina, along with Brazil and Ecuador, joined the group responsible for the task

[2192] In May 2014, the Ministries of Defense approved the actions of the Responsible Group, and in April 2015, the first meeting of the nascent institution was held at UNASUR headquarters in Quito

[2193] ESUDE, established as a higher education center that seeks to coordinate national initiatives, represents an institutional framework dedicated to training in regional defense and security issues at the political-strategic level

[2194] The National Defense University

[2195] In November 2014, the National Congress passed Law No. 27015, which created the National Defense University (UNDEF

[2196] The UNDEF draws on the valuable experience gained by the Armed Forces University Institutes since their creation in the 1990s

[2197] In the process of developing the foundations and institutional design of the UNDEF, different international experiences on training for the armed forces and training for Defense were analyzed, a joint work was carried out with the Ministry of Education, through the Secretariat of University Policies, opinions were collected from the National Interuniversity Council (CIN) and from experts in the academic field, and a compilation and systematization of the evaluations carried out by the National Commission for University Evaluation and Accreditation (CONEAU), by the UNDP MINDEF ARG 06/019 Program and by the Undersecretariat of Training of the Ministry of Defense

[2198] The UNDEF will institutionalize curricular, pedagogical, and institutional reforms with the goal of building fully university-like practices, cultures, and environments for the training of military professionals, but also for all citizens who choose to pursue their undergraduate and/or graduate studies in the programs offered by this university

[2199] The UNDEF aims to gradually integrate the military training of the three armed forces in their various specialties and levels into a single university institution within the Ministry of Defense

[2200] It will also promote the improvement of academic quality by increasing research activities and adopting evaluation standards based on the national scientific and technological system; by increasing outreach activities and relations with the community, promoting and building its framework for action based on the concept of public institutions and university social responsibility

[2201] Through the UNDEF, research activities in the areas of social sciences and natural sciences will be promoted, as well as the development of technologies that contribute to the substantial improvement of resources for Defense, to the creation and improvement of the capabilities of the Military Instrument and to the consolidation and growth of the industries of the Defense complex (Military Manufacturing, Argentine Aircraft Factory, Naval Industrial Complex). [2203] GENDER, HUMAN RIGHTS AND INTERNATIONAL HUMANITARIAN LAW Guidelines for human rights policy The Human Rights (HR) policy applied in the case of the armed forces is the result of the synergy of two complementary concepts

[2204] On the one hand, the armed forces as an institution vis-à-vis the human rights of the inhabitants of the national territory; on the other hand, the members of the armed forces as individuals who hold human rights vis-à-vis the State

[2205] In this situation, the concept of "military citizen" is activated, which conceives of armed forces personnel as individuals with the same rights as the rest of the citizenry, but subject to specific obligations due to their professional activity

[2206] Thus, the process of conceptually updating the armed forces is directly linked to promoting and ensuring compliance with human rights within the exercise of military functions

[2207] The conceptualization of the "military citizen" within the framework of the rule of law requires providing the theoretical and practical tools to safeguard such fundamental rights and obligations

[2208] The National Directorate of Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law, created by Decree 788/2007, is institutionally within the scope of the Secretariat of Strategy and Military Affairs of the Ministry of Defense (MINDEF), having as its primary responsibility to implement and disseminate the norms of international human rights law and international humanitarian law (IHL) in its area of competence, with the aim of strengthening respect for and protection of the essential rights of people, both in times of peace and conflict

[2209] The objectives of this national directorate are: To implement and disseminate the norms of international human rights law and IHL within its area of competence in order to strengthen respect for and protection of the fundamental rights of individuals, both in times of peace and conflict. To intervene in the orientation and formulation of training plans for the armed forces with the aim of deepening the teaching and dissemination of human rights and IHL. To promote, evaluate, and supervise actions aimed at ensuring the incorporation of a gender perspective in the design and execution of policies in the area of Defense. To understand the reception, follow-up, and supervision of petitions, complaints, and submissions related to civilian or military personnel in the area of Defense, when they may constitute a violation of human rights or IHL

[2210] The constitutional hierarchy achieved by the International Treaties signed by the Argentine Republic implied the adaptation of all its work to those standards

[2211] The set of human rights enshrined in our National Constitution constitute pillars that run transversally through our entire national defense policy

[2212] CHAPTER XXVI HUMAN RIGHTS The goal of having professionalized and modern armed forces that pursue peace and the integration of their capabilities into the regional framework implies the need to guarantee that their members have the fundamental protection of their rights

[2213] In building a workforce that is attentive to the human rights of the population, we must strengthen its own coverage, as a necessary requirement for the consolidation of forces that respect the democratic order

[2214] To achieve equitable integration of women into the armed forces, a gender intervention strategy was initially developed. This strategy involved: removing legal and formally institutionalized obstacles that hindered equal professional development; training, awareness-raising, and disseminating the gender perspective within the armed forces; incorporating the gender perspective into peacekeeping operations; promoting women's access to decision-making; addressing domestic violence; monitoring cases of gender-related human rights violations; and designing methodological and statistical tools to more fully assess inequities within the institution

[2215] As a result of the policies implemented, almost 15% of the total military personnel is currently female, meaning there is one woman for every seven men

[2216] However, inequalities persist that still threaten equality between men and women, making it difficult to reconcile professional development with life plans, given that the armed forces are a traditionally and historically male-dominated institution

[2217] The Ministry of Defense promotes equality between women and men in defense institutions, guaranteeing equal access and permanence, and banishing discriminatory practices and violence based on gender

[2218] Currently, the entry of women into the military institution is a formally resolved aspect after the opening to the incorporation of women in the Cavalry and Infantry arms CHAPTER XXVII GENDER POLICY The purpose of having professionalized and modern armed forces, which pursue peace and the integration of their capabilities into the regional framework, implies the need to guarantee that its members have the fundamental safeguard of their rights

[2219] In building a workforce that is attentive to the human rights of the population, we must strengthen its own coverage, as a necessary requirement for the consolidation of forces that respect the democratic order

[2220] Institutional framework for gender-based approaches The Gender Policy Council serves as the advisory body to the Minister of Defense and the Chiefs of Staff on gender issues

[2221] It was created following the conclusions drawn by the Observatory on the Integration of Women into the Armed Forces, through Resolution MD

[2222] The council's mission is to develop proposals to improve the conditions for women's access, retention, and advancement in the military

[2223] Likewise, actions, regulatory reviews, and strategies are being developed to guarantee the entry, permanence, and equal treatment of the lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and intersex (LGBTI) community

[2224] The council is composed of representatives from the three armed forces, the Ministry of Education (MINDEF), academic institutions, various state agencies, and civil society organizations

[2225] Regarding its working methodology, it is divided into three committees: Training and Capacity Building; Resolutions and Regulations on Gender and the Armed Forces; and Dissemination and Communication

[2226] Currently, the Ministry of Education (MINDEF) offers a Diploma in Gender and Institutional Management, declared of ministerial interest for the armed forces. This is one of the prominent policies in the field of training military personnel in gender perspective

[2227] The diploma program includes students from the armed forces of Argentina, Venezuela, Peru, Chile, and Ecuador, as well as from security forces, and even includes professionals outside the military or security sectors

[2228] It is also noted that the Minister of Defense instructed the Chiefs of Staff of the Armed Forces to annually designate members of the gender offices and two individuals from the General Directorates of Personnel to complete the diploma course, in order to provide trained personnel in areas where gender issues are addressed

[2229] Gender offices were created in 2008 as formal channels of communication, support, and guidance for military personnel on such important issues

[2230] These offices report directly to the Chiefs of Staff of the forces and are made up of interdisciplinary teams composed of professionals in the fields of psychology, law, and social work, who may be civilian or military personnel

[2231] Gender offices receive inquiries and reports regarding cases that may involve some form of gender-based discrimination or abuse, while also providing advice on a variety of issues related to pregnancy, maternity, housing, LGBTI rights, and the application of current regulations, among other topics

[2232] Between January 2010 and December 2014, nine new gender offices were created outside the autonomous city of Buenos Aires

[2233] Likewise, the creation of a new office is planned at the "Sergeant Cabral" non-commissioned officer school in Campo de Mayo

[2234] Recently, efforts have been made to empower the people who make up the gender office teams by giving them a leading role in disseminating and raising awareness on the issue within the forces

[2235] In addition, the tools for recording complaints and inquiries were improved and standardized through a common service protocol for use by the three armed forces. To expand contact, registration, and follow-up of inquiries and cases, liaison points were established, comprised of military personnel who provide gender counseling in various units, primarily in the interior of the country, without forming interdisciplinary teams like the gender offices

[2236] At the liaison points, inquiries and complaints are channeled to the gender offices, and the offices are periodically informed of the activities carried out by these staff, the number and nature of inquiries and complaints made, and their topics

[2237] The Domestic Violence Response Teams, meanwhile, were established on an interdisciplinary basis to assist victims and raise awareness and provide training on the issue

[2238] Since the beginning of the definition of a Gender Agenda for the Defense Sector, domestic violence has been considered a socially relevant issue requiring interdisciplinary and interinstitutional work to prevent human rights violations within the family and re-victimization at the institutional level, especially following the passage of Law 26.465 on the Comprehensive Protection of Women

[2239] Regulatory review, team building, and standardization of a victim care protocol were carried out in relation to the "National Joint Work Plan to Promote a Comprehensive Policy for the Detection, Response, and Recording of Cases of Domestic Violence in the Armed Forces" (Resolution MD

[2240] Measures were also taken to ensure that victims of domestic violence remained at home, and a “Comprehensive Policy for the Detection, Care, and Registration of Domestic Violence Cases in the Armed Forces Health Services” was promoted

[2241] Among the policies developed by MINDEF to promote gender equality are the granting of a critical activity supplement for personnel who care for victims of domestic violence, the standardization of a "Referral Guide for Cases of Domestic Violence," the implementation of campaigns such as "260 Men Against Machismo" and "1,000 Women Say NO to Gender Violence," and the holding of various institutional awareness-raising events within the framework of the commemoration of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women

[2248] Reconciling professional and family life In order to reconcile the professional and family responsibilities of civilian and military personnel, maternity leave and time off for breastfeeding and childcare were regularized and standardized

[2249] Furthermore, the "National Plan for Daycare Centers and Responsible Parenthood" was launched, and the initiative to create lactation centers within the armed forces began

[2250] The objective of the "National Plan for Daycare Centers and Responsible Parenthood," created by Resolution MD 198/2008, is to reconcile work and family life in order to eliminate all forms of discrimination against women in the workplace

[2251] According to data from the Observatory for the Integration of Women in the Armed Forces—currently the Gender Policy Council—a large number of military and civilian women serving in military units felt their careers were at risk due to the lack of appropriate childcare facilities

[2252] Nursery schools are for children between 45 days and two years old

[2253] The plan includes the construction and expansion of new facilities, the assessment of needs and demands for new gardens, and the supervision of building conditions and the working conditions of the staff in charge of the gardens already in operation

[2254] It also provides for the signing of agreements with provincial governments to ensure that education is public

[2255] Finally, it should be noted that both the Ministry of Education (MINDEF) in the Libertador building and the FAA in the Cóndor building have inaugurated lactation rooms so that women have a suitable space to express their breast milk during the workday

[2256] In addition, the initiative is expected to be replicated at other armed forces headquarters

[2257] Right to health with a gender perspective in the armed forces In accordance with Resolution MD 28/2010, progress was made in the design of the “Sexual and Reproductive Health Plan in the Armed Forces” – based on compliance with laws 25.673 (National Program for Sexual Health and Responsible Procreation) and 26.150 (National Program for Comprehensive Sexual Education) – to promote sexual and reproductive rights within the armed forces

[2258] In this regard, the heads of the forces were instructed to disseminate the 0800-SEXUAL HEALTH Line based on Resolution MD

[2259] The Ministry of Education (MINDEF) also promoted a review of regulations regarding HIV testing, given its stigmatizing nature, in order to avoid making it mandatory for entry into the armed forces. In conjunction with the Sexual Health and Responsible Procreation Program, teachers at military high schools were trained and actions of visibility and impact were generated—such as the campaign that led to the distribution of some three thousand units of condoms and contraceptive ampoules on the Libertad frigate. Military personnel were also trained in "counseling devices" to provide information on the subject

[2260] During 2013, efforts were made to coordinate with military hospital management to raise awareness about the problems faced by conscientious objectors. A survey was subsequently conducted, which revealed that a large percentage of personnel declared themselves as such

[2261] Within the framework of UN Peacekeeping Operations (PKO), the integration of women into deployed Argentine contingents places the country among the top ten nations in terms of the participation of female military personnel in these missions

[2262] Currently, the Argentine Republic has a 6.38% participation rate of female military personnel in the PKO

[2263] Since 2008, our country has implemented the "National Plan for the Implementation of United Nations Security Council Resolution No. 1,325" (Resolution MD 1,226/2008), which refers to the incorporation of the gender perspective in the framework of peacekeeping operations

[2264] In this regard, work is being done to promote female participation, analyze and diagnose the problem, and designate personnel as Gender Focal Points (Resolution MD 91/2011) to prepare reports on the deployment that address the issue

[2265] In 2011, the Gender Policy Directorate began participating in evaluations for selecting senior positions for the Peace Operations (PMOs). Since 2012, it has distributed a "Gender Primer for Peace Operations" to raise awareness among staff

[2266] Our country is actively promoting the incorporation of regional and international measures on this issue, as well as cooperation in training and awareness-raising through seminars, conferences, and workshops organized on the theme "Women and Peacekeeping Operations

Rossi Minister of Defense Buenos Aires, March 10, 2015 Right to diversity The socially demanded expansion of rights regarding sexual diversity took on greater and broader visibility and validity with the approval of Law 26.618, which amended the Argentine Civil Code in its Second Section: On rights in family relations, Title I: On marriage (articles 159 to 239) – and which is known as the “Equal Marriage Law” – and the subsequent approval of Law 26.743 on Gender Identity

[2269] In this context, not only were the commanders of the three armed forces instructed to adapt their internal regulations and practices to the provisions of the aforementioned laws, but actions were also taken to broaden understanding of the issue in order to prevent unequal treatment and discrimination

[2270] In this regard, the Gender Policies Directorate acts as the MINDEF representative in the Group of National State Agencies for the Protection and Promotion of the Rights of the LGBTI Population, coordinated by the Department of Labor and Sexual Diversity, which reports to the Ministerial Unit of the Ministry of Labor, Employment, and Social Security

[2271] Its objective is to adopt measures to promote and protect human rights, especially in the recognition and respect for the free sexual orientation and gender identity of individuals

[2272] Currently, progress is being made on developing a “National Plan for the Protection of LGBTI Rights” that includes strengthening and developing public policies for the LGBTI population, promoting non-discrimination and equal inclusion, creating specific regulations on the subject, and incorporating the perspective of sexual diversity into public policies

[2273] During 2014, the ministry trained and sensitized staff in the gender offices of the three armed forces and the FFA gender liaison points to disseminate the laws on Marriage Equality and Gender Identity

[2287] The program activates the process of building and transmitting collective memory as a way to strengthen human rights values, democratic practices, and critical civic engagement among new generations

[2288] In order to expand participation, the Framework Agreement for Cooperation between MINDEF and the Provincial Commission for Memory of the province of Buenos Aires was signed on March

[2290] Among Argentina's state policies since 2003, government action has paid special attention to the socio-historical themes of Memory, Truth, and Justice

[2291] Consequently, the Ministry of Defense has promoted and implemented both regulatory updates and all types of related actions, consolidating and strengthening the process of democratic institutionalization of national defense and the military instrument of the State: its armed forces

[2292] This policy has made it possible to keep memory alive through the consolidation of social and cultural ties as a basis for consolidating national identity, while maintaining the full force of its democratic rule of law

[2293] The Ministry has collaborated in the search for documentation, the review of military personnel files and digital copies of photographs of former combatant officers and non-commissioned officers who participated in the South Atlantic war conflict, which were requested for the establishment of the museum inaugurated in June

[2295] In its first issue, the magazine addressed, among other topics, gender politics, domestic violence, and sexual harassment

[2296] The second issue was published in October 2013, containing articles on the opening of the Cavalry and Infantry branches to female members of the Army, the National Mechanism for the Prevention of Genocide, the CADHI (National Human Rights Commission), and cultural assets

[2299] Tributes and historical reparations The commemorations of each March 24th, the anniversary of the beginning of the last civil-military dictatorship that occurred in Argentina between 1976 and 1983, have had special participation from the Ministry of Defense

[2300] In March 2014, a series of activities began with the aim of reflecting on our recent history, with the goal of helping to raise awareness about the value of democracy and respect for human rights

[2301] On March 13, a series of activities began at various military units with the presentation of facsimiles of personal files—presided over by Minister Agustín O. Rossi—to victims of political repression who were detained at the former Armed Forces Penal Institute in Magdalena, Buenos Aires province, during the aforementioned years

[2302] Citizens who were deprived of their liberty in that prison—mostly civilians, but also military personnel—and their families participated in and received these facsimiles of files, the originals of which are now historical documents in the possession of the national State

[2303] Facsimiles of the files of Jacobo Timerman, Jorge Alberto Taiana, Mario Guillermo Galli and Julio César Urien were handed over, among others

[2304] Also in 2014, other tributes were held to prominent figures in the Argentine armed forces

[2305] In chronological order, on March 20, the Ministry of Defense commemorated Captain Vedania Adriel Mannuwal, an Air Force pilot who made the first flights of the Argentine Pulqui II aircraft and died on May 31, 1951, while practicing aerobatics

[2306] This was the first recognition given to a pioneering pilot, an icon of the development of the national aeronautical industry

[2307] Furthermore, and having as a precedent the posthumous promotion to general (Decree 892/2009) of the patriot of Upper Peru, Lieutenant Colonel Juana Azurduy de Padilla – a figure in the emancipation of the River Plate colonies whose memory is honored both in the Plurinational State of Bolivia and in the Argentine Republic – President Cristina Fernández de Kirchner signed on April 1, 2014 Decree 463 of posthumous promotion to the rank of General of the Argentine Nation, of the until then Colonel of Blandengues, Andrés Guacurarí y Artigas

[2308] In line with changes in the institutional culture of our armed forces, this measure is also part of the set of reparation policies for personalities from Latin American and South American history, and that consider gender equality and religious and cultural equality

[2309] Finally, on November 17, 2014, the Minister of Defense paid tribute at the National Defense School to Mr. José Agustín Navarro, who, as a First Sergeant, participated in the "June 9 Movement of 1956" in the city of Santa Fe, province of Santa Fe, in the civic-military uprising in defense of the National Constitution, commanded by General Juan José Valle

[2310] For this incident, Mr. Navarro was sentenced to one year and three months in prison on charges of "conspiracy and solicitation of rebellion

[2311] Ceremony to present replicas of personal files to families and victims detained at the former Armed Forces Penal Institute in Magdalena

[2312] Deepening the policy of symbolic reparation for detained-disappeared conscript soldiers. During 2014, a new data collection and cross-referencing process was carried out, resulting in the identification of 92 cases of conscript soldiers who had not been included in the 2009 resolution in which 63 cases had been identified, and who, according to the Unified Registry of Victims of State Terrorism (RUVTE) of the National Human Rights Secretariat, are detained-disappeared

[2313] Many of these cases of conscript soldiers whose disappearance is recorded by the RUVTE, continue to be recorded in the records of the respective discharges in the armed forces as "No Data - Article 600 Paragraph 5° CJM" Therefore, through Resolution MD 764/14, the three forces were instructed to modify the records corresponding to the 92 conscript soldiers so that they show that each of them is in the status of detained-disappeared

[2314] In January 2015, the first tribute to detained-disappeared conscripts was held, with the installation of a plaque in two military units in the province of Santa Fe in honor of the detained-disappeared conscript soldiers Francisco Domingo Lera and Roberto Daniel Suarez Barrera

[2315] Agreements Celebrated Among the documentation found in the basement of the Condor Building are documents that could be linked to economic crimes committed during the civil-military dictatorship from 1976 to 1983, which is why on December 13, 2013, the Ministry signed a cooperation and technical assistance agreement with the National Securities Commission for the analysis of this particular documentation and thus contribute to the investigations into the financial support of the repressive apparatus

[2316] In another agreement of a similar nature and purpose, on March 27, 2015, Defense Minister Agustín Rossi signed an agreement with the head of the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic, Alejandro Vanoli, to promote joint work spaces aimed at strengthening technical assistance between the parties for the purposes of analyzing and eventually providing documentary evidence related to massive human rights violations

[2319] The opportunity to implement a program to modernize the Defense Archives System was confirmed with the discovery of documentation in the basement of the Cóndor Building

[2320] On October 31, 2013, the Chief of the Air Force General Staff informed the Minister of the discovery, in an underground storage room in that building, of documentation that could be of judicial and historical interest since it corresponded to the period of the last civil-military dictatorship

[2321] The discovery was unprecedented in Argentine history and highlighted the attitude of the force's personnel and commander as a true expression of the democratization and integration process led by our armed forces, who quickly informed the civilian leadership about the discovery of documents dating from 1976 to

[2322] The documents discovered reveal the workings of the Military Junta, the supreme governing body composed of the commanders-in-chief of the three armed forces, as well as the doctrine and plans that underpinned the last civil-military dictatorship

[2323] Minutes and other documents were also found relating to the functioning of the then “Legislative Advisory Commission,” which was composed of a few “personalities” appointed by the Board itself and which operated under the authority of the National Congress

[2324] Resolution 47/2012 of the Ministry of Defense established the modernization of the Archives System in order to guarantee public access to the archives of the Armed Forces

[2325] To this end, archival and archival teams were formed to address the preservation and digitization of documents and to train the personnel who work daily in the Armed Forces archives

[2326] Minutes of the Dictatorship A special printed edition of six volumes with the reproduction of 280 Minutes of the Meeting of the Military Junta was arranged by the Ministry of Defense to be delivered to all human rights organizations and to the main libraries, archives and spaces for both public and specialized consultation in the country

[2327] The edition contains facsimiles of all the secret records found, respecting the original order in which they were found

[2328] They explicitly describe the arguments and decisions made at the Military Junta meetings throughout the dictatorship, revealing the plans and ideological foundations of state terrorism and the strategies used to present it to the public

[2329] Open Archives To facilitate and continue to guarantee real public access to the information stored in the archives of the Armed Forces, the Ministry of Defense developed a digital platform for public access and consultation, whether virtual or physical: Open Archives

[2330] The site also features audiovisual testimonies and newspaper articles related to the Ministry's work in the armed forces archives

[2331] Inventories and other methodological tools relating to documents found in the archives of the armed forces can also be found

[2332] In Open Archives, you can view and download documents related to the actions of the armed forces between 1976 and 1983, including the Minutes of the Military Junta Meeting, also published in hard copy

[2333] The page is constantly being updated, so new documents and tools are periodically made available for consultation. Minister Agustín Rossi at the presentation of the documentary collection found in the Cóndor Building in October

[2334] The documentation found in the Cóndor building constitutes a very important documentary core for our country at this stage in its history

[2335] “It is one of the most important discoveries that have been recovered in democracy.”

[2336] Agustín O. Rossi Minister of Defense Buenos Aires, March 2014 A very important detail is that evidence was found of the role played by some economic groups in financially supporting the repressive apparatus during the last dictatorship

[2337] Minister Agustín Rossi then ordered, through Resolution MD 445/13, that a specialized working group, in coordination with the National Directorate of Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law, resolve the identification and preservation tasks for the prompt availability of this material to the public

[2338] During the work, detailed analysis was prioritized with the aim of selecting those documents that were relevant to judicial investigations related to crimes against humanity and economic crimes

[2339] Documents were also identified that chronicled events or figures of historical and cultural significance and contributed to the Memory, Truth, and Justice processes, as well as to other topics of interest, which would therefore be crucial for reconstructing our recent history

[2340] Isaac Francisco Rojas Documentary Collection Within the framework of the identification, classification, and description of the documentary collections found in the archives of the armed forces, the personal archive of Rojas (1906-1993) was found in the Department of Naval Historical Studies of the ARA. Rojas stands out in Argentine history as one of the architects of the self-proclaimed "Liberating Revolution", which in September 1955 led to the overthrow of the constitutional government of President Juan Domingo Perón, and the installation of a provisional government of which Rojas himself assumed the vice presidency until the calling of elections in

[2341] The documents comprising this private collection are primarily those produced and received by Rojas as a public official, covering the various positions he held in the ARA, his tenure as provisional vice president of the nation, and his political and intellectual activities as a retired officer

[2342] In this sense, Resolution MD 1019/14 was promoted, through which the personal documentary collection of the sailor Isaac Francisco Rojas was declared to be of public interest, given that it has value for the history, research, science and culture of the Nation, since it contains documentation related to fundamental events such as the military uprising against the then President Juan Domingo Perón in 1951, the bombing of the Plaza de Mayo in June 1955, the coup d'état of September 1955 and the shootings of June

[2343] Digitized inventories and documents of this historically significant find can be downloaded from the Open Archives website

[2344] Declassification of documents from the Malvinas War Having assumed the Argentine Republic, by mandate of its people, firm commitments regarding respect and guarantee of human rights, and in particular the obligations and guarantees arising from the right to the truth and the effective exercise of the right of access to information, Decree 200/12 ordered the declassification of the report produced by the "Commission for the Analysis and Evaluation of Political and Strategic Military Responsibilities in the South Atlantic Conflict", known as the Rattenbach Report

[2345] Three years later, Decree 503/2015 ordered the declassification of all non-public documentation related to the South Atlantic conflict held in the archives of the armed forces

[2346] Through the Open Archives website, you can access inventories of these documents, as well as information on how to access them

[2348] The protection and respect of Human Rights constitute a program of action in continuous implementation carried out at all levels of the Argentine State

[2349] Following the constitutional reform of 1994, the Argentine Republic's domestic and international commitment was strengthened by prioritizing international instruments for the protection of these fundamental rights

[2350] Obligations arising from international humanitarian law, especially the duties of prevention, dissemination, and awareness-raising, have guided the actions carried out by the Ministry of Defense

[2351] The Argentine Commission for the Application of International Humanitarian Law (CADIH) was created by Decree 933/1994 as an inter-ministerial state body responsible for the treatment and application of international humanitarian law

[2352] The objectives of the commission are to carry out studies and propose measures leading to their teaching, dissemination and effective application

[2353] The CADIH executive secretariat operates within the National Directorate of Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law of the Ministry of Education, Sports, and Human Rights and is composed of representatives from the Human Rights Secretariat of the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, along with members of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Worship

[2354] To fulfill the national State's international obligations, CADIH has developed various working groups made up of representatives of state agencies with expertise in the respective areas

[2355] The executive secretariat is the coordinator of the groups and responsible for promoting the implementation of the work agenda through regular meetings and the preparation of management reports for each working group, which are submitted annually to the relevant authorities

[2356] In view of the reforms adopted at the Review Conference of the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court held in Kampala, Uganda, in 2010, the ICCAT established a Working Group on the subject in May of the following year

[2357] As a result, the draft final report was prepared in September 2013 and sent for review to the various relevant state agencies of the ministries that comprise CADIH

[2358] The report, which represents the basis for the draft regulation for the adoption by the Argentine Republic of the amendments to the Rome Statute, was completed in 2015 with the signatures of the Secretary of Human Rights, the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Worship, and the Minister of Defense

[2359] Development of protocols for the care and protection of persons with disabilities in situations of armed conflict The Working Group responsible for the analysis and proposal of measures tending to the development of a specific protocol on the care of persons with disabilities in the context of an armed conflict or a humanitarian emergency, in accordance with the provisions of Art

[2360] of the International Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, carried out a task of compiling information together with the interpretation and editing of a final report updated to the organic changes of MINDEF - such as the creation of the Secretariat of Military Coordination of Emergency Assistance - and to the regulatory changes - such as the sanction of Law 27.044, which granted constitutional hierarchy to the aforementioned convention

[2361] Thus, a Draft Final Information Document was proposed which, in accordance with its founding resolution, contains sufficient information that can be used by the armed forces to create the Protocol for Action on the Care and Protection of Persons with Disabilities in Emergency Cases

[2362] The document, after being circulated for comment among CADIH members, was approved in May

[2363] Compliance with the obligations assumed in the "Convention for the Protection of Cultural Property in the Event of Armed Conflict

[2364] The CADIH developed a work plan for the implementation of the international obligations assumed by the State within the framework of the 1954 Hague Convention for the Protection of Cultural Property in the Event of Armed Conflict

[2365] Thus, pursuant to Resolution MD 754/2012, the "Working Group on Cultural Property" was created to identify those assets eligible for the protection afforded by the aforementioned convention

[2366] The main objective is to identify cultural assets that can be protected by means of Blue Shield marking, in addition to implementing cultural asset signage and awareness raising and dissemination activities

[2367] The protection of the cultural heritage that defines us as a society is a commitment for states, in relation to the duties of respect and guarantee of the human right to culture, recognized through international regulatory bodies reinforced by the work carried out over the past fifty years

[2368] The cultural heritage of a people contains its memory, its history and its identity

[2369] In this sense, the effectiveness of cultural heritage protection depends on its organization in times of peace through the adoption of measures at both the national and international levels

[2370] The placement of the blue emblem represents the defense of Argentine history and culture, while also highlighting the commitment of the Armed Forces and the Defense sector to society as a whole

[2371] The Working Group is composed of various areas of MINDEF (the National Directorate of Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law, as coordinator, together with the General Directorate of Real Estate and Infrastructure, and the General Audit Office of the Armed Forces), the Ministry of Culture (the National Directorate of Cultural Policy and International Cooperation, the National Directorate of Heritage and Museums), the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Worship (General Directorate of Legal Counsel), and the Ministry of Education (Argentine National Commission for Cooperation with UNESCO), as guests

[2372] Since 2014, numerous cultural assets have been marked with the Blue Shield, followed by training and outreach activities

[2375] Following this, a phase of assessment and advice was initiated for the implementation of the measures contained therein

[2376] Work is currently underway to follow up on such resolutions within each agency, assessing the measures they deemed appropriate and providing guidance on the estimated possible outcomes

[2377] Likewise, various members of CADIH formed working groups to address the fulfillment of the promises made

[2378] Consequently, all the promises made have been fulfilled, and the information was submitted to the International Committee of the Red Cross in July 2015, with expectations of its presentation at the 32nd Conference to be held in December

[2379] ADMINISTRATION OF MILITARY JUSTICE One of the main transformations in the legal framework of the Armed Forces was the comprehensive reform of its penal-disciplinary system, a system governed by an old Code of Military Justice

[2380] It did not comply with current national legislation and international regulations, nor was it consistent with the concepts and political guidelines for national defense in a democratic state governed by the rule of law and with international standards for the protection of human rights

[2381] At the request of the Executive Branch and based on the recommendations made by the commission of experts convened by MINDEF, in August 2008 the National Congress passed Law 26,394, which repealed the Military Justice Code (Law 14,029), amended the National Penal and Criminal Procedure Codes, instituted a Military Criminal Procedure for Times of War or Other Armed Conflicts and Instructions for the Civilian Population, and established a Code of Discipline for the Armed Forces and a Joint Justice Service for the Armed Forces

[2382] Two essential concepts prevailed in the reform

[2383] On the one hand, there can be no rules governing the performance of members or officials of a State institution that are not in accordance with the Constitution of the Nation

[2384] On the other hand, in this context, to strengthen the quality of the armed forces as institutions of a democratic state governed by the rule of law, it was essential to adapt their rules and procedures

[2385] The previous model, governed by the Military Code of 1951, established for citizens of military profession norms and a system of judgment and administration of sentences that contradicted the constitutional system of the Judicial Branch of the Nation, lacked guarantees for due process and respect for the principles of publicity and contradictoriness - it was disconnected from national and international legal instruments for the protection of human rights - and even in the treatment of minor disciplinary matters it proceeded with extreme bureaucratic delay, lacked the possibility of review and with sanctions that deprived liberty that could extend up to a period of six months

[2386] The main points of the reform were as follows: a. Treatment of essentially military crimes within the jurisdiction of the Federal Justice of the Nation: military jurisdiction was eliminated for the prosecution of crimes committed by members of the armed forces

[2387] In this way, the procedural guarantees of independence, impartiality, and equality of military professionals who could be reasonably suspected of having committed crimes are safeguarded

[2388] This innovation assumes that the recognition of the principles that inform common criminal law must also apply to citizens with a military profession

[2389] b. Elimination of the death penalty from the Argentine legal system: the death penalty, although no longer in use, remained in force in the military legal system

[2390] Its elimination is not a mere formality but a step forward in deepening the democratic state's commitment to people, their integrity, and their dignity

[2391] Furthermore, the elimination eliminates the risk that the death penalty—formally legitimized by its existence in the legal system—could be used at some point, and constitutes full compliance with the Optional Protocol to the American Convention on Human Rights on the Abolition of the Death Penalty

[2392] c. Elimination of the courts of honor: Law 26.394 eliminated the so-called "courts of honor" established in Argentina in the early 19th century, originating in Spanish military traditions and regulated by provisions of the de facto government of Alejandro A. Lanusse since

[2393] These courts were solely responsible for judging the "moral conduct of officers," establishing that violations of honor are "all acts and omissions attributable to officers that harm their own honor, or that of others, and affect the ethical heritage of military institutions and the military profession and its traditions

[2394] The courts of honor could punish those who, for the same offense, had been deemed innocent by a civilian judge or even by the military disciplinary system, thus contradicting one of the general principles of law that prohibits double jeopardy for the same offense

[2395] d. Complete redesign of the disciplinary system: the reform involved adapting definitions and procedures to the needs of service efficiency, but, above all, to the requirements of the National Constitution (Article 18) and international instruments for the protection of human rights

[2396] In this way, the value of military discipline was ensured and rules that favored bureaucracy and arbitrariness were eliminated

[2397] To this end, the objectives of disciplinary control and their relationship to the needs of the services and functions of military activity were clearly established

[2398] Thus, concepts that considered disciplinary structures as abstract guardians of the hierarchical nature of organizations, without any connection to the real need for discipline and its effectiveness, were overcome

[2399] e. Reorganization of justice services in the military sphere: Since the new law came into force, the technical management of the Joint Justice Service of the Armed Forces is the responsibility of the General Audit Office of the Armed Forces and is correlated with the technical dependence of the lawyers who make up the legal services of each of the forces

[2400] This involved the creation of a common justice service for all armed forces, based on the principle of jointness as a guide to military organization

[2401] The General Audit Office of the Armed Forces has the authority to issue circulars that are binding on the entire judicial branch of the armed forces, with the purpose of providing information or standardizing the technical and legal assistance provided by the various advisory bodies

[2402] These circulars address various topics, including: an analysis of the powers and obligations of military authorities in the event of the commission of criminal offenses in the military sphere, in relation to the duty to notify and preserve evidence, apprehend suspected perpetrators, etc

[2403] Circulars 1 and 2); the guidelines for interpreting what behaviors may constitute workplace violence and how they are classified in the disciplinary system (Circular 15); and what should be understood as sexual harassment and how it is classified in the disciplinary system (Circular

[2404] Role of the National Directorate of Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law Law 26.394 is based on the principles and standards of human rights

[2405] In this sense, the National Directorate of Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law has a supervisory role in the military disciplinary regulatory system

[2406] That same year the law was passed, Resolution MD 1,451/06 created the Programs Directorate of the National Human Rights Directorate. Among its main functions is assisting in the implementation, commissioning, and monitoring of the new military justice system

[2407] The Programs Department receives, processes, supervises, initiates, and monitors disciplinary actions, placing special emphasis on those arising from potential violations or threats to the basic rights of military or civilian personnel

[2408] It acts daily, jointly with the armed forces and the General Audit Office of the Armed Forces, in all cases that in any way relate to the application of the international human rights system

[2409] Regulatory Decree 2.666/2012 Within the framework of the comprehensive reform of the military justice system carried out by the Argentine State based on Law 26.394, the Executive Branch issued Decree 2.666/2012, the purpose of which was to regulate both the Military Criminal Procedure for times of War and other Armed Conflicts, as well as the Code of Discipline of the Armed Forces and the Joint Justice Service of the Armed Forces

[2410] The National Directorate of Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law and the General Audit Office of the Armed Forces agreed on a legislative methodology that allowed for the unification of the three regulations in Annex IV of the aforementioned law, considering that while in the first stage the three forces favored separate regulations, the final result showed that there were no substantial differences among them that justified such regulatory dispersion

[2411] On criminal procedure in times of war, was incorporated into a single text for all pending regulations, including the Joint Service Regulations

[2412] Decree 2.666/12 maintains and elaborates on the conceptual principles of the military disciplinary administration system, establishing a unity among the armed forces that goes beyond mere joint military action and progressively materializes the military instrument of the Nation as an efficient and effective component of the National Defense System

[2415] Between reform and permanence”, RESDAL, Buenos Aires, 2010 part VIII | chapter XXXI PART IX MILITARY STRATEGIC INTELLIGENCE The Ministry of Defense (MINDEF) placed emphasis on consolidating the institutionalization of intelligence activities under its jurisdiction

[2416] This institutionalization process was addressed through various regulatory instruments that allowed for the implementation of organic, functional, doctrinal, and operational reforms

[2417] Methodological transformations also took place aimed at consolidating their missions and functions, adjusting the processes within the agencies to what is established in the regulations that govern them

[2418] Law 23.554 on National Defense of 1988 established the general bases regarding the levels of direction and coordination of military intelligence, as well as the scope of its action, by establishing in its Article 15: "The highest level of intelligence agency shall provide the information and intelligence necessary at the level of the national defense strategy

[2419] The production of intelligence at the strategic military level will be the responsibility of an intelligence agency, which will be integrated with the intelligence agencies of the armed forces and will report directly and immediately to the Minister of Defense

[2420] Questions relating to the country's internal politics may under no circumstances be used as working hypotheses by military intelligence agencies

[2421] The provisions of the Defense Law were reaffirmed and supplemented by the Internal Security Law of

[2422] The National Intelligence Law of 2001 and its regulations established the legal, organizational, and functional foundations of the National Intelligence System (SIN), as well as the oversight activities based on the creation of the Bicameral Commission for the Oversight of Intelligence Agencies and Activities within the National Congress

[2423] The reform of the National Intelligence Law established by Law 27,126 of 2015, although it provided for important changes in terms of the structures, functional relationships and operation of the SIN, substantially maintained the ethical spirit of the previous regulations regarding the general principles that should guide this public activity and the limits of the system, establishing in its purpose the legal framework within which intelligence agencies must develop their activities, which must be adjusted to the National Constitution, the Human Rights Treaties signed and those that are signed after the sanction of the law and any other norm that establishes rights and guarantees

[2424] According to the National Intelligence Law (Law 25.520), the SIN is the set of functional relationships of the intelligence agencies of the National State, directed by the Federal Intelligence Agency for the purpose of contributing to decision-making in matters of the nation's external and internal security

[2425] Based on this regulation and its reform implemented by Law 27.126, the SIN is composed of: The Federal Intelligence Agency (AFI): the governing body of the Intelligence System that organically and directly depends on the Presidency of the Nation, and has the function of directing and coordinating the SIN

[2426] It also produces criminal intelligence related to complex federal crimes involving terrorism, drug trafficking, arms trafficking, human trafficking, cybercrimes, and attacks on the economic and financial order, as well as crimes against public authorities and the constitutional order

[2427] The National Directorate of Military Strategic Intelligence (DNIEM): an entity dependent on the Ministry of Defense—under the hierarchical authority of its head, the Minister of Defense—which is responsible for the Defense Intelligence System with exclusive jurisdiction over the production of Military Strategic Intelligence

[2428] The National Directorate of Criminal Intelligence (DINIC): is responsible for the production of criminal intelligence under the jurisdiction of the AFI, pursuant to Law

[2429] National legislation classifies the activities carried out in the SIN and assigns and attributes them to the different organizations that comprise the system according to their specificities and capabilities

[2430] National Intelligence: is the activity consisting of obtaining, gathering, systematizing and analyzing specific information related to the facts, risks and conflicts that affect national defense and the internal security of the nation (Law

[2431] Counterintelligence: is the activity within the field of intelligence that is carried out with the purpose of preventing intelligence activities by actors that represent threats or risks to the security of the National State (Law

[2432] Criminal Intelligence: This is the part of intelligence related to specific criminal activities that, due to their nature, magnitude, foreseeable consequences, danger or modalities, affect the freedom, life, property of the inhabitants, their rights and guarantees and the institutions of the representative, republican and federal system established by the National Constitution (Law

[2433] Military Strategic Intelligence: This is the branch of intelligence concerned with understanding the capabilities and weaknesses of the military potential of countries of interest from the perspective of national defense, as well as the geographic environment of the strategic operational areas determined by military strategic planning (Law

[2434] The main objective of Strategic Defense Intelligence is to obtain and process the information necessary to fulfill the purposes established by the National Defense Law, in order to permanently guarantee the sovereignty and independence of the Argentine Republic, its territorial integrity and capacity for self-determination in order to protect the life and liberty of its inhabitants

[2435] CHAPTER XXXIII THE DEFENSE INTELLIGENCE SYSTEM The National Intelligence Law and its derived regulations established the criteria for organization and coordination and defined the chain of command of the military intelligence agencies, placing as the apex of the system a civil structure dependent on political power, such as the National Directorate of Military Strategic Intelligence

[2436] Structure of the Defense Intelligence System The Defense Intelligence System's mission is to assist the Minister of Defense in all aspects related to the intelligence necessary for the conduct of national defense affairs

[2437] The structure of the Defense Intelligence System is comprised of a set of intelligence agencies and departments within the Ministry, the Joint Staff, and each of the similar agencies within the three armed forces. These agencies are functionally linked to produce strategic military intelligence, strategic operational intelligence, and tactical intelligence

[2438] The National Directorate of Military Strategic Intelligence (DNIEM), headed by a civilian official who is also a member of the National Intelligence Service (SIN) and appointed by presidential decree as head of the Defense Intelligence System, is responsible for the guidance, coordination, direction, planning, and supervision of activities related to the intelligence production cycle carried out by the intelligence agencies of the armed forces at their respective levels

[2439] The intelligence agencies of the armed forces are exclusively responsible for producing strategic, operational, tactical, and technical intelligence based on compliance with the guidelines and requirements established by the DNIEM (DNI) and the needs of joint military planning and management

[2440] The EMCO, the Strategic Operational Commands, and any other joint bodies that may be created are the bodies within the Defense Intelligence System that are specifically responsible for producing strategic operational intelligence, based on the needs of joint military planning and leadership, and compliance with the guidelines and requirements established by the DNIEM

[2441] The intelligence agencies of each of the armed forces, for their part, are tasked with providing intelligence on the specific military component of their jurisdiction

[2442] Regarding the functioning of the system, a fundamental contribution provided by the DNIEM is the Strategic Plan of the Defense Intelligence System (PESID), which supports the intelligence cycle of the EMCO and those corresponding to the armed forces

[2443] The process begins with a thorough analysis and assessment of each of the contributions made by the various state sectors involved, identifying actors, situations, and trends that may be of interest at both the regional and global levels

[2444] This is reported to the Presidency of the Nation, describing the different scenarios and situations that may represent opportunities or potential risks to the achievement of national interests

[2445] Consequently, the President of the Nation has the necessary elements of judgment to establish the scenarios relevant to national defense and intelligence, establishing the strategic guidelines that will serve to develop the National Intelligence Plan and Defense Policy

[2446] In this regard, Decree 2,645/2014, which updated the National Defense Policy Directive (DPDN), established guidelines for the MINDEF, stipulating that it, through the DNIEM, must continue to guide, coordinate, direct, plan, and supervise activities related to the intelligence production cycle carried out by the intelligence agencies of the armed forces at their respective operational and strategic levels

[2447] Pursuant to the guidelines of the national defense policy and the strategic positioning and attitude of the Argentine Republic, military strategic intelligence must be dedicated exclusively to understanding the capabilities and weaknesses of the military potential of countries of interest to national defense, as well as the geographic environment of the strategic operational areas determined by National Defense Planning and, more specifically, by its contributor, Military Strategic Planning

[2448] Within the framework of the National Defense Policy Directive, the Minister of Defense drafts the Intelligence Directive, through which he provides the DNIEM with the guidelines that should guide the planning and production of intelligence for the entire system

[2449] These documents enable the DNIEM, as the governing body of the Defense Intelligence System, to initiate the Defense Intelligence Planning Cycle and develop the actions that direct and supervise activities at the national strategic (defense sector), military strategic, operational strategic, and tactical levels

[2450] The DNIEM, according to Decree 1,451/2008, is responsible for: Planning the activities of obtaining and analyzing information for the production of strategic intelligence for Defense, producing the strategic intelligence necessary to support the planning and conduct of operations derived from the missions assigned to the armed forces

[2451] Provide information and intelligence to serve as a basis for military and operational strategic planning and support the evolution of the military instrument

[2452] • Provide sectoral intelligence to facilitate the direction of defense policy and military leadership. • Require the agency responsible for the direction of the National Intelligence Service (SIN) to provide the information and intelligence necessary to contribute to the production of strategic military intelligence, as established in the National Defense Law

[2453] Strengthen the Defense Intelligence System by effectively supervising the intelligence agencies contributing to the EMCO and the General Staffs of the Armed Forces

[2454] • Contribute to “strategic early warning” through the timely provision of the necessary strategic military intelligence, in order to prevent potential external military state aggression

[2455] • Contribute, through information obtained by the Defense Intelligence System, to National Defense Planning

[2456] • Propose, progressively, the incorporation of resources for the National Defense Intelligence System

[2457] • Establish the necessary policies to enable the joint and integrated use of intelligence resources available to the military

[2458] Propose the generation of capabilities for the National Defense Intelligence System through research and development. Promote the establishment of bilateral relations in the specific area of military strategic intelligence

[2459] According to the established methodology, the DNIEM's development and implementation of the Defense Intelligence System Strategic Plan (PESID) makes it possible to generate the dynamics of the intelligence cycle, allowing dependent structures to develop and disseminate plans appropriate to their respective levels

[2460] This is what the EMCO does by developing its own Intelligence Plan (PIEMCO) and, subsequently, the three armed forces do so by developing their specific plans

[2461] Challenges of the Defense Intelligence System Strict compliance with the provisions of the National Intelligence Law has led the DNIEM to establish controls that ensure the effectiveness, efficiency, and transparency of actions in all intelligence structures under its control

[2462] Its implementation is aimed at supervising aspects related to personnel, resources, means, and management control in all intelligence agency activities

[2463] The Defense Intelligence System is made up of civilian and military elements that work together at different levels to ensure its efficient operation

[2464] The National Defense Policy Directive states that without exception, no agency belonging to the MINDEF, the EMCO, the Army, the Navy or the Air Force may carry out intelligence activities incompatible with the provisions of the National Intelligence Law and its regulatory and subsidiary norms

[2467] The need for trained and educated personnel in various areas, particularly in intelligence management, production, and control, has motivated the DNIEM to develop specific training processes

[2468] Through the academic contributions of the National Intelligence School (ENI) and the Armed Forces Intelligence Institute (IIFA), training and education processes for civilian and military officials are carried out

[2469] The complex changes in the field of cyberspace and information and communications technologies that have impacted most states require their study as an important phenomenon from the perspective of cyber defense

[2470] It is also a challenge for cyber intelligence at the strategic level to study, analyze, and identify threats and risks, which allows for the generation of elaborate knowledge essential for guiding cyber defense efforts and capabilities

[2471] The DNIEM collaborates in the development of cyber defense policies established by the Ministry, aimed at detecting military threats or risks that could potentially affect strategic capabilities, critical infrastructure, or essential potential for national defense
